1	---
2	title: "Record a voice-over"
3	description: "Record narration from your microphone with no picture, at the playhead of the project you're editing or as a new project."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A voice-over is the microphone alone, with no picture. Use it to record narration over your edit: it lands at the playhead, on a new track of its own.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
13	  keys="⌥⌘N"
14	  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Microphone Only"
15	  tools="record_screen"
16	  needs="The Microphone permission. Screen Recording isn't needed."
17	/>
18	
19	## Record a voice-over
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Move the playhead to where the narration should start.
24	
25	2. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to **Microphone Only**.
26	
27	3. Choose your microphone in **Microphone**.
28	
29	4. Check **Record Into**: the project to land in, or **New Project**.
30	
31	5. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks the Microphone permission, then counts down from 3.
32	
33	6. Speak. The panel stays up while you do.
34	
35	7. Press **Stop**. The button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…**, and the voice-over lands. The panel stays up, back on **Record**, ready for another take.
36	
37	</Steps>
38	
39	With **Microphone** set to **Off**, **Record** starts nothing and the panel says "Microphone Only records the microphone alone — choose a microphone first."
40	
41	The controls that only make sense for a picture grey out, keeping their values for next time: **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Cursor**, **Record shortcuts** and the **When it lands:** boxes. The note under **Size** reads "no picture — the microphone alone". **Rate** stays live, because it sets the frame rate of a new project.
42	
43	Frame Job keeps **Microphone Only** in **Source** until you quit, then goes back to your display.
44	
45	## While it records
46	
47	Nothing on screen is being filmed, so the panel stays up:
48	
49	- Its rows are locked.
50	- The [level meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) stays live.
51	- The footnote at the bottom left shows ● and the elapsed time, or ❚❚ and the time held still while paused.
52	- **Record** reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** button stands beside it, reading **Resume** while paused.
53	
54	The countdown and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) work as they do for a screen recording, so you can also pause and stop from the menu bar, or from **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>).
55	
56	**Close** takes the panel away and the voice-over carries on. To bring the panel back, click **New Recording…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/). <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> won't do it, because it stops the recording.
57	
58	## Where a voice-over lands
59	
60	**In an open project,** each [stretch](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) between pauses is its own file, and they land end to end from the playhead on one new back track named **Microphone**. It's all one undo step, **Add Recording**. If a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) is open, they land inside it.
61	
62	A voice-over always gets a new track. It never goes on an existing one, even one already named **Microphone**.
63	
64	**As a new project,** the first file is the project itself, audio only at 1920×1080 and the frame rate in **Rate**. Later files follow it on its one track, as one undo step named **Add Recording Segments**.
65	
66	Either way they're ordinary audio clips, with everything in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/).
67	
68	## The files
69	
70	Each stretch is an `.m4a` file in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by the moment it began, for example `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/).
71	
72	## Good to know
73	
74	- If the microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, and the note reads "The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped."
75	- A **Resume** that fails shows its reason in the panel's note, and the voice-over stays paused. Try again, or press **Stop** to land what you have.
76	- A file too short to fill one frame goes to the media list without a clip, and a note says so. If that's every file, no **Microphone** track is added.
77	- A project already at its track limit can't take the new track. The files stay on disk and the note names them. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).
78	
79	## With an agent
80	
81	`record_screen` records a voice-over too. An agent gets your Mac's default microphone rather than a chosen one, and there's no countdown. It can't pass any of the screen settings with a voice-over. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).
82	
83	## Related

1	---
2	title: "System audio and the microphone"
3	description: "Record what your Mac plays and your voice as two separate sounds, check your level, and see how the microphone lines up with the picture."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	A recording can carry two sounds: what your Mac plays, and your voice. Frame Job keeps them apart, so you can set the level of each on its own after the recording lands.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
13	  keys="⌥⌘N"
14	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ System Audio', 'New Recording panel ▸ Microphone']}
15	  tools="record_screen"
16	  needs={['System Audio: the Screen Recording permission', 'Microphone: the Microphone permission']}
17	/>
18	
19	<Shot
20	  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
21	  alt="The New Recording panel. Microphone is set to Off with a level meter beside it, and the System Audio switch below it is on."
22	/>
23	
24	## Record what your Mac plays
25	
26	**System Audio** records the sound from every app but Frame Job, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track. It's on until you turn it off, and Frame Job remembers your choice.
27	
28	With it off, the movie has no sound track at all. The switch applies to the screen, so **Camera** and **Microphone Only** in **Source** grey it out, keeping its value.
29	
30	## Play the timeline while you record
31	
32	Frame Job's own sound is never recorded, whether or not **Include Frame Job windows** is on. You can play your timeline during a recording and its sound won't be in the file.
33	
34	## Record your voice
35	
36	Choose a microphone in **Microphone**. **Off** comes first and is the default, then every connected microphone by name. Frame Job remembers your choice, and falls back to **Off** if that microphone isn't connected.
37	
38	It works with every source. The voice goes into a second file beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, and never into the movie. With a microphone chosen, pressing **Record** also checks the [Microphone permission](/recording/permissions/).
39	
40	To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/). To record your voice with no picture, see [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).
41	
42	## Check your level
43	
44	A meter sits beside **Microphone**. It starts moving at the countdown, not when you choose the microphone, so the 3, 2, 1 is your chance to check your level before the recording starts.
45	
46	It stays live through the recording, and goes silent while paused. For a display or a window the panel leaves the screen once recording begins, so you only see the meter during the countdown. For a camera on its own or a voice-over, the panel stays up and so does the meter.
47	
48	## Your first words are kept
49	
50	The microphone starts during the countdown, not when the recording does, so your first words are in the file. A camera's capture starts early the same way. Both are let go if you cancel the countdown, close the panel, or the start fails.
51	
52	## How the microphone lands
53	
54	Each file lands on one new back track named **Microphone**, lined up with its picture, so your voice and the computer's sound have separate volumes.
55	
56	Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started, for each stretch of a [paused recording](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) separately, and places the clip to match. The alignment is exact to half a frame.
57	
58	If your voice started before its clip could, at the very start of the timeline or right after the previous microphone clip, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip being placed late.
59	
60	If no voice can be placed, no empty track is added. [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the undo steps.
61	
62	## If the microphone stops
63	
64	A microphone that fails doesn't stop a screen or camera recording. The picture keeps going, the meter goes silent, and the panel's note reads "The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording." What the microphone wrote lands with the recording.
65	
66	A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/#good-to-know) is different. With nothing else recording, it ends there.
67	
68	## Plug devices in and take them out
69	
70	The **Camera**, **Format** and **Microphone** lists follow the devices you plug in or take away.
71	
72	- Changes apply only while the panel is idle, so nothing moves during a countdown, a recording or a landing. A change that waited applies when the panel goes idle.
73	- A change made while the panel was closed is picked up when it next shows.
74	- A microphone you take away falls back to **Off**. A camera falls back to the default camera, or to **None connected** when there's no camera left.
75	- When a device comes back it's chosen again, and a camera comes back with its stored format.
76	- Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers. The next control you change saves whatever the lists show at that moment, so a device that's away at that point is forgotten.
77	- A list is rebuilt only when its own devices changed, so a menu you have open isn't disturbed by an unrelated device.
78	
79	## With an agent
80	
81	An agent turns each sound on or off rather than choosing a device. Its microphone is your Mac's default microphone, off unless it asks. It can't ask for the Microphone permission either: that takes one press of **Record** in the panel. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).
82	
83	## Related

1	---
2	title: "Start, pause and stop"
3	description: "Start a recording with its three-second countdown, pause and resume it, stop it from wherever you are, and see what happens if you close the panel or quit."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	This page follows a recording from the press of **Record** to the moment it lands: the countdown, pausing, the places you can stop from, and what Frame Job does if you close the panel or quit along the way.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['File ▸ New Recording…', 'File ▸ Pause Recording', 'File ▸ Stop Recording']}
13	  keys="⌥⌘N"
14	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record', 'The menu-bar item while recording']}
15	  tools="record_screen"
16	/>
17	
18	## Start a recording
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Set up the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) and press **Record**.
23	
24	2. Frame Job checks the [permissions](/recording/permissions/) it needs.
25	
26	3. The panel counts 3, 2, 1, a second each. **Record** reads **Cancel** meanwhile, and the [microphone meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) already moves. Press **Cancel** or close the panel to stop, and nothing is recorded.
27	
28	4. The recording starts. For a display or a window, the panel leaves the screen and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) takes over. With **Source** set to **Camera** or **Microphone Only**, nothing on screen is filmed, so the panel stays up.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	## What the button says
33	
34	The panel's main button tells you where the recording has got to.
35	
36	| The button reads | What's happening | Pressing it |
37	| --- | --- | --- |
38	| **Record** | Nothing yet. | Starts the permission checks and the countdown. |
39	| **Cancel** | The countdown is running. | Ends it with nothing recorded. |
40	| **Starting…** | The recording is starting. | It's dimmed. |
41	| **Stop** | A recording runs or is paused. | Stops and lands it. |
42	| **Stopping…** | The files are being written. | It's dimmed. |
43	| **Adding…** | The files are being added to the project. | It's dimmed. |
44	
45	## If a recording doesn't start
46	
47	A recording that hasn't started within 20 seconds fails rather than hanging. The panel says "The recording did not start within 20 s." and goes back to **Record**. Any other failed start puts its reason in the same note.
48	
49	While the button reads **Starting…**, you can still stop with **File ▸ Stop Recording**, or by closing the panel. If Frame Job hadn't begun yet, the note reads "Stopped before the recording began; nothing was recorded." A moment later, it's too late to abandon: the recording ends as soon as it begins, and whatever it caught lands as usual.
50	
51	## One recording at a time
52	
53	Only one recording runs at a time. If you press **Record** while another runs or is paused, including one an agent started, the countdown runs and the panel then says "A recording is already in progress."
54	
55	## Pause and resume
56	
57	You can pause from any of these:
58	
59	- the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)'s **Pause Recording**
60	- **File ▸ Pause Recording**, directly under **New Recording…**
61	- the panel's **Pause** button, for a [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) or a [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)
62	
63	While paused, each of these reads **Resume Recording** or **Resume**. The **File** item is available only while a recording runs or is paused. Pausing has no keyboard shortcut.
64	
65	On a recording you started, a pause Frame Job can't make beeps, and the recording carries on. A resume that fails leaves it paused, with the reason in the panel's note: at once if the panel is up, otherwise when it comes back after you stop. Try again, or stop and land what you have.
66	
67	## Paused recordings are stretches
68	
69	A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so a paused recording is several stretches. Each stretch has its own movie, and its own microphone, camera and [cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) when the recording has them.
70	
71	- Each file is named by the moment its stretch began.
72	- Each stretch keeps its own width, height and frame rate.
73	- The paused time is in no file, and the elapsed time counts only what was recorded.
74	
75	When the recording lands, the stretches sit end to end on one track, touching, with no transition between them. Each stretch's microphone goes on the **Microphone** track, lined up with its own picture.
76	
77	## Stop a recording
78	
79	You can stop a running or paused recording from any of these:
80	
81	- the menu-bar item's **Stop Recording**
82	- **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>). While any recording runs, **File ▸ New Recording…** reads **Stop Recording**, paused included.
83	- the panel's **Stop** button, for a camera on its own or a voice-over
84	
85	Frame Job writes the files and [lands the recording](/recording/where-it-lands/). A clean landing doesn't bring a hidden panel back. Press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> when you want it again.
86	
87	:::caution
88	There's no global shortcut to stop. <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> works in Frame Job's own menus, so it does nothing while another app is in front. Use the menu-bar item.
89	:::
90	
91	## Stop from macOS's indicator
92	
93	macOS shows its own indicator in the menu bar during a screen recording, and it can end the recording too. Frame Job keeps what was captured and adds it. The panel's note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added."
94	
95	## The Welcome window during a recording
96	
97	The **New Recording…** button on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/) never stops a recording.
98	
99	- During a screen recording you started in the panel, it only beeps. Use **File ▸ Stop Recording** or the menu-bar item.
100	- During a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording, it shows the panel.
101	
102	## If the panel closes
103	
104	A recording carries on if the panel closes, under the menu-bar item and **File ▸ Stop Recording**. You can only do this with a camera on its own or a voice-over, because the panel is off screen for anything else.
105	
106	Closing it at other moments is different:
107	
108	- During the countdown, it cancels the countdown and nothing is recorded.
109	- While the button reads **Starting…**, it counts as a Stop.
110	- Closing also lets go of a microphone or camera that was warming up for a recording.
111	
112	## Quit during a recording
113	
114	Choosing **Quit Frame Job** (<kbd>⌘Q</kbd>) during a recording doesn't quit. It puts the recording's controls in front of you, so you can stop or resume first:
115	
116	- With the panel hidden for a screen recording, it opens the menu-bar item's menu.
117	- For a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording, it shows the panel.
118	
119	Frame Job reviews your unsaved projects before this. If that review closes the project you were recording into, the recording opens as a new project when it lands, and the note says so.
120	
121	## Stop an agent's recording
122	
123	A recording an agent starts shows the same menu-bar item, so you can pause, resume or stop it from there or from the **File** menu.
124	
125	Your Stop ends the agent's recording early, and what was recorded still lands. An agent asks for a length of real time, so a pause shortens what gets recorded rather than extending it. An agent has no way to pause or resume, and it has no countdown. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).
126	
127	## Related
128	
129	- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
130	- [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)
131	- [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/)
132	- [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/)

1	---
2	title: "The menu-bar item"
3	description: "See the elapsed time of a running recording in the menu bar, and pause, resume or stop it from there while another app is in front."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	While a recording runs, Frame Job puts an item in the menu bar. For a display or a window the panel is off screen, so this item is the recording's control, wherever you're working.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where="The menu bar, while a recording runs"
12	  tools="record_screen"
13	/>
14	
15	## What it shows
16	
17	The item appears when the recording starts, and shows the elapsed time as `m:ss`, then `h:mm:ss` past an hour. Hover over it and its tooltip says which state it's in.
18	
19	| State | The menu bar shows | Tooltip | Its menu |
20	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
21	| Recording | A coral ● and the running time | "Frame Job is recording" | **Pause Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
22	| Paused | ❚❚ and the time, held still | "Frame Job's recording is paused" | **Resume Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
23	
24	It needs no permission. It appears for an agent's recording too, so you can [pause or stop one](/recording/pause-and-stop/#stop-an-agents-recording). It comes down the moment the recording ends, before the recording has landed.
25	
26	## Pause, resume and stop
27	
28	Click the item for its menu.
29	
30	- **Pause Recording** pauses. The row then reads **Resume Recording**.
31	- **Stop Recording** stops the recording, running or paused, and lands it.
32	
33	The time keeps ticking while the menu is open, so you can read it before you decide. [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/) has the other places to do this. If you choose **Quit Frame Job** while the panel is hidden for a screen recording, Frame Job opens this menu instead of quitting.
34	
35	## The keyboard mark
36	
37	While a recording [records shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/), a ⌨︎ mark follows the ● or ❚❚, and the menu starts with a greyed-out **Recording keyboard shortcuts** row. Both show whether the recording is running or paused, and they hold for a recording an agent started with shortcuts on.
38	
39	## A fixed width
40	
41	The item is sized once, so the other items in your menu bar don't shift as the seconds tick, when the hours appear, or at a pause. It's sized for times up to 9:59:59, and a little wider when it shows the keyboard mark. Past 9:59:59 the label is wider than that.
42	
43	## If macOS hides the item
44	
45	macOS can drop the item from a crowded menu bar or behind the notch. **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work once you switch to Frame Job.
46	
47	## Related
48	
49	- [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/)
50	- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
51	- [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/)

349	/// The camera's live preview in the panel (camera-recording CR2b, spec §11
350	/// CAM-7) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s eleventh file, NEW rather than
351	/// cut, as `+Camera.swift` was: the rule that says what the well shows, and
352	/// the one sync that acts on it. The well is `CameraPreviewWell`, a grid row
353	/// of its own right under Format (`+Rows.swift`), shown only while a camera
354	/// is wanted: Source Camera, or "Record the camera too" beside a screen
355	/// source (spec §11 CAM-11 (4)).
356	///
357	/// **The step** (`cameraPreviewStep`, pure, first match wins): a panel not
358	/// visible or closing, or no camera wanted → off; a camera recording, or a
359	/// screen recording's camera beside it → its layer; the countdown or
360	/// starting → the prepared layer, never a build; any other phase, or a
361	/// busy recorder → blank; no camera → "No camera is connected."; the
362	/// Camera grant not authorized → a sentence; a prepared capture that
363	/// failed, or a build that threw → its sentence, never retried; else
364	/// prepare. The grant is read only at its own step, through
365	/// `grantDoors.cameraStatus`, so showing the panel never prompts and a
366	/// hidden panel reads nothing.
367	///
368	/// **The sync** runs at the end of `show()`, of every control change, of
369	/// `syncPhase()`, at the one-second tick while the panel is visible, and at
370	/// each device notification. Its first act applies a pending hot-plug
371	/// (`+Devices.swift`, CAM-8 (2)), so the step sees the new selection. It
372	/// keeps the row's visibility (refitting the window when it changes), lets
373	/// the prepared capture go when the well is off or shows a sentence while
374	/// everything is idle, stops a failed prepared capture once (not at every
375	/// tick, CAM-8 (6)), and otherwise hosts the layer the step names. The
376	/// capture is the recorder's (`ScreenRecorder+CameraPrepare.swift`): the
377	/// countdown's `prepareCamera` keeps it, the panel's start adopts it, and a
378	/// tool's start never does (CAM-7 (7)), so through a tool's recording the
379	/// well reads "The camera is recording."
380	extension RecorderPanelController {
381	    static let previewGrantSentence = "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera."
382	    static let previewRecordingSentence = "The camera is recording."
383	
384	    /// CAM-7 (3)'s rule. `grant` and `failure` are called only at their own
385	    /// steps.
386	    static func cameraPreviewStep(
387	        visible: Bool, cameraSource: Bool, phase: Phase, recorderIdle: Bool,
388	        recordingCamera: Bool, cameraChosen: Bool, grant: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus,
389	        failure: () -> String?
390	    ) -> CameraPreviewStep {
391	        guard visible, cameraSource else { return .off }
392	        if recordingCamera { return .recording }
393	        switch phase {
394	        case .countdown, .starting: return .prepared
395	        case .idle: break
396	        case .recording, .paused, .stopping, .landing: return .blank
397	        }
398	        guard recorderIdle else { return .blank }
399	        guard cameraChosen else { return .message(CameraDevices.noCameraSentence) }
400	        guard grant() == .authorized else { return .message(Self.previewGrantSentence) }
401	        if let failure = failure() { return .failed(failure) }
402	        return .prepare
403	    }
404	
405	    /// The well's grid row.
406	    var cameraPreviewRow: NSGridRow? {
407	        (cameraPreview.superview as? NSGridView)?.cell(for: cameraPreview)?.row
408	    }
409	
410	    /// For the chosen camera at its resolved format (CAM-6 (3)): the
411	    /// prepared capture's stop on its own, else its failed start, else a
412	    /// failed build's record; nil when there is none.
413	    var previewFailure: String? {
414	        guard let id = selectedCameraID, let device = CameraDevices.device(withID: id) else {
415	            return nil
416	        }
417	        let facts = CameraDevices.facts(of: device)
418	        guard
419	            let format = CameraDevices.chosenFormat(
420	                selectedCameraFormat, in: facts.formats, active: facts.activeFormat)
421	        else { return nil }
422	        if let prepared = recorder.preparedCamera, prepared.deviceID == id, prepared.format == format,
423	            let sentence = prepared.stoppedOnItsOwn ?? prepared.startError?.localizedDescription
424	        {
425	            return sentence
426	        }
427	        guard let failure = recorder.preparedCameraFailure, failure.deviceID == id,
428	            failure.format == format
429	        else { return nil }
430	        return failure.sentence
431	    }
432	
433	    /// A pending hot-plug applied (CAM-8 (2)), the row's visibility, then the
434	    /// step acted on (the type doc).
435	    func syncCameraPreview() {
436	        applyPendingDevices()
437	        let hidden = !cameraWanted
438	        if let row = cameraPreviewRow, row.isHidden != hidden {
439	            row.isHidden = hidden
440	            fitWindowToContent()
441	        }
442	        let step = Self.cameraPreviewStep(
443	            visible: window?.isVisible == true && !panelClosing, cameraSource: cameraWanted,
444	            phase: phase, recorderIdle: recorder.state == .idle,
445	            recordingCamera: recorder.cameraSession != nil || recorder.session?.cameraCapture != nil,
446	            cameraChosen: selectedCameraID != nil,
447	            grant: { Self.grantDoors.cameraStatus() }, failure: { self.previewFailure })
448	        switch step {
449	        case .off, .message:
450	            if phase == .idle, recorder.state == .idle { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
451	            if case .message(let sentence) = step {
452	                cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
453	            } else {
454	                cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
455	            }
456	        case .failed(let sentence):
457	            if let capture = recorder.preparedCamera?.capture, !capture.stopped { capture.stop() }
458	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
459	        case .prepare:
460	            recorder.prepareCamera(for: currentChoice())
461	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
462	        case .prepared:
463	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
464	        case .recording:
465	            hostPreview(
466	                (recorder.cameraSession?.capture ?? recorder.session?.cameraCapture)?.previewLayer,
467	                else: Self.previewRecordingSentence)
468	        case .blank:
469	            cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
470	        }
471	    }
472	
473	    /// `layer` in the well, else `sentence` (nil a blank well).
474	    private func hostPreview(_ layer: AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer?, else sentence: String?) {
475	        if let layer {
476	            cameraPreview.show(layer)
477	        } else {
478	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
479	        }
480	    }
481	}

485	/// CO-81): Remove Background run over a finished recording's CAMERA clips as a follow-up to the
486	/// landing — never part of it — as its own undo step, "Remove Background", in AU-68's pattern

488	/// nothing need be measured first. Both doors call `apply` right after the landing's commit and
489	/// before Enhance Voice and the polish (CU-101 (a)): the panel's two branches
490	/// (`RecorderPanelController+Landing.swift`) and the tool's `landAndEnhance`. On-device, so
491	/// never keyed (CJ-3). Names no `rc_*`; main thread.
492	enum RecordingCutout {
493	    /// The undo step's name, Clip ▸ Remove Background's.
494	    static let actionName = "Remove Background"
495	    /// The tool's `camera_cutout_error` when no camera clip took the cutout.
496	    static let noCameraSentence =
497	        "No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run."
498	
499	    /// Every segment's camera file, in segment order; empty paths dropped, each path once. Pure.
500	    static func cameraPaths(of result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
501	        var seen: Set<String> = []
502	        return result.segments.compactMap { $0.cameraDescriptor?.path }
503	            .map(RecordingLanding.trimmed)
504	            .filter { !$0.isEmpty && seen.insert($0).inserted }
505	    }
506	
507	    /// Every clip of the open container whose media is one of `paths`, that can be cut out
508	    /// (`CutoutStatus.canCutOut`) and has no cutout yet, in id order. Main.
509	    static func cameraClips(_ paths: [String], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
510	        let wanted = Set(paths)
511	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return [] }
512	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
513	        return snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
514	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip), wanted.contains(media.path) else {
515	                return false
516	            }
517	            return CutoutStatus.canCutOut(clip, in: snapshot) && clip.video?.cutout == nil
518	        }.map(\.id).sorted()
519	    }

521	    /// One base `set_video {cutout}` per clip, the whole default cutout, as Clip ▸ Remove
522	    /// Background writes. Pure over the ids.
523	    static func ops(_ clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [ReelOp] {
524	        clips.map { .setVideo(clips: [$0], patch: VideoPatch(cutout: .some(CutoutProps()))) }
525	    }

527	    /// When the recording's choice asks for it, its camera clips cut out as ONE grouped step
528	    /// "Remove Background" (`performGroupedEdit`: a landing is not an AppKit event). Answers the
529	    /// clips the step was asked for, empty when the choice did not ask or no camera clip
530	    /// qualifies (the panel is then quiet; the tool answers `noCameraSentence`). Main.
531	    @discardableResult static func apply(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument)

2	// (camera-recording CR3b, spec §11 CAM-10): a screen recording's
3	// `(Camera).mov` files, one per segment (CAM-9), on ONE new FRONT track
4	// named "Camera", each clip lined up with its screen segment by the
5	// segment's measured `cameraOffset` and laid out in the recorder's layout.
6	//
7	// `addCameras` is `addMicrophones`' shape, attempt for attempt: every file's
8	// `add_media` in segment order, then — with the screen's starts — the track
9	// added on the attempt of the first camera clip that takes a frame and kept
10	// only when that clip lands, and each clip by the floor rule. The floor is
11	// `max(screenStart_k, previous camera clip's end)`, so a camera never starts
12	// before its own screen clip and never overlaps the camera before it, and a
13	// start below the floor is head-trimmed by the microphone's own dance
14	// (`headTrimmed`, `+Microphone`, internal for this file). CR3a measured
15	// every offset NEGATIVE — the camera begins 32–146 ms before the screen — so
16	// the trim is the ordinary path here, not the exception it is for a voice.
17	//
18	// The layout (road map "creator-jobs" CO8, spec §11 CO-80) is ONE
19	// `switch_layout` per camera clip right after its placement: the camera and
20	// its segment's screen clip at the camera clip's start, one canvas frame
21	// long so both roles CUT there, in `choice.cameraLayout` (Corner by
22	// default, the owner's answer, which is CAM-10 (3)'s corner to the pixel),
23	// its reach bounded by `through` = the later of the screen clip's end and
24	// the camera clip's, so it re-bases only a later screen clip this camera
25	// overruns into — never a later segment's own screen, nor a clip placed
26	// before the recording. No curve, focus or nest: no masks exist yet, so the
27	// crop centres on the source. When the segment's screen minted no clip, or
28	// its clip does not play at the camera's start, `cornerPatch` is the
29	// fallback (CO-80 (c)): arithmetic over the container's canvas and the
30	// file's size, the precedent `CaptionStyle.size(for:)` set for a Swift-side
31	// placement — a quarter of the canvas wide, a third of it tall, inside the
32	// 90 % ring of View ▸ Safe Areas (`SafeGuidesView`) — as one `set_video {x,
33	// y, scale}`, read back. Either way the clip stays an ordinary clip a person
34	// moves, and Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ re-lays it.
35	//
36	// The ops come back UNSCOPED, as every landing op does; the trial applies
37	// them scoped exactly as the commit will (the base file's header).

41	extension RecordingLanding {
42	    /// The new front track every camera clip lands on — ONE for the whole
43	    /// recording, added with the first camera clip that takes a frame, so a
44	    /// recording none of whose camera files can be placed adds no track.
45	    static let cameraTrackName = "Camera"
46	    /// The corner box is a quarter of the canvas wide…
47	    static let cornerWidthFraction: Double = 0.25
48	    /// …and a third of it tall; the picture is scaled to fit inside both.
49	    static let cornerHeightFraction: Double = 1.0 / 3.0
50	    /// The inset from the canvas's right and bottom edges, as a fraction of
51	    /// each: the 90 % ring of View ▸ Safe Areas (`SafeGuidesView`, spec §4.1's
52	    /// title-safe guide; the industry calls 90 % action-safe).
53	    static let cornerInsetFraction: Double = 0.05
54	
55	    /// The bottom-right corner patch for a `sourceWidth × sourceHeight`
56	    /// camera picture on a `canvasWidth × canvasHeight` canvas (CAM-10 (3)):
57	    /// the scale that fits the picture inside the corner box, clamped to the
58	    /// core's scale range (`props_check.rs`' `SCALE_MIN`, `SCALE_MAX`), and
59	    /// the `x`, `y` that put its bottom-right corner on the 90 % safe-area
60	    /// ring — an offset of the layer's centre from the canvas centre, y
61	    /// down (`core/src/edit_zoom.rs`'s C frame), rounded to whole pixels.
62	    /// nil when any dimension is not positive.
63	    static func cornerPatch(
64	        canvasWidth: Int, canvasHeight: Int, sourceWidth: Int, sourceHeight: Int
65	    ) -> VideoPatch? {
66	        guard canvasWidth > 0, canvasHeight > 0, sourceWidth > 0, sourceHeight > 0 else {
67	            return nil
68	        }
69	        let cw = Double(canvasWidth)
70	        let ch = Double(canvasHeight)
71	        let sw = Double(sourceWidth)
72	        let sh = Double(sourceHeight)
73	        let fit = min(cornerWidthFraction * cw / sw, cornerHeightFraction * ch / sh)
74	        let scale = min(max(fit, 0.01), 10)
75	        let x = (cw / 2 - cornerInsetFraction * cw - sw * scale / 2).rounded()
76	        let y = (ch / 2 - cornerInsetFraction * ch - sh * scale / 2).rounded()
77	        return VideoPatch(x: x, y: y, scale: scale)
78	    }
79	
80	    /// One entry per SEGMENT from a per-stretch list (`result.stretches`'
81	    /// order): the `.segment(k)` positions only. A left-out segment's voice
82	    /// is a stretch of its own and has no camera to place (CAM-10 (2)).
83	    static func segmentStarts(_ perStretch: [Ticks?], of result: RecordingResult) -> [Ticks?] {
84	        var starts: [Ticks?] = result.segments.map { _ in nil }
85	        for (stretch, at) in zip(result.stretches, perStretch) {
86	            if case .segment(let k) = stretch { starts[k] = at }
87	        }
88	        return starts
89	    }

91	    /// Every segment's camera file: its `add_media` in segment order, then —
92	    /// when `screenStarts` is given, one per segment — ONE new FRONT track
93	    /// named "Camera" and each camera clip by the floor rule, laid out with
94	    /// `screenClips[k]`, segment k's screen clip (nil where it minted none),
95	    /// as its screen (`layOut`). A nil
96	    /// `screenStarts` is `place: false`: the media land and no clip or track
97	    /// does; a nil ENTRY lands that camera as media only. Answers one media
98	    /// id and one clip id PER SEGMENT, nil where the segment has no camera
99	    /// file or its camera minted no clip — too short for a frame, or wholly
100	    /// under its head, each with its sentence in `notes`.
101	    ///
102	    /// The track's index is the container's track count when it is added,
103	    /// which — the pictures having landed first — puts it in front of every
104	    /// track, the pictures' included. Its id is `next_id` off the trial at
105	    /// that moment, unchanged by a discarded attempt.
106	    static func addCameras(
107	        _ result: RecordingResult, screenStarts: [Ticks?]?, screenClips: [UInt32?],
108	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp],
109	        notes: inout [String]
110	    ) throws -> (media: [UInt32?], clips: [UInt32?]) {
111	        precondition(
112	            screenStarts.map { $0.count == result.segments.count } ?? true,
113	            "one screen start per segment")
114	        precondition(screenClips.count == result.segments.count, "one screen clip per segment")
115	        var media: [UInt32?] = []
116	        for segment in result.segments {
117	            if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
118	                media.append(try addMedia(camera, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
119	            } else {
120	                media.append(nil)
121	            }
122	        }
123	        let none: [UInt32?] = result.segments.map { _ in nil }
124	        guard let starts = screenStarts else { return (media, none) }
125	        var track: UInt32?
126	        var clips: [UInt32?] = []
127	        var previousEnd: Ticks?
128	        for (k, segment) in result.segments.enumerated() {
129	            guard let id = media[k], let screenAt = starts[k] else {
130	                clips.append(nil)
131	                continue
132	            }
133	            var attempt = trial
134	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
135	            let on: UInt32
136	            if let added = track {
137	                on = added
138	            } else {
139	                let front = try view(of: attempt, scope: scope).snapshot.tracks.count
140	                on = attempt.snapshot.nextId
141	                let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: front, name: cameraTrackName)
142	                guard let withTrack = try attempt.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project
143	                else {
144	                    throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the camera could not be added.")
145	                }
146	                attempt = withTrack
147	                attemptOps.append(addTrack)
148	            }
149	            let behindCamera = previousEnd.map { $0 > screenAt } ?? false
150	            let floor = max(screenAt, previousEnd ?? screenAt)
151	            guard
152	                let placed = try addCameraClip(
153	                    id, on: on, screenAt: screenAt, offset: segment.cameraOffset, floor: floor,
154	                    behindCamera: behindCamera, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
155	                    notes: &notes)
156	            else {
157	                clips.append(nil)
158	                continue
159	            }
160	            try layOut(
161	                placed, screen: screenClips[k], layout: result.choice.cameraLayout, scope: scope,
162	                to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
163	            trial = attempt
164	            ops += attemptOps
165	            track = on
166	            clips.append(placed.id)
167	            previousEnd = placed.end
168	        }
169	        return (media, clips)
170	    }

172	    /// One camera clip on `track`, at `screenAt + offset` and never below
173	    /// `floor` — its screen clip's start, or the previous camera clip's end
174	    /// when that is later (`behindCamera`, which the note names). nil, with a
175	    /// sentence in `notes`, for a camera that gets no clip; the trial and the
176	    /// ops are advanced only for a clip returned.
177	    ///
178	    /// **The sign.** `offset` is the camera's first buffer minus the screen's
179	    /// start (CAM-9 (4)); positive means the camera began AFTER the screen,
180	    /// so its clip starts that much later — the opposite of the
181	    /// microphone's `micOffset`, which is measured the other way round.
182	    ///
183	    /// The rest is `addMicrophoneClip`'s, step for step: a start within half
184	    /// a frame of the floor makes no trim (the core's snap lands it there);
185	    /// further below, the head is the core's snap of the shortfall and
186	    /// `headTrimmed` adds at the floor, trims, moves back and reads every
187	    /// step back, a second try a frame up when an inexact rate lands the
188	    /// move a tick under the floor; a trim that clamps is a camera wholly
189	    /// under its head, media only with `cameraUnderNote`.
190	    static func addCameraClip(
191	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, screenAt: Ticks, offset: Ticks, floor: Ticks,
192	        behindCamera: Bool, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp],
193	        notes: inout [String]
194	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
195	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
196	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
197	        if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
198	            notes.append(note)
199	            return nil
200	        }
201	        let start = screenAt + offset
202	        let head = start < floor ? ReelTime.snapToFrame(floor - start, fps: fps) : 0
203	        guard head > 0 else {
204	            guard
205	                let placed = try placeClip(
206	                    media, on: track, at: max(start, floor), notBelow: floor, scope: scope,
207	                    to: &trial, ops: &ops)
208	            else {
209	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
210	            }
211	            return placed
212	        }
213	        let frame = fps.frameDuration
214	        for (at, head) in [(floor, head), (floor + frame, head + frame)] {
215	            var attempt = trial
216	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
217	            guard
218	                let placed = try headTrimmed(
219	                    media, file: file, on: track, at: at, head: head, floor: floor, fps: fps,
220	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
221	            else {
222	                notes.append(cameraUnderNote(file, head: head, behindCamera: behindCamera))
223	                return nil
224	            }
225	            if placed.start >= floor {
226	                trial = attempt
227	                ops += attemptOps
228	                return placed
229	            }
230	        }
231	        throw ReelCoreError(
232	            message: "\(file.path) could not be placed clear of the previous camera clip.")
233	    }
234	
235	    /// The camera clip laid out (CO-80): ONE `switch_layout` with `screen` as its screen at the
236	    /// clip's start, one frame of the CONTAINER's canvas long — the nest's inside one — in
237	    /// `layout`, `through` the later of the screen clip's end and the camera clip's, applied
238	    /// scoped and read back: the camera must then carry its layout action at clip time 0, or
239	    /// the throw names the clip. A refusal throws "Clip N could not be laid out:
240	    /// <the core's sentence>". With no screen clip, or one that does not play at the camera's
241	    /// start, the fallback is `corner` (CO-80 (c)), whatever the layout.
242	    private static func layOut(
243	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, screen: UInt32?, layout: RecordingCameraLayout,
244	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
245	    ) throws {
246	        let at = clip.start
247	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
248	        guard let screen, let shown = container.clips.first(where: { $0.id == screen }),
249	            shown.start <= at, at < shown.end
250	        else {
251	            try corner(clip, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
252	            return
253	        }
254	        let frame = container.canvas.fps.frameDuration
255	        let choice = layout.choice
256	        let op = ReelOp.switchLayout(
257	            camera: clip.id, screen: screen, layout: choice.kind, shape: choice.shape,
258	            corner: choice.corner, at: at, duration: frame, through: max(shown.end, clip.end))
259	        switch try trial.applying(op.scoped(scope)) {
260	        case .applied(let next):
261	            guard try self.clip(clip.id, in: next, scope: scope).actions.contains(where: {
262	                $0.start == 0
263	            })
264	            else {
265	                throw ReelCoreError(
266	                    message: "Clip \(clip.id) could not be laid out: it has no layout action "
267	                        + "at its first frame.")
268	            }
269	            trial = next
270	            ops.append(op)
271	        case .refused(let why):
272	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "Clip \(clip.id) could not be laid out: \(why.reason)")
273	        case .identity:
274	            throw ReelCoreError(
275	                message: "Clip \(clip.id) could not be laid out: the layout changed nothing.")
276	        }
277	    }
278	
279	    /// The fallback corner (`cornerPatch` over the CONTAINER's canvas — the nest's inside one —
280	    /// and the camera file's size) as one `set_video` on `clip`, applied and read back: the clip
281	    /// must report exactly the `x`, `y` and `scale` asked, or the throw names the clip. A size
282	    /// the patch cannot be made for (a dimension of 0) sets nothing.
283	    private static func corner(
284	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
285	    ) throws {
286	        guard case .media(let media, _, _) = clip.source else { return }
287	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
288	        let canvas = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas
289	        guard
290	            let patch = cornerPatch(
291	                canvasWidth: canvas.width, canvasHeight: canvas.height,
292	                sourceWidth: file.width, sourceHeight: file.height)
293	        else { return }
294	        let op = ReelOp.setVideo(clips: [clip.id], patch: patch)
295	        guard let next = try trial.applying(op.scoped(scope)).project,
296	            let video = try self.clip(clip.id, in: next, scope: scope).video,
297	            video.x == patch.x, video.y == patch.y, video.scale == patch.scale
298	        else {
299	            throw ReelCoreError(
300	                message: "Clip \(clip.id) could not be placed in the corner of the canvas.")
301	        }
302	        trial = next
303	        ops.append(op)
304	    }
305	
306	    /// The sentence for a camera wholly under its head.
307	    private static func cameraUnderNote(_ file: MediaSnapshot, head: Ticks, behindCamera: Bool)
308	        -> String
309	    {
310	        let clear = behindCamera ? "the previous camera clip" : "the start of its screen clip"
311	        return "\(file.path) was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of "
312	            + "it would remain after the \(milliseconds(head)) ms head that keeps it clear of "
313	            + "\(clear)."
314	    }
315	}

319	/// The calls a press of Record makes about the four grants, as values a
320	/// probe can replace: the reads, the four system prompts, the two remembered
321	/// "asked" flags and the one opener of System Settings. `live` is the app's;
322	/// `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` puts a sealed spy in
323	/// `RecorderPanelController.grantDoors` before any mode runs, so no probe
324	/// can prompt, open Settings or touch the key. Input Monitoring's four
325	/// (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-62) come last and default INERT —
326	/// never granted, never asking, never remembering — so a probe that fills
327	/// only the first ten compiles unchanged and can never prompt.
328	struct RecorderGrantDoors {
329	    /// Whether the panel has put up the Screen Recording prompt once
330	    /// (spec §11 recording). Written only by a launchd-owned press.
331	    static let screenRecordingAskedKey = "FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked"
332	    /// Whether the panel has asked for Input Monitoring once (spec §11 CU-3,
333	    /// CU-62). Written only by a launchd-owned press.
334	    static let inputMonitoringAskedKey = "FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked"
335	
336	    var screenGranted: () -> Bool
337	    var launchedByLaunchd: () -> Bool
338	    var requestScreen: () -> Void
339	    var screenAsked: () -> Bool
340	    var rememberScreenAsked: () -> Void
341	    var microphoneStatus: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus
342	    var requestMicrophone: (@escaping () -> Void) -> Void
343	    var openSettings: (URL) -> Bool
344	    /// The Camera grant (CR1c, spec §11 CAM-5), asked only for Source Camera.
345	    var cameraStatus: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus
346	    var requestCamera: (@escaping () -> Void) -> Void
347	    /// Input Monitoring (CU-62), read only with Record shortcuts on.
348	    var inputMonitoringGranted: () -> Bool = { false }
349	    var requestInputMonitoring: () -> Void = {}
350	    var inputMonitoringAsked: () -> Bool = { false }
351	    var rememberInputMonitoringAsked: () -> Void = {}
352	
353	    static var live: RecorderGrantDoors {
354	        RecorderGrantDoors(
355	            screenGranted: { RecordingGrant.screenRecordingGranted },
356	            launchedByLaunchd: { RecordingGrant.launchedByLaunchd },
357	            requestScreen: { _ = CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess() },
358	            screenAsked: { UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: screenRecordingAskedKey) },
359	            rememberScreenAsked: { UserDefaults.standard.set(true, forKey: screenRecordingAskedKey) },
360	            microphoneStatus: { RecordingGrant.microphoneStatus },
361	            requestMicrophone: { answered in
362	                // The framework does not say which queue it answers on, so
363	                // the answer hops to main.
364	                AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .audio) { _ in
365	                    DispatchQueue.main.async { answered() }
366	                }
367	            },
368	            openSettings: { url in NSWorkspace.shared.open(url) },
369	            cameraStatus: { RecordingGrant.cameraStatus },
370	            requestCamera: { answered in
371	                // As the microphone's: the answer hops to main.
372	                AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .video) { _ in

385	/// The grants, for the recorder panel (road map 3, R1c; spec §11
386	/// recording) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s seventh file, cut out of
387	/// `+Recording.swift` when the press learned to open System Settings.
388	///
389	/// **The grants are asked for HERE and nowhere else, and UNCONDITIONALLY**
390	/// (decision 4: the TOOL never asks — it reads the status and refuses by
391	/// name — because a system prompt needs a person in front of it; the panel
392	/// asks, because a press of Record IS that person, exactly as the transcribe
393	/// sheet's Start is). **This is also the only place System Settings is
394	/// opened for them**, and the tool never opens it. Screen Recording is
395	/// asked with `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` on the FIRST press that finds
396	/// it absent — the system prompt appears once per app, not per launch — and
397	/// the ask is remembered in `FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked`; every later press
398	/// opens the Screen & System Audio Recording pane and the note says so.
399	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` returns false at once on a first ask, so
400	/// the refusal sentence is shown either way and the person presses Record
401	/// again once the grant is on. The flag is read and written only in a
402	/// launchd-owned launch: a shell-launched press always asks and never
403	/// remembers, because TCC attributes that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1).
404	/// The microphone is asked only when one is chosen, from `.notDetermined`,
405	/// and the countdown starts from the answer; `.denied` and `.restricted`
406	/// open the Microphone pane and stop there, and a prompt's answer never
407	/// opens it. Both readings happen BEFORE the countdown, so a countdown never
408	/// ends in a prompt. An earlier draft gated both asks on a `canAsk` (since
409	/// deleted with the speech grant) — false for a scripted agent launch —
410	/// and the R1 review measured what that cost: under that flag the refusal
411	/// note told the person to press the button they had just pressed, and a
412	/// `notDetermined` microphone could never be granted from anywhere.
413	/// `canAsk` is the tool's rule about a prompt nobody would see; it does not
414	/// apply to a button somebody clicked. **The Camera grant** (CR1c, spec §11
415	/// CAM-5) is the third, read only for Source Camera, whose press never reads
416	/// Screen Recording: the microphone's steps, through its own pane
417	/// (`Privacy_Camera`), and its prompt's answer RE-READS the grant before the
418	/// microphone and the countdown, so a refused prompt stops there. **Input
419	/// Monitoring** (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-3, CU-62) is the
420	/// fourth, read only when Record shortcuts is on with a screen source, after
421	/// Screen Recording and before the Camera and the Microphone. Its step is
422	/// Screen Recording's table, remembered in `FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked`;
423	/// because no prompt shows and Frame Job is not listed until a person adds
424	/// it (CU0b), an ask ALSO opens the Input Monitoring pane, and the note says
425	/// to add Frame Job with + (`inputMonitoringNote(opened:)`).
426	extension RecorderPanelController {
427	    /// The doors every grant call goes through; a probe replaces it.
428	    static var grantDoors = RecorderGrantDoors.live
429	
430	    /// A system prompt, or System Settings, is about to come up in ANOTHER
431	    /// process at normal window level, and a `.floating` panel sits over
432	    /// every normal window on the screen: the person found the Screen
433	    /// Recording prompt hidden behind the panel until they dragged it away
434	    /// (2026-09-28). So the panel steps down to `.normal` first, and
435	    /// `floatAgain` puts it back on the next press that goes on, or on
436	    /// `show()`.
437	    func stepAsideForSystemUI() { window?.level = .normal }
438	    func floatAgain() { window?.level = .floating }
439	
440	    /// Screen Recording, for a press: true to go on; false with the note
441	    /// set, and the press ends. `screenStep` is the one decision point.
442	    func checkScreenRecordingGrant() -> Bool {
443	        floatAgain()
444	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
445	        let owned = doors.launchedByLaunchd()
446	        let step = RecordingGrant.screenStep(
447	            granted: doors.screenGranted(), asked: doors.screenAsked(), launchedByLaunchd: owned)
448	        switch step {
449	        case .proceed:
450	            return true
451	        case .ask:
452	            if owned { doors.rememberScreenAsked() }
453	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
454	            doors.requestScreen()
455	            setNote(RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal)
456	            return false
457	        case .openPane:
458	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
459	            let opened = RecordingGrant.screenRecordingPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
460	            setNote(
461	                opened ? RecordingGrant.screenRecordingOpenedNote : RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal)
462	            return false
463	        }
464	    }
465	
466	    /// Input Monitoring, for a press (CU-62): true to go on — Record shortcuts
467	    /// off (it is `.off` for a voice-over and a camera) or granted; false with
468	    /// the note set, and the press ends. `inputMonitoringStep` decides.
469	    func checkInputMonitoringGrant() -> Bool {
470	        guard currentChoice().keys == .shortcuts else { return true }
471	        floatAgain()
472	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
473	        let owned = doors.launchedByLaunchd()
474	        let step = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringStep(
475	            granted: doors.inputMonitoringGranted(), asked: doors.inputMonitoringAsked(),
476	            launchedByLaunchd: owned)
477	        switch step {
478	        case .proceed:
479	            return true
480	        case .ask:
481	            if owned { doors.rememberInputMonitoringAsked() }
482	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
483	            doors.requestInputMonitoring()
484	            let opened = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
485	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))
486	            return false
487	        case .openPane:
488	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
489	            let opened = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
490	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))
491	            return false
492	        }
493	    }
494	
495	    /// The microphone, for a press: true to go on (none chosen, or
496	    /// authorized); false when it asked (the answer continues the press) or
497	    /// opened its pane.
498	    func checkMicrophoneGrant() -> Bool {
499	        guard currentChoice().microphone != nil else { return true }
500	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
501	        let status = doors.microphoneStatus()
502	        switch RecordingGrant.microphoneStep(status) {
503	        case .proceed:
504	            return true
505	        case .ask:
506	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
507	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
508	            doors.requestMicrophone { [weak self] in self?.microphoneAnswered() }
509	            return false
510	        case .openPane:
511	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
512	            let opened = RecordingGrant.microphonePaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
513	            setNote(
514	                opened
515	                    ? RecordingGrant.microphoneOpenedNote(status)
516	                    : RecordingGrant.microphoneRefusal(status))
517	            return false
518	        }
519	    }
520	
521	    /// The prompt's answer. The button comes back either way; the countdown
522	    /// begins only in an idle panel that is still ON SCREEN (R1 review) — a
523	    /// panel closed during the prompt must not count down where nobody can
524	    /// cancel it, and `panelWillClose` cannot cancel a countdown that has not
525	    /// begun. It never opens System Settings.
526	    private func microphoneAnswered() {
527	        recordButton.isEnabled = true
528	        guard phase == .idle, window?.isVisible == true else { return }
529	        let status = Self.grantDoors.microphoneStatus()
530	        guard status == .authorized else {
531	            setNote(RecordingGrant.microphoneRefusal(status))
532	            return
533	        }
534	        setNote("")
535	        floatAgain()
536	        beginCountdown()
537	    }
538	
539	    /// The camera, for a press with Source Camera: true to go on
540	    /// (authorized); false when it asked (the answer continues the press) or
541	    /// opened its pane — `checkMicrophoneGrant`'s three arms.
542	    func checkCameraGrant() -> Bool {
543	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
544	        let status = doors.cameraStatus()
545	        switch RecordingGrant.cameraStep(status) {
546	        case .proceed:
547	            return true
548	        case .ask:
549	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
550	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
551	            doors.requestCamera { [weak self] in self?.cameraAnswered() }
552	            return false
553	        case .openPane:
554	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
555	            let opened = RecordingGrant.cameraPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
556	            setNote(
557	                opened
558	                    ? RecordingGrant.cameraOpenedNote(status)
559	                    : RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(status))
560	            return false
561	        }
562	    }
563	
564	    /// The camera prompt's answer, `microphoneAnswered`'s rule: the button
565	    /// comes back either way, and the press goes on only in an idle panel
566	    /// still on screen. The grant is READ AGAIN first — anything but
567	    /// authorized stops with the refusal, no microphone prompt and no
568	    /// countdown — then the microphone's grant, then the countdown.
569	    private func cameraAnswered() {
570	        recordButton.isEnabled = true
571	        guard phase == .idle, window?.isVisible == true else { return }
572	        let status = Self.grantDoors.cameraStatus()
573	        guard status == .authorized else {
574	            setNote(RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(status))
575	            return
576	        }
577	        setNote("")
578	        floatAgain()
579	        guard checkMicrophoneGrant() else { return }
580	        beginCountdown()
581	    }
582	}

713	/// Who is the camera and who the screen for the menu (CO-66).
714	enum CameraLayoutRoles {
715	    /// The track a recording's camera lands on (`RecordingLanding`).
716	    static let cameraTrackName = "Camera"
717	
718	    /// Two selected picture clips on different tracks: the front one is the
719	    /// camera and the other the screen. One: it is the camera and the core
720	    /// finds the screen. None: the clip at the playhead on the front-most
721	    /// track named "Camera". nil when that yields no camera containing the
722	    /// playhead.
723	    static func roles(selected: [ClipSnapshot], playhead: Ticks, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot)
724	        -> (camera: UInt32, screen: UInt32?)?
725	    {
726	        let picture = { (clip: ClipSnapshot) in
727	            clip.video != nil && snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip) != nil
728	        }
729	        let plays = { (clip: ClipSnapshot) in clip.start <= playhead && playhead < clip.end }
730	        switch selected.count {
731	        case 2:
732	            guard selected.allSatisfy(picture),
733	                let a = snapshot.trackIndex(of: selected[0].track),
734	                let b = snapshot.trackIndex(of: selected[1].track), a != b
735	            else { return nil }
736	            let (camera, screen) = a > b ? (selected[0], selected[1]) : (selected[1], selected[0])
737	            return plays(camera) ? (camera.id, screen.id) : nil
738	        case 1:
739	            let camera = selected[0]
740	            return picture(camera) && plays(camera) ? (camera.id, nil) : nil
741	        case 0:
742	            guard let track = snapshot.tracks.last(where: { $0.name == cameraTrackName }),
743	                let camera = snapshot.clips.first(where: {
744	                    $0.track == track.id && plays($0) && picture($0)
745	                })
746	            else { return nil }
747	            return (camera.id, nil)
748	        default:
749	            return nil
750	        }
751	    }
752	}

339	enum CameraPreviewStep: Equatable {

341	    case message(String)
342	    case failed(String)
343	    case prepare
344	    case prepared
345	    case recording
346	    case blank

349	/// The camera's live preview in the panel (camera-recording CR2b, spec §11
350	/// CAM-7) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s eleventh file, NEW rather than
351	/// cut, as `+Camera.swift` was: the rule that says what the well shows, and
352	/// the one sync that acts on it. The well is `CameraPreviewWell`, a grid row
353	/// of its own right under Format (`+Rows.swift`), shown only while a camera
354	/// is wanted: Source Camera, or "Record the camera too" beside a screen
355	/// source (spec §11 CAM-11 (4)).
356	///
357	/// **The step** (`cameraPreviewStep`, pure, first match wins): a panel not
358	/// visible or closing, or no camera wanted → off; a camera recording, or a
359	/// screen recording's camera beside it → its layer; the countdown or
360	/// starting → the prepared layer, never a build; any other phase, or a
361	/// busy recorder → blank; no camera → "No camera is connected."; the
362	/// Camera grant not authorized → a sentence; a prepared capture that
363	/// failed, or a build that threw → its sentence, never retried; else
364	/// prepare. The grant is read only at its own step, through
365	/// `grantDoors.cameraStatus`, so showing the panel never prompts and a
366	/// hidden panel reads nothing.
367	///
368	/// **The sync** runs at the end of `show()`, of every control change, of
369	/// `syncPhase()`, at the one-second tick while the panel is visible, and at
370	/// each device notification. Its first act applies a pending hot-plug
371	/// (`+Devices.swift`, CAM-8 (2)), so the step sees the new selection. It
372	/// keeps the row's visibility (refitting the window when it changes), lets
373	/// the prepared capture go when the well is off or shows a sentence while
374	/// everything is idle, stops a failed prepared capture once (not at every
375	/// tick, CAM-8 (6)), and otherwise hosts the layer the step names. The
376	/// capture is the recorder's (`ScreenRecorder+CameraPrepare.swift`): the
377	/// countdown's `prepareCamera` keeps it, the panel's start adopts it, and a
378	/// tool's start never does (CAM-7 (7)), so through a tool's recording the
379	/// well reads "The camera is recording."
380	extension RecorderPanelController {
381	    static let previewGrantSentence = "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera."
382	    static let previewRecordingSentence = "The camera is recording."
383	
384	    /// CAM-7 (3)'s rule. `grant` and `failure` are called only at their own
385	    /// steps.
386	    static func cameraPreviewStep(
387	        visible: Bool, cameraSource: Bool, phase: Phase, recorderIdle: Bool,
388	        recordingCamera: Bool, cameraChosen: Bool, grant: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus,
389	        failure: () -> String?
390	    ) -> CameraPreviewStep {
391	        guard visible, cameraSource else { return .off }
392	        if recordingCamera { return .recording }
393	        switch phase {
394	        case .countdown, .starting: return .prepared
395	        case .idle: break
396	        case .recording, .paused, .stopping, .landing: return .blank
397	        }
398	        guard recorderIdle else { return .blank }
399	        guard cameraChosen else { return .message(CameraDevices.noCameraSentence) }
400	        guard grant() == .authorized else { return .message(Self.previewGrantSentence) }
401	        if let failure = failure() { return .failed(failure) }
402	        return .prepare
403	    }
404	
405	    /// The well's grid row.
406	    var cameraPreviewRow: NSGridRow? {
407	        (cameraPreview.superview as? NSGridView)?.cell(for: cameraPreview)?.row
408	    }
409	
410	    /// For the chosen camera at its resolved format (CAM-6 (3)): the
411	    /// prepared capture's stop on its own, else its failed start, else a
412	    /// failed build's record; nil when there is none.
413	    var previewFailure: String? {
414	        guard let id = selectedCameraID, let device = CameraDevices.device(withID: id) else {
415	            return nil
416	        }
417	        let facts = CameraDevices.facts(of: device)
418	        guard
419	            let format = CameraDevices.chosenFormat(
420	                selectedCameraFormat, in: facts.formats, active: facts.activeFormat)
421	        else { return nil }
422	        if let prepared = recorder.preparedCamera, prepared.deviceID == id, prepared.format == format,
423	            let sentence = prepared.stoppedOnItsOwn ?? prepared.startError?.localizedDescription
424	        {
425	            return sentence
426	        }
427	        guard let failure = recorder.preparedCameraFailure, failure.deviceID == id,
428	            failure.format == format
429	        else { return nil }
430	        return failure.sentence
431	    }
432	
433	    /// A pending hot-plug applied (CAM-8 (2)), the row's visibility, then the
434	    /// step acted on (the type doc).
435	    func syncCameraPreview() {
436	        applyPendingDevices()
437	        let hidden = !cameraWanted
438	        if let row = cameraPreviewRow, row.isHidden != hidden {
439	            row.isHidden = hidden
440	            fitWindowToContent()
441	        }
442	        let step = Self.cameraPreviewStep(
443	            visible: window?.isVisible == true && !panelClosing, cameraSource: cameraWanted,
444	            phase: phase, recorderIdle: recorder.state == .idle,
445	            recordingCamera: recorder.cameraSession != nil || recorder.session?.cameraCapture != nil,
446	            cameraChosen: selectedCameraID != nil,
447	            grant: { Self.grantDoors.cameraStatus() }, failure: { self.previewFailure })
448	        switch step {
449	        case .off, .message:
450	            if phase == .idle, recorder.state == .idle { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
451	            if case .message(let sentence) = step {
452	                cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
453	            } else {
454	                cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
455	            }
456	        case .failed(let sentence):
457	            if let capture = recorder.preparedCamera?.capture, !capture.stopped { capture.stop() }
458	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
459	        case .prepare:
460	            recorder.prepareCamera(for: currentChoice())
461	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
462	        case .prepared:
463	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
464	        case .recording:
465	            hostPreview(
466	                (recorder.cameraSession?.capture ?? recorder.session?.cameraCapture)?.previewLayer,
467	                else: Self.previewRecordingSentence)
468	        case .blank:
469	            cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
470	        }
471	    }
472	
473	    /// `layer` in the well, else `sentence` (nil a blank well).
474	    private func hostPreview(_ layer: AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer?, else sentence: String?) {
475	        if let layer {
476	            cameraPreview.show(layer)
477	        } else {
478	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
479	        }
480	    }
481	}

484	/// "Remove the camera's background when it lands" (road map "creator-jobs" CO8, spec §11
485	/// CO-81): Remove Background run over a finished recording's CAMERA clips as a follow-up to the
486	/// landing — never part of it — as its own undo step, "Remove Background", in AU-68's pattern
487	/// with no wait: the masks are wanted by the edit itself (`ensureMasks`, after every edit), so
488	/// nothing need be measured first. Both doors call `apply` right after the landing's commit and
489	/// before Enhance Voice and the polish (CU-101 (a)): the panel's two branches
490	/// (`RecorderPanelController+Landing.swift`) and the tool's `landAndEnhance`. On-device, so
491	/// never keyed (CJ-3). Names no `rc_*`; main thread.
492	enum RecordingCutout {
493	    /// The undo step's name, Clip ▸ Remove Background's.
494	    static let actionName = "Remove Background"
495	    /// The tool's `camera_cutout_error` when no camera clip took the cutout.
496	    static let noCameraSentence =
497	        "No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run."
498	
499	    /// Every segment's camera file, in segment order; empty paths dropped, each path once. Pure.
500	    static func cameraPaths(of result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
501	        var seen: Set<String> = []
502	        return result.segments.compactMap { $0.cameraDescriptor?.path }
503	            .map(RecordingLanding.trimmed)
504	            .filter { !$0.isEmpty && seen.insert($0).inserted }
505	    }
506	
507	    /// Every clip of the open container whose media is one of `paths`, that can be cut out
508	    /// (`CutoutStatus.canCutOut`) and has no cutout yet, in id order. Main.
509	    static func cameraClips(_ paths: [String], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
510	        let wanted = Set(paths)
511	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return [] }
512	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
513	        return snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
514	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip), wanted.contains(media.path) else {
515	                return false
516	            }
517	            return CutoutStatus.canCutOut(clip, in: snapshot) && clip.video?.cutout == nil
518	        }.map(\.id).sorted()
519	    }
520	
521	    /// One base `set_video {cutout}` per clip, the whole default cutout, as Clip ▸ Remove
522	    /// Background writes. Pure over the ids.
523	    static func ops(_ clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [ReelOp] {
524	        clips.map { .setVideo(clips: [$0], patch: VideoPatch(cutout: .some(CutoutProps()))) }
525	    }
526	
527	    /// When the recording's choice asks for it, its camera clips cut out as ONE grouped step
528	    /// "Remove Background" (`performGroupedEdit`: a landing is not an AppKit event). Answers the
529	    /// clips the step was asked for, empty when the choice did not ask or no camera clip
530	    /// qualifies (the panel is then quiet; the tool answers `noCameraSentence`). Main.
531	    @discardableResult static func apply(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument)
532	        -> [UInt32]
533	    {
534	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
535	        guard result.choice.cameraCutout else { return [] }
536	        let clips = cameraClips(cameraPaths(of: result), in: document)
537	        guard !clips.isEmpty else { return [] }
538	        document.performGroupedEdit(actionName, ops(clips, in: document))
539	        return clips
540	    }
541	}

1	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding+Camera.swift — the camera half of the landing
2	// (camera-recording CR3b, spec §11 CAM-10): a screen recording's
3	// `(Camera).mov` files, one per segment (CAM-9), on ONE new FRONT track
4	// named "Camera", each clip lined up with its screen segment by the
5	// segment's measured `cameraOffset` and laid out in the recorder's layout.
6	//
7	// `addCameras` is `addMicrophones`' shape, attempt for attempt: every file's
8	// `add_media` in segment order, then — with the screen's starts — the track
9	// added on the attempt of the first camera clip that takes a frame and kept
10	// only when that clip lands, and each clip by the floor rule. The floor is
11	// `max(screenStart_k, previous camera clip's end)`, so a camera never starts
12	// before its own screen clip and never overlaps the camera before it, and a
13	// start below the floor is head-trimmed by the microphone's own dance
14	// (`headTrimmed`, `+Microphone`, internal for this file). CR3a measured
15	// every offset NEGATIVE — the camera begins 32–146 ms before the screen — so
16	// the trim is the ordinary path here, not the exception it is for a voice.
17	//
18	// The layout (road map "creator-jobs" CO8, spec §11 CO-80) is ONE
19	// `switch_layout` per camera clip right after its placement: the camera and
20	// its segment's screen clip at the camera clip's start, one canvas frame
21	// long so both roles CUT there, in `choice.cameraLayout` (Corner by
22	// default, the owner's answer, which is CAM-10 (3)'s corner to the pixel),
23	// its reach bounded by `through` = the later of the screen clip's end and
24	// the camera clip's, so it re-bases only a later screen clip this camera
25	// overruns into — never a later segment's own screen, nor a clip placed
26	// before the recording. No curve, focus or nest: no masks exist yet, so the
27	// crop centres on the source. When the segment's screen minted no clip, or
28	// its clip does not play at the camera's start, `cornerPatch` is the
29	// fallback (CO-80 (c)): arithmetic over the container's canvas and the
30	// file's size, the precedent `CaptionStyle.size(for:)` set for a Swift-side
31	// placement — a quarter of the canvas wide, a third of it tall, inside the
32	// 90 % ring of View ▸ Safe Areas (`SafeGuidesView`) — as one `set_video {x,
33	// y, scale}`, read back. Either way the clip stays an ordinary clip a person
34	// moves, and Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ re-lays it.
35	//
36	// The ops come back UNSCOPED, as every landing op does; the trial applies
37	// them scoped exactly as the commit will (the base file's header).
