41	extension RecordingLanding {
42	    /// The new front track every camera clip lands on — ONE for the whole
43	    /// recording, added with the first camera clip that takes a frame, so a
44	    /// recording none of whose camera files can be placed adds no track.
45	    static let cameraTrackName = "Camera"
46	    /// The corner box is a quarter of the canvas wide…
47	    static let cornerWidthFraction: Double = 0.25
48	    /// …and a third of it tall; the picture is scaled to fit inside both.
49	    static let cornerHeightFraction: Double = 1.0 / 3.0
50	    /// The inset from the canvas's right and bottom edges, as a fraction of
51	    /// each: the 90 % ring of View ▸ Safe Areas (`SafeGuidesView`, spec §4.1's
52	    /// title-safe guide; the industry calls 90 % action-safe).
53	    static let cornerInsetFraction: Double = 0.05
54	
55	    /// The bottom-right corner patch for a `sourceWidth × sourceHeight`
56	    /// camera picture on a `canvasWidth × canvasHeight` canvas (CAM-10 (3)):
57	    /// the scale that fits the picture inside the corner box, clamped to the
58	    /// core's scale range (`props_check.rs`' `SCALE_MIN`, `SCALE_MAX`), and
59	    /// the `x`, `y` that put its bottom-right corner on the 90 % safe-area
60	    /// ring — an offset of the layer's centre from the canvas centre, y
61	    /// down (`core/src/edit_zoom.rs`'s C frame), rounded to whole pixels.
62	    /// nil when any dimension is not positive.
63	    static func cornerPatch(
64	        canvasWidth: Int, canvasHeight: Int, sourceWidth: Int, sourceHeight: Int
65	    ) -> VideoPatch? {
66	        guard canvasWidth > 0, canvasHeight > 0, sourceWidth > 0, sourceHeight > 0 else {
67	            return nil
68	        }
69	        let cw = Double(canvasWidth)
70	        let ch = Double(canvasHeight)
71	        let sw = Double(sourceWidth)
72	        let sh = Double(sourceHeight)
73	        let fit = min(cornerWidthFraction * cw / sw, cornerHeightFraction * ch / sh)
74	        let scale = min(max(fit, 0.01), 10)
75	        let x = (cw / 2 - cornerInsetFraction * cw - sw * scale / 2).rounded()
76	        let y = (ch / 2 - cornerInsetFraction * ch - sh * scale / 2).rounded()
77	        return VideoPatch(x: x, y: y, scale: scale)
78	    }

80	    /// One entry per SEGMENT from a per-stretch list (`result.stretches`'
81	    /// order): the `.segment(k)` positions only. A left-out segment's voice
82	    /// is a stretch of its own and has no camera to place (CAM-10 (2)).
83	    static func segmentStarts(_ perStretch: [Ticks?], of result: RecordingResult) -> [Ticks?] {
84	        var starts: [Ticks?] = result.segments.map { _ in nil }
85	        for (stretch, at) in zip(result.stretches, perStretch) {
86	            if case .segment(let k) = stretch { starts[k] = at }
87	        }
88	        return starts
89	    }

91	    /// Every segment's camera file: its `add_media` in segment order, then —
92	    /// when `screenStarts` is given, one per segment — ONE new FRONT track
93	    /// named "Camera" and each camera clip by the floor rule, laid out with
94	    /// `screenClips[k]`, segment k's screen clip (nil where it minted none),
95	    /// as its screen (`layOut`). A nil
96	    /// `screenStarts` is `place: false`: the media land and no clip or track
97	    /// does; a nil ENTRY lands that camera as media only. Answers one media
98	    /// id and one clip id PER SEGMENT, nil where the segment has no camera
99	    /// file or its camera minted no clip — too short for a frame, or wholly
100	    /// under its head, each with its sentence in `notes`.
101	    ///
102	    /// The track's index is the container's track count when it is added,
103	    /// which — the pictures having landed first — puts it in front of every
104	    /// track, the pictures' included. Its id is `next_id` off the trial at
105	    /// that moment, unchanged by a discarded attempt.
106	    static func addCameras(
107	        _ result: RecordingResult, screenStarts: [Ticks?]?, screenClips: [UInt32?],
108	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp],
109	        notes: inout [String]
110	    ) throws -> (media: [UInt32?], clips: [UInt32?]) {
111	        precondition(
112	            screenStarts.map { $0.count == result.segments.count } ?? true,
113	            "one screen start per segment")
114	        precondition(screenClips.count == result.segments.count, "one screen clip per segment")
115	        var media: [UInt32?] = []
116	        for segment in result.segments {
117	            if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
118	                media.append(try addMedia(camera, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
119	            } else {
120	                media.append(nil)
121	            }
122	        }
123	        let none: [UInt32?] = result.segments.map { _ in nil }
124	        guard let starts = screenStarts else { return (media, none) }
125	        var track: UInt32?
126	        var clips: [UInt32?] = []
127	        var previousEnd: Ticks?
128	        for (k, segment) in result.segments.enumerated() {
129	            guard let id = media[k], let screenAt = starts[k] else {
130	                clips.append(nil)
131	                continue
132	            }
133	            var attempt = trial
134	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
135	            let on: UInt32
136	            if let added = track {
137	                on = added
138	            } else {
139	                let front = try view(of: attempt, scope: scope).snapshot.tracks.count
140	                on = attempt.snapshot.nextId
141	                let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: front, name: cameraTrackName)
142	                guard let withTrack = try attempt.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project
143	                else {
144	                    throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the camera could not be added.")
145	                }
146	                attempt = withTrack
147	                attemptOps.append(addTrack)
148	            }
149	            let behindCamera = previousEnd.map { $0 > screenAt } ?? false
150	            let floor = max(screenAt, previousEnd ?? screenAt)
151	            guard
152	                let placed = try addCameraClip(
153	                    id, on: on, screenAt: screenAt, offset: segment.cameraOffset, floor: floor,
154	                    behindCamera: behindCamera, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
155	                    notes: &notes)
156	            else {
157	                clips.append(nil)
158	                continue
159	            }
160	            try layOut(
161	                placed, screen: screenClips[k], layout: result.choice.cameraLayout, scope: scope,
162	                to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
163	            trial = attempt
164	            ops += attemptOps
165	            track = on
166	            clips.append(placed.id)
167	            previousEnd = placed.end
168	        }
169	        return (media, clips)
170	    }

172	    /// One camera clip on `track`, at `screenAt + offset` and never below
173	    /// `floor` — its screen clip's start, or the previous camera clip's end
174	    /// when that is later (`behindCamera`, which the note names). nil, with a
175	    /// sentence in `notes`, for a camera that gets no clip; the trial and the
176	    /// ops are advanced only for a clip returned.
177	    ///
178	    /// **The sign.** `offset` is the camera's first buffer minus the screen's
179	    /// start (CAM-9 (4)); positive means the camera began AFTER the screen,
180	    /// so its clip starts that much later — the opposite of the
181	    /// microphone's `micOffset`, which is measured the other way round.
182	    ///
183	    /// The rest is `addMicrophoneClip`'s, step for step: a start within half
184	    /// a frame of the floor makes no trim (the core's snap lands it there);
185	    /// further below, the head is the core's snap of the shortfall and
186	    /// `headTrimmed` adds at the floor, trims, moves back and reads every
187	    /// step back, a second try a frame up when an inexact rate lands the
188	    /// move a tick under the floor; a trim that clamps is a camera wholly
189	    /// under its head, media only with `cameraUnderNote`.
190	    static func addCameraClip(
191	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, screenAt: Ticks, offset: Ticks, floor: Ticks,
192	        behindCamera: Bool, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp],
193	        notes: inout [String]
194	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
195	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
196	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
197	        if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
198	            notes.append(note)
199	            return nil
200	        }
201	        let start = screenAt + offset
202	        let head = start < floor ? ReelTime.snapToFrame(floor - start, fps: fps) : 0
203	        guard head > 0 else {
204	            guard
205	                let placed = try placeClip(
206	                    media, on: track, at: max(start, floor), notBelow: floor, scope: scope,
207	                    to: &trial, ops: &ops)
208	            else {
209	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
210	            }
211	            return placed
212	        }
213	        let frame = fps.frameDuration
214	        for (at, head) in [(floor, head), (floor + frame, head + frame)] {
215	            var attempt = trial
216	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
217	            guard
218	                let placed = try headTrimmed(
219	                    media, file: file, on: track, at: at, head: head, floor: floor, fps: fps,
220	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
221	            else {
222	                notes.append(cameraUnderNote(file, head: head, behindCamera: behindCamera))
223	                return nil
224	            }
225	            if placed.start >= floor {
226	                trial = attempt
227	                ops += attemptOps
228	                return placed
229	            }
230	        }
231	        throw ReelCoreError(
232	            message: "\(file.path) could not be placed clear of the previous camera clip.")
233	    }
234	
235	    /// The camera clip laid out (CO-80): ONE `switch_layout` with `screen` as its screen at the
236	    /// clip's start, one frame of the CONTAINER's canvas long — the nest's inside one — in
237	    /// `layout`, `through` the later of the screen clip's end and the camera clip's, applied
238	    /// scoped and read back: the camera must then carry its layout action at clip time 0, or
239	    /// the throw names the clip. A refusal throws "Clip N could not be laid out:
240	    /// <the core's sentence>". With no screen clip, or one that does not play at the camera's
241	    /// start, the fallback is `corner` (CO-80 (c)), whatever the layout.
242	    private static func layOut(
243	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, screen: UInt32?, layout: RecordingCameraLayout,
244	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
245	    ) throws {
246	        let at = clip.start
247	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
248	        guard let screen, let shown = container.clips.first(where: { $0.id == screen }),
249	            shown.start <= at, at < shown.end
250	        else {
251	            try corner(clip, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
252	            return
253	        }
254	        let frame = container.canvas.fps.frameDuration
255	        let choice = layout.choice
256	        let op = ReelOp.switchLayout(
257	            camera: clip.id, screen: screen, layout: choice.kind, shape: choice.shape,
258	            corner: choice.corner, at: at, duration: frame, through: max(shown.end, clip.end))
259	        switch try trial.applying(op.scoped(scope)) {
260	        case .applied(let next):
261	            guard try self.clip(clip.id, in: next, scope: scope).actions.contains(where: {
262	                $0.start == 0
263	            })
264	            else {
265	                throw ReelCoreError(
266	                    message: "Clip \(clip.id) could not be laid out: it has no layout action "
267	                        + "at its first frame.")
268	            }
269	            trial = next
270	            ops.append(op)
271	        case .refused(let why):
272	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "Clip \(clip.id) could not be laid out: \(why.reason)")
273	        case .identity:
274	            throw ReelCoreError(
275	                message: "Clip \(clip.id) could not be laid out: the layout changed nothing.")
276	        }
277	    }
278	
279	    /// The fallback corner (`cornerPatch` over the CONTAINER's canvas — the nest's inside one —
280	    /// and the camera file's size) as one `set_video` on `clip`, applied and read back: the clip
281	    /// must report exactly the `x`, `y` and `scale` asked, or the throw names the clip. A size
282	    /// the patch cannot be made for (a dimension of 0) sets nothing.
283	    private static func corner(
284	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
285	    ) throws {
286	        guard case .media(let media, _, _) = clip.source else { return }
287	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
288	        let canvas = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas
289	        guard
290	            let patch = cornerPatch(
291	                canvasWidth: canvas.width, canvasHeight: canvas.height,
292	                sourceWidth: file.width, sourceHeight: file.height)
293	        else { return }
294	        let op = ReelOp.setVideo(clips: [clip.id], patch: patch)
295	        guard let next = try trial.applying(op.scoped(scope)).project,
296	            let video = try self.clip(clip.id, in: next, scope: scope).video,
297	            video.x == patch.x, video.y == patch.y, video.scale == patch.scale
298	        else {
299	            throw ReelCoreError(
300	                message: "Clip \(clip.id) could not be placed in the corner of the canvas.")
301	        }
302	        trial = next
303	        ops.append(op)
304	    }
305	
306	    /// The sentence for a camera wholly under its head.
307	    private static func cameraUnderNote(_ file: MediaSnapshot, head: Ticks, behindCamera: Bool)
308	        -> String
309	    {
310	        let clear = behindCamera ? "the previous camera clip" : "the start of its screen clip"
311	        return "\(file.path) was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of "
312	            + "it would remain after the \(milliseconds(head)) ms head that keeps it clear of "
313	            + "\(clear)."
314	    }

342	    var requestMicrophone: (@escaping () -> Void) -> Void

385	/// The grants, for the recorder panel (road map 3, R1c; spec §11
386	/// recording) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s seventh file, cut out of
387	/// `+Recording.swift` when the press learned to open System Settings.
388	///
389	/// **The grants are asked for HERE and nowhere else, and UNCONDITIONALLY**
390	/// (decision 4: the TOOL never asks — it reads the status and refuses by
391	/// name — because a system prompt needs a person in front of it; the panel
392	/// asks, because a press of Record IS that person, exactly as the transcribe
393	/// sheet's Start is). **This is also the only place System Settings is
394	/// opened for them**, and the tool never opens it. Screen Recording is
395	/// asked with `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` on the FIRST press that finds
396	/// it absent — the system prompt appears once per app, not per launch — and
397	/// the ask is remembered in `FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked`; every later press
398	/// opens the Screen & System Audio Recording pane and the note says so.
399	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` returns false at once on a first ask, so
400	/// the refusal sentence is shown either way and the person presses Record
401	/// again once the grant is on. The flag is read and written only in a
402	/// launchd-owned launch: a shell-launched press always asks and never
403	/// remembers, because TCC attributes that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1).
404	/// The microphone is asked only when one is chosen, from `.notDetermined`,
405	/// and the countdown starts from the answer; `.denied` and `.restricted`
406	/// open the Microphone pane and stop there, and a prompt's answer never
407	/// opens it. Both readings happen BEFORE the countdown, so a countdown never
408	/// ends in a prompt. An earlier draft gated both asks on a `canAsk` (since
409	/// deleted with the speech grant) — false for a scripted agent launch —
410	/// and the R1 review measured what that cost: under that flag the refusal
411	/// note told the person to press the button they had just pressed, and a
412	/// `notDetermined` microphone could never be granted from anywhere.
413	/// `canAsk` is the tool's rule about a prompt nobody would see; it does not
414	/// apply to a button somebody clicked. **The Camera grant** (CR1c, spec §11
415	/// CAM-5) is the third, read only for Source Camera, whose press never reads
416	/// Screen Recording: the microphone's steps, through its own pane
417	/// (`Privacy_Camera`), and its prompt's answer RE-READS the grant before the
418	/// microphone and the countdown, so a refused prompt stops there. **Input
419	/// Monitoring** (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-3, CU-62) is the
420	/// fourth, read only when Record shortcuts is on with a screen source, after
421	/// Screen Recording and before the Camera and the Microphone. Its step is
422	/// Screen Recording's table, remembered in `FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked`;
423	/// because no prompt shows and Frame Job is not listed until a person adds
424	/// it (CU0b), an ask ALSO opens the Input Monitoring pane, and the note says
425	/// to add Frame Job with + (`inputMonitoringNote(opened:)`).
426	extension RecorderPanelController {
427	    /// The doors every grant call goes through; a probe replaces it.
428	    static var grantDoors = RecorderGrantDoors.live

430	    /// A system prompt, or System Settings, is about to come up in ANOTHER
431	    /// process at normal window level, and a `.floating` panel sits over
432	    /// every normal window on the screen: the person found the Screen
433	    /// Recording prompt hidden behind the panel until they dragged it away
434	    /// (2026-09-28). So the panel steps down to `.normal` first, and
435	    /// `floatAgain` puts it back on the next press that goes on, or on
436	    /// `show()`.
437	    func stepAsideForSystemUI() { window?.level = .normal }
438	    func floatAgain() { window?.level = .floating }

440	    /// Screen Recording, for a press: true to go on; false with the note
441	    /// set, and the press ends. `screenStep` is the one decision point.
442	    func checkScreenRecordingGrant() -> Bool {
443	        floatAgain()
444	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
445	        let owned = doors.launchedByLaunchd()
446	        let step = RecordingGrant.screenStep(
447	            granted: doors.screenGranted(), asked: doors.screenAsked(), launchedByLaunchd: owned)
448	        switch step {
449	        case .proceed:
450	            return true
451	        case .ask:
452	            if owned { doors.rememberScreenAsked() }
453	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
454	            doors.requestScreen()
455	            setNote(RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal)
456	            return false
457	        case .openPane:
458	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
459	            let opened = RecordingGrant.screenRecordingPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
460	            setNote(
461	                opened ? RecordingGrant.screenRecordingOpenedNote : RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal)
462	            return false
463	        }
464	    }

469	    func checkInputMonitoringGrant() -> Bool {

471	        floatAgain()
472	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
473	        let owned = doors.launchedByLaunchd()
474	        let step = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringStep(
475	            granted: doors.inputMonitoringGranted(), asked: doors.inputMonitoringAsked(),
476	            launchedByLaunchd: owned)
477	        switch step {
478	        case .proceed:
479	            return true
480	        case .ask:
481	            if owned { doors.rememberInputMonitoringAsked() }
482	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
483	            doors.requestInputMonitoring()
484	            let opened = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
485	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))
486	            return false
487	        case .openPane:
488	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
489	            let opened = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
490	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))

499	        guard currentChoice().microphone != nil else { return true }
500	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
501	        let status = doors.microphoneStatus()
502	        switch RecordingGrant.microphoneStep(status) {
503	        case .proceed:
504	            return true
505	        case .ask:
506	            recordButton.isEnabled = false

557	                opened
558	                    ? RecordingGrant.cameraOpenedNote(status)
559	                    : RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(status))

566	    /// still on screen. The grant is READ AGAIN first — anything but
567	    /// authorized stops with the refusal, no microphone prompt and no
568	    /// countdown — then the microphone's grant, then the countdown.

580	        beginCountdown()

642	/// and corner. A menu item's tag is its index in `menuRows` (CO-66).
643	struct CameraLayoutChoice: Equatable {

649	    /// the menu's order.

651	        CameraLayoutShape.allCases.flatMap { shape in

653	                CameraLayoutChoice(kind: .corner, shape: shape, corner: $0)

671	        focus: (Double, Double)? = nil, nest: Bool? = nil
672	    ) -> ReelOp {
673	        .switchLayout(

679	/// The recorder panel's Layout rows and `record_screen`'s `camera_layout` (road map
680	/// "creator-jobs" CO8, spec §11 CO-80, CO-82): the five a camera beside the screen may land
681	/// in, each corner at the bottom right. Each raw value is the key's and the tool's spelling.
682	enum RecordingCameraLayout: String, CaseIterable {
683	    case cornerSquare = "corner_square", cornerRounded = "corner_rounded"
684	    case cornerCircle = "corner_circle", sideBySide = "side_by_side", cameraFull = "camera_full"
685	
686	    /// The pop-up's row title.
687	    var title: String {
688	        switch self {
689	        case .cornerSquare: return "Corner"
690	        case .cornerRounded: return "Rounded Corner"
691	        case .cornerCircle: return "Circle"
692	        case .sideBySide: return "Side by Side"
693	        case .cameraFull: return "Camera Full"
694	        }
695	    }
696	
697	    /// The `switch_layout` vocabulary: a corner kind with its shape at the bottom right, else
698	    /// the kind alone.
699	    var choice: CameraLayoutChoice {
700	        let corner = { (shape: CameraLayoutShape) in
701	            CameraLayoutChoice(kind: .corner, shape: shape, corner: .bottomRight)
702	        }
703	        switch self {
704	        case .cornerSquare: return corner(.square)
705	        case .cornerRounded: return corner(.rounded)
706	        case .cornerCircle: return corner(.circle)
707	        case .sideBySide: return CameraLayoutChoice(kind: .sideBySide, shape: nil, corner: nil)
708	        case .cameraFull: return CameraLayoutChoice(kind: .cameraFull, shape: nil, corner: nil)
709	        }
710	    }
711	}
712	
713	/// Who is the camera and who the screen for the menu (CO-66).
714	enum CameraLayoutRoles {
715	    /// The track a recording's camera lands on (`RecordingLanding`).
716	    static let cameraTrackName = "Camera"
717	
718	    /// Two selected picture clips on different tracks: the front one is the
719	    /// camera and the other the screen. One: it is the camera and the core
720	    /// finds the screen. None: the clip at the playhead on the front-most
721	    /// track named "Camera". nil when that yields no camera containing the
722	    /// playhead.
723	    static func roles(selected: [ClipSnapshot], playhead: Ticks, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot)
724	        -> (camera: UInt32, screen: UInt32?)?
725	    {
726	        let picture = { (clip: ClipSnapshot) in
727	            clip.video != nil && snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip) != nil
728	        }
729	        let plays = { (clip: ClipSnapshot) in clip.start <= playhead && playhead < clip.end }
730	        switch selected.count {
731	        case 2:
732	            guard selected.allSatisfy(picture),
733	                let a = snapshot.trackIndex(of: selected[0].track),
734	                let b = snapshot.trackIndex(of: selected[1].track), a != b
735	            else { return nil }
736	            let (camera, screen) = a > b ? (selected[0], selected[1]) : (selected[1], selected[0])
737	            return plays(camera) ? (camera.id, screen.id) : nil
738	        case 1:
739	            let camera = selected[0]
740	            return picture(camera) && plays(camera) ? (camera.id, nil) : nil
741	        case 0:
742	            guard let track = snapshot.tracks.last(where: { $0.name == cameraTrackName }),
743	                let camera = snapshot.clips.first(where: {
744	                    $0.track == track.id && plays($0) && picture($0)
745	                })
746	            else { return nil }
747	            return (camera.id, nil)
748	        default:
749	            return nil
750	        }
751	    }
752	}

15	/// **Before the grants, the source** (R1 review): Record with the Source row
16	/// reading "Window…" and no picked filter refuses FIRST, by name, and starts
17	/// no countdown — `currentChoice()` would otherwise quietly fall back to the
18	/// main display and record the wrong thing. The picker is NOT presented from
19	/// the guard: a refusal that puts up a system UI is not a refusal. With
20	/// "Record the camera too" ticked (spec §11 CAM-11 (5)) no camera refuses
21	/// next, and the Camera grant is checked between Screen Recording and the
22	/// microphone; with it off the Camera grant is never read.
23	///
24	/// **The start is bounded and numbered** (R1 review). `.starting` used to
25	/// have no ceiling and no exit: `ScreenRecorder.shareableContent` can hold
26	/// its answer for tens of seconds on a locked console (measured ~37 s), and
27	/// a panel waiting on it showed "Starting…" with the button disabled and no
28	/// way back. Now each press of Record is one ATTEMPT with a number
29	/// (`startGeneration`), the lookup's completion carries the number and is
30	/// ignored once it is stale, and a one-shot timer at
31	/// `ScreenRecorder.armCeiling` fails the attempt with `.startTimedOut` while
32	/// the lookup is still pending. Once `launch` has handed the attempt to the
33	/// recorder its own arm ceiling is the bound (the same sentence, from the
34	/// start completion) and the panel's timer is cancelled, so the two cannot
35	/// both fire on one attempt.
36	///
37	/// **Stop while starting** (lane C's flag, closed by reading the seam):
38	/// after `launch` the recorder is arming and `stop()` is HELD — finishing
39	/// begins the moment the start lands, and the end arrives through the
40	/// session's `onFinish` like any other; a start that FAILS instead answers
41	/// the start completion alone, `onFinish` is never called for it, and
42	/// `startFailed` is the only thing that runs. Before `launch` there is
43	/// nothing to stop: `abandonStart` bumps the generation so the pending
44	/// answer is dropped, and the panel goes idle. Without that arm a Stop while
45	/// the lookup was pending left the panel at "Stopping…" for good, because
46	/// the answer then found the phase moved on and did nothing.
47	///
48	/// **The microphone is prepared at the countdown's start** (R1 review;
49	/// `ScreenRecorder+Microphone.swift` says why — `startRunning()`'s first-use
50	/// cost, up to 0.4 s of voice missing from the file) and discarded on cancel,
51	/// on close and on a refused start, so an input never stays open past the
52	/// recording it was for. **So is a camera's capture** (spec §11 CAM-5,
53	/// `ScreenRecorder+CameraPrepare.swift`), so CAM-3's warm-up runs through the
54	/// 3-2-1, and it is let go on the same four occasions. **The meter moves
55	/// during the countdown** (#98 c): `beginCountdown` arms the tick, which
56	/// through `.countdown` and `.starting` does nothing but
57	/// `publishMicrophoneLevel()`, read from the prepared session; the discard
58	/// publishes the silence. **The tick shows a microphone problem the moment
59	/// the recorder reports one**: the picture keeps recording, the meter goes
60	/// silent, and the note says so rather than leaving a dead bar.
61	///
62	/// **Two timers run in `.common` modes** — the countdown and the 30 Hz tick
63	/// — because a status item's menu runs the run loop in event-tracking mode
64	/// while it is open, and a default-mode timer stalls there: the elapsed
65	/// label in the menu bar froze at the one moment a person was looking at
66	/// it. `RecorderStatusItem`'s doc carries the same sentence from its side.
67	extension RecorderPanelController {
68	    /// The note for Record pressed over "Window…" with nothing picked.
69	    static let chooseWindowSentence = "Choose a window with Window… first, or pick a display."
70	    /// The note for a Stop that arrived before the recording had begun.
71	    static let abandonedSentence = "Stopped before the recording began; nothing was recorded."

73	    // MARK: - Record and Stop
74	
75	    /// The Record button in every phase: start, cancel the countdown, or
76	    /// stop; a beep while the recorder is finishing or the panel is adding.
77	    @objc func record(_ sender: Any?) {
78	        switch phase {
79	        case .idle:
80	            beginIfGranted()
81	        case .countdown:
82	            cancelCountdown()
83	        case .recording, .paused, .starting:
84	            stopRecording()
85	        case .stopping, .landing:
86	            NSSound.beep()
87	        }
88	    }

90	    /// Stop, from the panel's button, the status item's menu or File ▸ Stop
91	    /// Recording. A recording the panel did not start (the `record_screen`
92	    /// tool's) is not this panel's to stop — `AppDelegate.newRecording`
93	    /// routes that one to the recorder directly — so anything but a panel
94	    /// recording beeps. Paused is stopped exactly as recording is: the
95	    /// recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with the
96	    /// segment's output already closed — and the status item is FROZEN at
97	    /// the mark it shows, because the tick goes on through `.stopping` with
98	    /// `paused` false and would bring the coral dot back over a finish that
99	    /// captures nothing (R2 review; the footnote holds its mark the same
100	    /// way, `refreshStatusLabel`). While `.starting`: launched, the stop is
101	    /// held by the recorder and lands through `onFinish`; not yet, the
102	    /// attempt is abandoned (the type doc).
103	    func stopRecording() {
104	        switch phase {
105	        case .recording, .paused:
106	            statusItem?.freeze()
107	            phase = .stopping
108	            recorder.stop()
109	        case .starting where launched:
110	            phase = .stopping
111	            recorder.stop()
112	        case .starting:
113	            abandonStart()
114	        default:
115	            NSSound.beep()
116	        }
117	    }

119	    // MARK: - The grants
120	
121	    private func beginIfGranted() {
122	        if voiceOverSelected { return beginVoiceOverIfGranted() }
123	        if cameraSelected { return beginCameraIfGranted() }
124	        if sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag == Self.windowTag, pickedFilter == nil {
125	            setNote(Self.chooseWindowSentence)
126	            return
127	        }
128	        if cameraBesideSelected, selectedCameraID == nil {
129	            setNote(CameraDevices.noCameraSentence)
130	            return
131	        }
132	        guard checkScreenRecordingGrant(), checkInputMonitoringGrant(),
133	            !cameraBesideSelected || checkCameraGrant(), checkMicrophoneGrant()
134	        else { return }
135	        setNote("")
136	        beginCountdown()
137	    }

139	    // MARK: - The countdown
140	
141	    /// 3, 2, 1 in the panel, one second each — `TimelineView.flashRefusal`'s
142	    /// shape: `[weak self]`, self-invalidating — added to the main run loop
143	    /// in `.common` modes (the type doc). The Record button reads Cancel
144	    /// meanwhile, and a click on it or closing the panel ends the countdown
145	    /// with nothing started. The microphone the choice names is prepared
146	    /// here, after the grants and before the first second has passed, so its
147	    /// start cost is paid while the numeral is still on screen — and the
148	    /// tick is armed at once, so the meter reads that session through the
149	    /// 3-2-1 (#98 c). A `resumeProblem` left by the last recording is cleared
150	    /// first, so its sentence does not carry into this one's note (#193).
151	    func beginCountdown() {
152	        countdownTimer?.invalidate()
153	        resumeProblem = nil
154	        phase = .countdown(Self.countdownSeconds)
155	        recorder.prepareCamera(for: currentChoice())
156	        recorder.prepareMicrophone(currentChoice().microphone)
157	        armTick()
158	        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
159	            guard let self, case .countdown(let remaining) = self.phase else {
160	                timer.invalidate()
161	                return
162	            }
163	            if remaining > 1 {
164	                self.phase = .countdown(remaining - 1)
165	            } else {
166	                timer.invalidate()
167	                self.countdownTimer = nil
168	                self.startRecording()
169	            }
170	        }
171	        RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)
172	        countdownTimer = timer
173	    }
174	
175	    func cancelCountdown() {
176	        countdownTimer?.invalidate()
177	        countdownTimer = nil
178	        recorder.discardPreparedMicrophone()
179	        recorder.discardPreparedCamera()
180	        if case .countdown = phase { phase = .idle }
181	    }

183	    // MARK: - Start
184	
185	    /// The choice as the controls stand, then the filter: a picked window's
186	    /// is the picker's own; a display's is built from the shareable content
187	    /// and leaves out what `recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows:)`
188	    /// names (`ScreenRecorder.filter(for:in:excluding:)`) — Frame Job's own
189	    /// application, which keeps the document windows out of a display
190	    /// recording's picture, or with Include Frame Job windows on the panel's
191	    /// window alone. One attempt, numbered and bounded (the type doc).
192	    private func startRecording() {
193	        let choice = currentChoice()
194	        let exclusion = recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows: choice.includeFrameJobWindows)
195	        startGeneration += 1
196	        let generation = startGeneration
197	        launched = false
198	        phase = .starting
199	        // A voice-over has no lookup to bound (`+VoiceOver.swift`).
200	        if choice.source == .voiceOver { return launchVoiceOver(choice) }
201	        // Nor does a camera: the recorder's own arm ceiling bounds it.
202	        if choice.source == .camera { return launchCamera(choice) }
203	        startTimer?.invalidate()
204	        startTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(
205	            withTimeInterval: ScreenRecorder.armCeiling, repeats: false
206	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.armTimedOut(generation: generation) }
207	        if choice.source == .picked, let filter = pickedFilter {
208	            launch(filter: filter, choice: choice)
209	            return
210	        }
211	        ScreenRecorder.shareableContent { [weak self] outcome in
212	            guard let self, self.phase == .starting, generation == self.startGeneration else {
213	                return
214	            }
215	            switch outcome {
216	            case .failure(let error):
217	                self.startFailed(error)
218	            case .success(let content):
219	                do {
220	                    let filter = try ScreenRecorder.filter(
221	                        for: choice.source, in: content, excluding: exclusion)
222	                    self.launch(filter: filter, choice: choice)
223	                } catch {
224	                    self.startFailed(error)
225	                }
226	            }
227	        }
228	    }

230	    /// The arm ceiling, for the lookup half of an attempt: a stale number, a
231	    /// phase that moved on, or an attempt the recorder already holds (its
232	    /// own ceiling reports that one) does nothing. Internal so a probe can
233	    /// fire it without a lookup.
234	    func armTimedOut(generation: Int) {
235	        guard phase == .starting, generation == startGeneration, !launched else { return }
236	        startFailed(RecorderError.startTimedOut)
237	    }
238	
239	    /// A Stop before the recorder was handed the attempt: the pending
240	    /// lookup's answer is orphaned by the generation bump, the prepared
241	    /// microphone let go, and the panel idle with a note saying nothing was
242	    /// recorded.
243	    private func abandonStart() {
244	        startGeneration += 1
245	        startTimer?.invalidate()
246	        startTimer = nil
247	        recorder.discardPreparedMicrophone()
248	        recorder.discardPreparedCamera()
249	        phase = .idle
250	        setNote(Self.abandonedSentence)
251	    }
252	
253	    private func launch(filter: SCContentFilter, choice: RecordingChoice) {
254	        // From here the recorder's arm ceiling is the bound.
255	        startTimer?.invalidate()
256	        startTimer = nil
257	        launched = true
258	        recorder.start(
259	            filter: filter, choice: choice, mayAsk: true,
260	            onFinish: { [weak self] outcome in self?.recordingEnded(outcome) }
261	        ) { [weak self] error in
262	            guard let self else { return }
263	            if let error {
264	                self.startFailed(error)
265	                return
266	            }
267	            self.recordingDidStart()
268	        }
269	    }
270	
271	    /// A refused, failed or timed-out start: idle, the note, and the
272	    /// microphone the countdown prepared let go.
273	    func startFailed(_ error: any Error) {
274	        startTimer?.invalidate()
275	        startTimer = nil
276	        launched = false
277	        recorder.discardPreparedMicrophone()
278	        recorder.discardPreparedCamera()
279	        phase = .idle
280	        setNote(error.localizedDescription)
281	    }

283	    /// The recording chrome (decision 7): the status item in the menu bar
284	    /// with Pause, Resume and Stop (`+Pause.swift` for the first two), the
285	    /// 30 Hz tick, and the panel ordered OUT for EVERY source until the
286	    /// landing has something to say — whether or not it was on screen
287	    /// (`show()` beeps meanwhile; `showWhenLanded` remembers, and
288	    /// `revealIfNoted` reads it). R1 hid it for a picked window only,
289	    /// because a display's filter excludes Frame Job (R0 q3); the user asked
290	    /// for the dialog to go away whatever is recorded, and the menu bar's
291	    /// item is the recording's controls now. A voice-over and a camera are
292	    /// the exceptions (`hidesForRecording`): the panel stays as it was, so it is never
293	    /// `hiddenForRecording` and `showWhenLanded` is simply whether it is up.
294	    func recordingDidStart() {
295	        // A stop asked for while arming has moved the phase on; the end
296	        // comes through `recordingEnded`.
297	        guard phase == .starting else { return }
298	        phase = .recording
299	        resumeProblem = nil
300	        setNote("")
301	        let item = RecorderStatusItem(
302	            keys: recorder.recordsKeys,
303	            onPause: { [weak self] in self?.pauseRecording() },
304	            onResume: { [weak self] in self?.resumeRecording() },
305	            onStop: { [weak self] in self?.stopRecording() })
306	        item.show()
307	        statusItem = item
308	        armTick()
309	        showWhenLanded = window?.isVisible == true
310	        guard Self.hidesForRecording(currentChoice().source) else { return }
311	        hiddenForRecording = true
312	        window?.orderOut(nil)
313	    }

315	    // MARK: - The tick
316	
317	    /// 30 Hz from the countdown's start, in `.common` modes (the type doc).
318	    /// Through `.countdown` and `.starting` it ONLY meters — the prepared
319	    /// session's level (#98 c; the recorder publishes nothing while
320	    /// arming, so the bar holds its last pre-roll level for that instant).
321	    /// While recording or paused: the microphone's level into the panel's
322	    /// own meter (`ScreenRecorder.publishMicrophoneLevel`, a no-op without
323	    /// a microphone and while paused, the recorder having silenced the
324	    /// bar), the elapsed time in the footnote and in the status item — with
325	    /// `paused`, which is what flips the item's menu — and a microphone
326	    /// problem into the note. `recordingDidStart` re-arms it.
327	    private func armTick() {
328	        tickTimer?.invalidate()
329	        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: 1.0 / 30, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
330	            guard let self else {
331	                timer.invalidate()
332	                return
333	            }
334	            switch self.phase {
335	            case .countdown, .starting:
336	                self.recorder.publishMicrophoneLevel()
337	                return
338	            default:
339	                break
340	            }
341	            guard self.phase == .recording || self.phase == .paused || self.phase == .stopping
342	            else {
343	                timer.invalidate()
344	                return
345	            }
346	            self.recorder.publishMicrophoneLevel()
347	            self.refreshStatusLabel()
348	            self.statusItem?.update(elapsed: self.recorder.elapsed, paused: self.phase == .paused)
349	            self.syncMicrophoneNote()
350	        }
351	        RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)
352	        tickTimer = timer
353	    }
354	
355	    /// The live note — what the panel says while a recording runs or is
356	    /// paused — rebuilt at every tick from its two PARTS and never from the
357	    /// label's text: `ScreenRecorder.microphoneProblem` the moment it is
358	    /// non-nil (a device unplugged, a writer that gave up), and
359	    /// `resumeProblem`, a resume the recorder refused (`+Pause.swift`,
360	    /// whose `liveNote` is the composition). Composing from the label was
361	    /// the R2 review's defect: a microphone did-finish landing late
362	    /// replaced a note that did not yet contain its sentence and wiped the
363	    /// resume's, and each retried resume appended its sentence again. Set
364	    /// only on a change, because `setNote` refits the window and this runs
365	    /// at 30 Hz.
366	    func syncMicrophoneNote() {
367	        let text = Self.liveNote(
368	            microphoneProblem: recorder.microphoneProblem, resumeProblem: resumeProblem)
369	        if noteLabel.stringValue != text { setNote(text) }
370	    }
371	
372	    func disarmTick() {
373	        tickTimer?.invalidate()
374	        tickTimer = nil
375	    }
376	}

3	/// Pause and resume from the panel's side, the one door into a hidden
4	/// recording's controls, and the phases drawn (road map 3, R2c) —
5	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s sixth file, NEW rather than cut for its
6	/// first two members: they are the whole of what the panel adds for a pause,
7	/// and `+Recording.swift` and the base file were both within a dozen lines
8	/// of the 400-line cap when R2 began. `syncPhase` and `refreshStatusLabel`
9	/// then MOVED here from the base file when the R2 review's fixes took it
10	/// over the cap — the base file's toll, paid along the line the footnote
11	/// draws: its `.paused` and `.stopping` arms are what the pause added, and
12	/// `syncPhase` is its one caller besides the tick.
13	///
14	/// **Neither pause member is reachable from the panel's own controls** but
15	/// in a voice-over, whose panel stays up with a Pause / Resume button
16	/// (`+VoiceOver.swift`). The panel is off screen for every other recording
17	/// (decision 7), so Pause Recording
18	/// and Resume Recording are rows of the status item's menu, which calls
19	/// these through the closures `recordingDidStart` hands it, and File ▸
20	/// Pause/Resume Recording (`AppDelegate+Recording.swift`), the second door,
21	/// which calls them for the panel's own recording (#98). The panel's
22	/// phase — `.recording ⇄ .paused` — follows the recorder's own `pause()` /
23	/// `resume()` (`ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift`), which are synchronous and
24	/// throw. The phase moves only AFTER the call returns
25	/// without throwing, so the panel never claims a state the recorder
26	/// refused: a pause that could not close the segment's file leaves the
27	/// recorder `.recording` and the panel with it, and a resume whose output
28	/// could not be added leaves both `.paused`.
29	///
30	/// **The two refusals are answered differently, on purpose.** A refused
31	/// pause BEEPS: the recorder is still recording, nothing was lost, and the
32	/// panel is hidden, so a note there would be read by nobody until the
33	/// landing, by which time it would be stale. A refused resume keeps the
34	/// recorder's sentence as `resumeProblem` and stays paused: the stream still
35	/// captures but no file is taking it, so what the person does next — try
36	/// again, or stop and land what was recorded — depends on the sentence, and
37	/// the landing's reveal (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`) brings the
38	/// panel back with that sentence in its note when they stop. The sentence
39	/// is STATE and never text read back off the label (R2 review): the live
40	/// note is rebuilt from `[microphoneProblem, resumeProblem]` at every tick
41	/// (`syncMicrophoneNote`, over `liveNote` below), so a microphone
42	/// did-finish landing late cannot wipe it and a retried resume replaces it
43	/// rather than appending a second copy; and `landingNote` takes it as an
44	/// argument, so the landing's note carries it where the first shape — each
45	/// end replacing the label whole — dropped it, and the reveal showed
46	/// nothing. A resume that LANDS clears it: a sentence about a refusal the
47	/// person has since got past would bring the panel back with nothing true
48	/// to say.
49	///
50	/// A Stop while paused (`stopRecording`, `record(_:)`, File ▸ Stop
51	/// Recording) goes to `recorder.stop()` exactly as one while recording
52	/// does — the recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with
53	/// the segment's output already closed — and the status item comes down at
54	/// `recordingEnded` as ever. The tick runs through `.paused` (`armTick`):
55	/// the meter poll is a no-op there, the recorder having silenced the bar at
56	/// the pause, and `elapsed` is frozen, so the footnote and the item hold
57	/// still on their own.
58	extension RecorderPanelController {
59	    // MARK: - Pause and resume
60	
61	    /// The status item's Pause Recording, and File ▸ Pause Recording's for
62	    /// the panel's own recording. `.recording` → `.paused`; any
63	    /// other phase beeps — the row was clicked in the moment between a Stop
64	    /// and the item coming down — and so does any throw, `.alreadyPaused`
65	    /// among them (the header).
66	    func pauseRecording() {
67	        guard phase == .recording else {
68	            NSSound.beep()
69	            return
70	        }
71	        do {
72	            try recorder.pause()
73	            phase = .paused
74	        } catch {
75	            NSSound.beep()
76	        }
77	    }

79	    /// The status item's Resume Recording, and File ▸ Resume Recording's.
80	    /// `.paused` → `.recording`, with
81	    /// the refused-resume sentence cleared; any other phase beeps. A throw
82	    /// leaves the phase paused and keeps the recorder's sentence as
83	    /// `resumeProblem`, REPLACING an earlier one, redrawn into the note at
84	    /// once rather than at the tick's next turn (the header).
85	    func resumeRecording() {
86	        guard phase == .paused else {
87	            NSSound.beep()
88	            return
89	        }
90	        do {
91	            try recorder.resume()
92	            resumeProblem = nil
93	            phase = .recording
94	        } catch {
95	            resumeProblem = error.localizedDescription

98	    }

101	    /// the fact that the picture is still recording (a silent meter alone

103	    /// neither. Pure, so a probe can pin the composition without a recorder.
104	    static func liveNote(microphoneProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String?) -> String {

106	        if let microphoneProblem {
107	            sentences.append(

170	    /// The footnote: the folder while idle, the coral dot and the elapsed
171	    /// time while recording, the pause glyph and the frozen time while
172	    /// paused — faint, because the dot's colour means "capturing" — and
173	    /// through `.stopping` whichever of those two it last showed, left
174	    /// UNTOUCHED (R2 review): the phase no longer says whether the Stop

177	    /// finish that captures nothing. The status item keeps its mark the
178	    /// same way (`RecorderStatusItem.freeze`, called by `stopRecording`).
179	    func refreshStatusLabel() {
180	        switch phase {
181	        case .recording:
182	            statusLabel.stringValue = "● " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)

3	/// The recorder panel from the recording's END to the note that says where
4	/// it went (road map 3, R1c) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s fourth
5	/// file, cut out of `+Recording.swift` along the line `recordingEnded`
6	/// draws when the R1 review's fixes took that file past the 400-line cap:
7	/// everything before the session's `onFinish` fires stays there, everything
8	/// after it is here.
9	///
10	/// **One door for a finished recording.** The session's `onFinish` — called
11	/// exactly once whoever ended the recording: the panel's Stop, the status
12	/// item's, the system indicator's, a display that slept, a failure — arrives
13	/// at `recordingEnded`, which tears the recording chrome down (the tick, the
14	/// status item, and the `hiddenForRecording` flag that made `show()` beep —
15	/// clearing it, and showing NOTHING) and then lands. A DOCUMENT target
16	/// commits the placement through the document's
17	/// own door (`performGroupedEdit`, then `generateCaches`, the selection, and
18	/// the editor told through `viewStateDidChange`); a NEW PROJECT is
19	/// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, which does everything. A document
20	/// mid-drag is not committed over the gesture's base handle: the landing is
21	/// retried from a half-second timer until the drag ends, bounded at forty
22	/// tries — **20 s, kept** (lane C's flag, closed by reading): a landing that
23	/// waited for ever would hold the file's note back for ever, and the note
24	/// after the bound names the file, which is on disk either way — and on
25	/// either failure the note names the FILE, which is on disk whatever went
26	/// wrong after it. That timer stays in the DEFAULT run-loop mode on
27	/// purpose, unlike the countdown and the tick: a drag runs the loop in
28	/// tracking mode, so the retry fires when the drag ENDS, which is the
29	/// moment it is for.
30	///
31	/// **The commit is checked by its handle** (R1 review). `performGroupedEdit`
32	/// answers nothing: a refusal beeps or puts up the core's sentence on the
33	/// document's window and returns, and the panel — which cannot see either
34	/// — used to report "added" over a project with nothing in it. The
35	/// document's `project` handle changes ONLY on success (`applyEdit`'s three
36	/// outcomes), so `land` reads it before the commit and compares after, and
37	/// an unchanged handle is a failed landing with the file's path in the
38	/// note. The trial in `RecordingLanding.placement` sees everything the
39	/// commit will, so the arm is reached only by a race the trial cannot see —
40	/// an edit landing between the two on the same run-loop turn — and it is
41	/// there because the alternative is a note that lies.
42	///
43	/// **The note says six things, in order**, through `landingNote`, a pure
44	/// function so a probe can pin every combination without a landing: how the
45	/// recording ended when it was not this panel's own Stop (`.stopped` is the
46	/// status item's Stop too; `.userStopped` is the SYSTEM's indicator, and the
47	/// sentence names it so, now that Frame Job's own item is a menu-bar item as
48	/// well); that the document the person CHOSE had closed, when the choice
49	/// was a document and the landing opened a new project (R1 review — the
50	/// fallback is exact, and a person who chose "Untitled 2" should not have
51	/// to work out why a new window appeared instead); the segments left out
52	/// because their movie would not probe (`unreadableNote`, #97), each naming
53	/// the files it kept; the microphone's
54	/// problem, when the recording is a `.success` whose `micProblem` is set —
55	/// a success, not an error, so the picture lands first and the sentence
56	/// follows it; a resume the recorder refused (`resumeProblem`, STATE on the
57	/// panel and never text read back off the label — the R2 review's defect:
58	/// each end replaced the label whole, so after a refused resume and a clean
59	/// Stop the note was empty and the reveal showed nothing, the opposite of
60	/// what `+Pause.swift` promised); and the placement's own notes, one per
61	/// file the landing could not place. `failedToLand` names every file
62	/// through `filesClause` and carries the unreadable segments', the
63	/// microphone's and the resume's sentences too.
64	///
65	/// **The panel comes back ONLY with something to say** (decision 7, R2c).
66	/// It ordered out at `recordingDidStart` whatever the source, and each of
67	/// the three ends — `landed`, `failedToLand`, the failure arm of
68	/// `recordingEnded` — finishes with `revealIfNoted()`, AFTER its note is
69	/// set: the panel is ordered front when it was on screen as the recording
70	/// began (`showWhenLanded`) and the note is non-empty, and `showWhenLanded`
71	/// is cleared either way. A clean recording lands in its document or opens
72	/// its project and the panel stays away; ⌥⌘N shows it again. The reveal
73	/// belongs to the END and not to `recordingEnded`, because the deferred
74	/// landing's retries can put twenty seconds between the two, and a panel
75	/// shown with "Adding…" and no note yet is the dialog the user asked to be
76	/// rid of.
77	extension RecorderPanelController {
78	    static let landingRetryInterval: TimeInterval = 0.5
79	    static let landingRetryLimit = 40
80	    static let destinationClosedSentence =
81	        "The document you chose was closed, so the recording opened as a new project."
82	
83	    // MARK: - The end, and the landing
84	
85	    func recordingEnded(_ outcome: Result<RecordingResult, Error>) {
86	        disarmTick()
87	        statusItem?.remove()
88	        statusItem = nil
89	        launched = false
90	        hiddenForRecording = false
91	        switch outcome {
92	        case .failure(let error):
93	            phase = .idle
94	            setNote(
95	                [error.localizedDescription, resumeProblem].compactMap { $0 }
96	                    .joined(separator: " "))
97	            revealIfNoted()
98	        case .success(let result):
99	            phase = .landing
100	            landingAttempts = 0
101	            land(result)
102	        }
103	    }
104	
105	    func land(_ result: RecordingResult) {
106	        switch RecordingLanding.resolve(result.choice.destination) {
107	        case .document(let document):
108	            guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
109	                deferLanding(result)
110	                return
111	            }
112	            do {
113	                let placement = try RecordingLanding.placement(result, in: document, place: true)
114	                let before = document.project
115	                document.performGroupedEdit(RecordingLanding.actionName, placement.ops)
116	                // The handle changes only on success (the type doc).
117	                guard document.project !== before else {
118	                    failedToLand(
119	                        result,
120	                        ReelCoreError(
121	                            message: "the project refused the placement and nothing was added"))
122	                    return
123	                }
124	                document.generateCaches()
125	                // Every segment's clip, microphone clips included (R2b); a
126	                // segment that minted none is a nil entry, and its sentence
127	                // is in `placement.notes`.
128	                document.selection = Set(
129	                    (placement.clipIds + placement.micClipIds + placement.leftOutMicClipIds
130	                        + placement.cameraClipIds)
131	                        .compactMap { $0 })
132	                Self.editor(of: document)?.viewStateDidChange()
133	                landed(result, asNewProject: false, notes: placement.notes)
134	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: document)  // CO-81: its own step, first
135	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: document)  // AU-68: after the commit
136	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: document)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
137	            } catch {
138	                failedToLand(result, error)
139	            }
140	        case .newProject:
141	            do {
142	                let (opened, notes) = try ProjectDocument.untitled(around: result)
143	                landed(result, asNewProject: true, notes: notes)
144	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: opened)  // CO-81: its own step, first
145	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: opened)  // AU-68: after the commit
146	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: opened)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
147	            } catch {
148	                failedToLand(result, error)
149	            }
150	        }
151	    }
152	
153	    /// A drag is in progress: try again when it has had half a second to
154	    /// end, up to the limit — a landing over the gesture's base handle would
155	    /// be undone by the gesture's own end.
156	    private func deferLanding(_ result: RecordingResult) {
157	        landingAttempts += 1
158	        guard landingAttempts <= Self.landingRetryLimit else {
159	            let waited = Int(Double(Self.landingRetryLimit) * Self.landingRetryInterval)
160	            failedToLand(
161	                result,
162	                ReelCoreError(message: "A drag was still in progress after \(waited) s."))
163	            return
164	        }
165	        landingTimer?.invalidate()
166	        landingTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(
167	            withTimeInterval: Self.landingRetryInterval, repeats: false
168	        ) { [weak self] _ in
169	            self?.landingTimer = nil
170	            self?.land(result)
171	        }
172	    }
173	
174	    /// Back to idle; the note is `landingNote`'s, over the placement's own
175	    /// notes — the unreadable segments' sentences followed by what became of
176	    /// their readable voices (#181 item 2), said only here, on a landing
177	    /// that succeeded — led by every segment's camera sentences beside the
178	    /// screen (`cameraSegmentsNote`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) — and the reveal
179	    /// last.
180	    private func landed(_ result: RecordingResult, asNewProject: Bool, notes placed: [String]) {
181	        phase = .idle
182	        rebuildDestinations()
183	        // Then every segment's cursor problem (spec §11 CU-18).
184	        let notes = [result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote].compactMap { $0 } + placed
185	        let leftOut = [result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote].compactMap { $0 }
186	        setNote(
187	            Self.landingNote(
188	                stoppedBy: result.stoppedBy, chosen: result.choice.destination,
189	                landedAsNewProject: asNewProject, micProblem: result.micProblem,
190	                resumeProblem: resumeProblem, notes: notes,
191	                unreadable: leftOut.isEmpty ? nil : leftOut.joined(separator: " "),
192	                camera: result.camera, cameraBeside: result.camera != nil && !result.isCamera))
193	        revealIfNoted()
194	    }
195	
196	    /// The files are on disk whatever went wrong after them, so the note
197	    /// names every one (`filesClause`: each segment's movie, and the
198	    /// microphone files that landed) — then what became of an unreadable
199	    /// segment, the microphone, the camera (its `problem` and warm-up `note`,
200	    /// spec §11 CAM-5, then each segment's camera sentences beside the
201	    /// screen, CAM-10 (8)) and a refused resume, when the result or the panel
202	    /// carries those sentences — and the reveal last.
203	    private func failedToLand(_ result: RecordingResult, _ error: any Error) {
204	        phase = .idle
205	        var note =
206	            "The recording was saved at \(result.filesClause) but could not be added: "
207	            + error.localizedDescription
208	        for sentence in [
209	            result.unreadableNote, result.micProblem, result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
210	            result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote, resumeProblem,
211	        ].compactMap({ $0 })
212	        {
213	            note += " " + sentence
214	        }
215	        setNote(note)
216	        revealIfNoted()
217	    }
218	
219	    /// The panel back on screen after a landing, ONLY when it was on screen
220	    /// as the recording began and the note has something in it (the type
221	    /// doc). Called LAST by each of the three ends, after the note is set —
222	    /// which is the whole point — and reached after the deferred landing's
223	    /// retries as well, since nothing before it clears `showWhenLanded`.
224	    /// Cleared either way, so a later `show()` of the person's own is not
225	    /// mistaken for this one. Internal so a probe can drive both ways.
226	    func revealIfNoted() {
227	        if showWhenLanded, !noteLabel.stringValue.isEmpty { window?.orderFront(nil) }
228	        showWhenLanded = false
229	    }
230	
231	    /// The landing's note (the type doc): the stop's sentence unless the
232	    /// stop was this panel's own; the closed-document sentence when a chosen
233	    /// document was gone by the time the recording ended; the unreadable
234	    /// segments' sentences; the microphone's problem; a refused resume's
235	    /// sentence; then the placement's notes. Empty for the ordinary case, so
236	    /// `setNote` hides the label. The R2 arguments, #97's `unreadable` and
237	    /// CR1c's `camera` are LAST and default, so the probe's R1 rows read as
238	    /// they did. A CAMERA result (spec §11 CAM-5) says its own stop — the
239	    /// camera's `problem`, else that it stopped on its own — in place of the
240	    /// display's, and its warm-up `note` follows the microphone's problem.
241	    /// A camera BESIDE the screen (`cameraBeside`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) is
242	    /// not the recording's stop: the display's sentence stays, and the
243	    /// camera's `problem` follows the microphone's problem, before its note.
244	    static func landingNote(
245	        stoppedBy: StopReason, chosen: RecordingDestination, landedAsNewProject: Bool,
246	        micProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String? = nil, notes: [String] = [],
247	        unreadable: String? = nil, camera: RecordingCamera? = nil, cameraBeside: Bool = false
248	    ) -> String {
249	        var sentences: [String] = []
250	        switch stoppedBy {
251	        case .stopped:
252	            break
253	        case .userStopped:
254	            sentences.append(
255	                "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added.")
256	        case .systemStopped:
257	            if let camera, !cameraBeside {
258	                sentences.append(
259	                    (camera.problem ?? "The camera stopped on its own.")
260	                        + " What was captured was added.")
261	            } else {
262	                sentences.append(
263	                    "The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); "
264	                        + "what was captured was added.")
265	            }
266	        }
267	        if case .document = chosen, landedAsNewProject {
268	            sentences.append(destinationClosedSentence)
269	        }
270	        if let unreadable { sentences.append(unreadable) }
271	        if let micProblem { sentences.append(micProblem) }
272	        if cameraBeside, let problem = camera?.problem { sentences.append(problem) }
273	        if let note = camera?.note { sentences.append(note) }
274	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
275	        sentences.append(contentsOf: notes)
276	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
277	    }
278	
279	    /// `AgentServer.editor(_:)`'s lookup; nil for a windowless document.
280	    static func editor(of document: ProjectDocument) -> EditorViewController? {
281	        document.windowControllers
282	            .compactMap { $0.contentViewController as? EditorViewController }
283	            .first
284	    }
285	}

4	/// One popup row as a hot-plug compares it: the id it carries (nil for
5	/// "None connected" and "Off") and its title.
6	struct HotPlugRow: Equatable {
7	    let id: String?
8	    let title: String
9	}
10	
11	/// Hot-plug (camera-recording CR2c, spec §11 CAM-8) —
12	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s twelfth file, NEW rather than cut, as
13	/// `+Camera.swift` and `+CameraPreview.swift` were: the device observers,
14	/// the pending mark, the rebuild it applies, the selection rule and the
15	/// microphone list.
16	///
17	/// **The observers** are `AVCaptureDevice`'s connected and disconnected
18	/// notifications for any device, on main. `show()` adds the pair (one at
19	/// most) and adding it marks the lists pending, so a change made while the
20	/// panel was closed is caught up; `panelWillClose` removes them. A panel
21	/// ordered out for a recording keeps them.
22	///
23	/// **Pending until idle.** A notification marks the lists pending and steps
24	/// the preview (`syncCameraPreview`), whose FIRST act is
25	/// `applyPendingDevices`: it applies only while the panel's phase and the
26	/// recorder are both idle, so a change during a countdown, a recording or a
27	/// landing waits for the first step that finds both idle — the return to
28	/// idle draws the phase, which steps. It never steps the preview itself (no
29	/// recursion) and never persists.
30	///
31	/// **The rebuild** compares each popup's rows (id, title) with the devices
32	/// connected now and rebuilds only a popup that differs, so a menu the
33	/// person has open is not rebuilt for an unrelated device. The selection is
34	/// `hotPlugSelection` over the id held BEFORE the rebuild; the camera is
35	/// selected again — which rebuilds the Format popup, the stored format else
36	/// Best (CAM-6 (2)) — only when its popup was rebuilt or the id changed.
37	/// **No key is written**, so a camera that goes and comes back is selected
38	/// again with its stored format; the next control change writes what the
39	/// popups then show (CAM-5 (2)).
40	extension RecorderPanelController {
41	
42	    /// CAM-8 (3): `stored` when `listed` holds it, else `current` when
43	    /// listed, else nil (the default). `""` counts as nil for both.
44	    static func hotPlugSelection(listed: [String], stored: String?, current: String?) -> String? {
45	        let stored = stored.flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 }
46	        let current = current.flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 }
47	        if let stored, listed.contains(stored) { return stored }
48	        if let current, listed.contains(current) { return current }
49	        return nil
50	    }
51	
52	    /// The microphones connected now: the discovery session
53	    /// `ScreenRecorder.microphone(withID:)` asks, keeping only those whose
54	    /// `isConnected` is true (CAM-8 (5)).
55	    static func connectedMicrophones() -> [AVCaptureDevice] {
56	        AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession(
57	            deviceTypes: [.microphone, .external], mediaType: .audio, position: .unspecified
58	        ).devices.filter(\.isConnected)
59	    }
60	
61	    /// `popup`'s rows as a hot-plug compares them.
62	    static func hotPlugRows(of popup: NSPopUpButton) -> [HotPlugRow] {
63	        popup.itemArray.map { HotPlugRow(id: $0.representedObject as? String, title: $0.title) }
64	    }
65	
66	    // MARK: - The observers
67	
68	    /// Idempotent: one pair at most. Adding the pair marks the lists
69	    /// pending, so the sync that follows catches up a change made while the
70	    /// panel was closed.
71	    func observeDevices() {
72	        guard deviceObservers.isEmpty else { return }
73	        let center = NotificationCenter.default
74	        let names = [AVCaptureDevice.wasConnectedNotification, AVCaptureDevice.wasDisconnectedNotification]
75	        for name in names {
76	            let observer = center.addObserver(forName: name, object: nil, queue: .main) {
77	                [weak self] _ in
78	                self?.devicesDidChange()
79	            }
80	            deviceObservers.append(observer)
81	        }
82	        devicesPending = true
83	    }
84	
85	    /// Removes both observers.
86	    func stopObservingDevices() {
87	        deviceObservers.forEach(NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver)
88	        deviceObservers = []
89	    }

3	/// The panel SHOWN: `show()`, the one-second timer that keeps the Record Into
4	/// rows current while it is up, `setNote` and the refit that keeps the card on
5	/// its screen — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s ninth file. A pure move out
6	/// of the base file, which stood at 399 lines against the 400-line cap a
7	/// Camera source would have grown: camera recording's CR1-0, paid first and
8	/// alone. Its `// MARK: - Showing` came here whole, bodies untouched;
9	/// `armSyncTimer` stays private, since its one caller, `show()`, moved with it.
10	extension RecorderPanelController {
11	
12	    // MARK: - Showing
13	
14	    /// Beeps and shows nothing while a recording has the panel hidden (the
15	    /// type doc): the welcome window's button is the caller that would
16	    /// otherwise un-hide it into the recording. Shown while idle, a prepared
17	    /// capture that failed (or a build that threw) is let go first, so the
18	    /// preview's sync tries again (spec §11 CAM-7 (5)). The device observers
19	    /// are added before that sync, which applies a change made while the
20	    /// panel was closed (CAM-8 (1)).
21	    func show() {
22	        guard !hiddenForRecording else {
23	            NSSound.beep()
24	            return
25	        }
26	        panelClosing = false
27	        if phase == .idle {
28	            rebuildSources()
29	            rebuildMicrophones()
30	            rebuildCameras()
31	            restoreChoices()
32	            if recorder.state == .idle, previewFailure != nil { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
33	        }
34	        rebuildDestinations()
35	        refreshSizeNote()
36	        fitWindowToContent()
37	        floatAgain()
38	        if NSApp.isActive {
39	            showWindow(nil)
40	            window?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
41	        } else {
42	            window?.orderFrontRegardless()
43	        }
44	        armSyncTimer()
45	        observeDevices()
46	        syncCameraPreview()
47	    }
48	
49	    /// One second, while the panel is up: the Record Into rows follow the
50	    /// documents that open and close and the one in front — while idle,
51	    /// which `rebuildDestinations` itself decides — and the camera preview
52	    /// steps again (CAM-7 (5)).
53	    private func armSyncTimer() {
54	        guard syncTimer == nil else { return }
55	        syncTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
56	            guard let self else {
57	                timer.invalidate()
58	                return
59	            }
60	            guard self.window?.isVisible == true else { return }
61	            self.rebuildDestinations()
62	            self.syncCameraPreview()
63	        }
64	    }
65	
66	    // `syncPhase()` and `refreshStatusLabel()` — the phases drawn — are
67	    // `+Pause.swift`'s since the R2 review, the base file's toll.
68	
69	    func setNote(_ text: String) {
70	        noteLabel.stringValue = text
71	        noteLabel.isHidden = text.isEmpty
72	        fitWindowToContent()
73	    }
74	
75	    /// The window takes the card's fitting size, keeping its TOP-LEFT where
76	    /// it was — `setContentSize` would keep the bottom-left and walk the
77	    /// title bar up the screen every time the note appeared — and then
78	    /// CONSTRAINED to its screen (`window.screen`, else the main one), so a
79	    /// panel whose bottom edge sits near the Dock is pushed up when the
80	    /// countdown grows it rather than growing under the Dock (R1 review;
81	    /// measured, the numeral adds 88 pt below the rows and a note 42 more).
82	    /// `setFrame` itself constrains nothing — a window can be put anywhere
83	    /// programmatically, on screen or off — which is why the call is
84	    /// explicit.
85	    func fitWindowToContent() {
86	        guard let window else { return }
87	        card.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
88	        let content = NSRect(origin: .zero, size: card.fittingSize)
89	        var frame = window.frameRect(forContentRect: content)
90	        let current = window.frame
91	        frame.origin = NSPoint(x: current.minX, y: current.maxY - frame.height)
92	        let screen = window.screen ?? NSScreen.main ?? NSScreen.screens.first
93	        frame = window.constrainFrameRect(frame, to: screen)
94	        window.setFrame(frame, display: window.isVisible)
95	    }
96	}
