15	/// It is created when a recording starts and removed the moment the
16	/// recording ENDS — before the landing, not after it: once the recorder is
17	/// finishing there is nothing left for it to do. The label is pushed by its
18	/// owner's timer (`update(elapsed:paused:)` — the panel's at 30 Hz, the
19	/// tool's at 1 Hz), so this class keeps no timer and no recorder; it holds
20	/// three closures, `AudioNormalize`'s value-in-value-out posture applied to
21	/// a control, so a probe can make one without the panel. It never asks
22	/// whether a pause SUCCEEDED: the owner's next `update` says, by `paused`,
23	/// and that is the one place the menu is decided.
24	///
25	/// **The menu is rebuilt only when `paused` FLIPS, never per tick**, and
26	/// the rows are replaced inside the one `NSMenu` the item was shown with
27	/// rather than the menu swapped. A status item's menu may be OPEN when a
28	/// tick fires — the tracking run loop delivers the timer (below) — and a
29	/// title change under an open menu is harmless where rebuilding its rows
30	/// thirty times a second is not; the flip itself cannot arrive under the
31	/// open menu from the menu's own row, because a click closes the menu
32	/// before its action runs. `menuTitles(paused:)` and
33	/// `title(elapsed:paused:)` are PURE, which is how a probe pins both menus
34	/// and both labels without a menu bar.
35	///
36	/// **`freeze()` pins the mark from the owner's Stop on** (R2 review). The
37	/// owner's tick goes on calling `update` through its stopping phase, with
38	/// `paused` read off a phase that is `.stopping` and no longer `.paused`,
39	/// so a Stop from paused used to bring the coral dot back for the second or
40	/// two the finish takes — a recording that was not capturing, shown as
41	/// capturing. Frozen, `update` keeps the mark and the menu it last showed
42	/// and moves only the time; the panel calls it in `stopRecording()`, the
43	/// tool's chrome at its Stop. And `openMenu()` is a click on the button —
44	/// it pops the menu exactly as a person's click would — for the quit guard
45	/// while the panel is hidden (`RecorderPanelController.revealControls`), so
46	/// a person who paused and forgot is shown Pause, Resume and Stop rather
47	/// than beeped at.
48	///
49	/// **That timer runs in `.common` run-loop modes, and this item is why**
50	/// (R1 review). Opening a status item's menu runs the main run loop in
51	/// event-tracking mode for as long as the menu is down, and a timer
52	/// scheduled in the default mode alone does not fire there — so the elapsed
53	/// label froze at the moment its menu opened, which is the one moment a
54	/// person is looking at it to decide whether to press Stop. The panel adds
55	/// its tick (and its countdown, for the same reason) with
56	/// `RunLoop.main.add(_:forMode: .common)`, and `update(elapsed:paused:)` is
57	/// then called under the open menu as it is at any other time.
58	///
59	/// **One fixed length** (#98). The item is sized ONCE, `itemLength`: the
60	/// widest title either mark makes at `widestElapsed` (9:59:59) plus
61	/// `titleInset` each side, so the menu bar's other items never shift as the
62	/// seconds tick, the hour appears or the mark flips between the dot and
63	/// the pause glyph. A label past 9:59:59 is wider than that; it is not
64	/// sized for.
65	///
66	/// The fonts are the SYSTEM's, not `DS`'s: the menu bar is the OS's chrome
67	/// and a vendored face there would read as a foreign object. Monospaced
68	/// digits so the label does not jitter as the seconds tick. The pause
69	/// glyph takes NO colour of its own — the coral dot means "capturing", and
70	/// a paused recording is not — so it is drawn in whatever the menu bar
71	/// draws its text in, light or dark.
72	///
73	/// **While shortcuts record** (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-61; the
74	/// owner: a keyboard mark plus a menu row) — `keys`, from the recorder's
75	/// `recordsKeys` at construction — the title carries `keysGlyph` after the
76	/// dot or the pause glyph, in the menu bar's own colour, and the menu's first
77	/// row is a disabled `keysRow` and a separator, paused or not. The length is
78	/// fixed per item for the marks it shows (`itemLength(keys:)`), so an item
79	/// without shortcuts keeps the one length, title and menu it always had.
80	final class RecorderStatusItem: NSObject {
81	    /// Two heavy vertical bars (U+275A). The panel's footnote spells a pause
82	    /// with the same glyph, from here, so the two never drift apart.
83	    static let pauseGlyph = "❚❚"
84	    /// The keyboard (U+2328) with the text presentation selector, so the menu bar draws it in
85	    /// its own ink and never as an emoji (CU-61).
86	    static let keysGlyph = "⌨\u{FE0E}"
87	    /// The menu's first, disabled row while shortcuts record (CU-61).
88	    static let keysRow = "Recording keyboard shortcuts"
89	    /// The longest time the item is sized for (the type doc).
90	    static let widestElapsed: TimeInterval = 35_999
91	    /// Room each side of the title inside the item.
92	    static let titleInset: CGFloat = 6
93	    /// The item's one length: the wider of the two marks' titles at
94	    /// `widestElapsed`, rounded up, plus the insets (the type doc).
95	    static let itemLength: CGFloat = RecorderStatusItem.itemLength(keys: false)
96	
97	    /// The length for an item that shows the keyboard mark or not: the wider of the two marks'
98	    /// titles at `widestElapsed`, rounded up, plus the insets (CU-61).
99	    static func itemLength(keys: Bool) -> CGFloat {
100	        [false, true].map { paused in
101	            ceil(
102	                RecorderStatusItem.title(elapsed: widestElapsed, paused: paused, keys: keys)
103	                    .size().width)
104	                + 2 * titleInset
105	        }.reduce(0, max)
106	    }
107	
108	    /// Whether this item shows the keyboard mark and row: the recording records shortcuts.
109	    let keys: Bool
110	    private let onPause: () -> Void
111	    private let onResume: () -> Void
112	    private let onStop: () -> Void
113	    private var item: NSStatusItem?
114	    /// Which of the two menus the item shows. `update` compares `paused`
115	    /// with it before touching the menu (the type doc).
116	    private var menuShowsPaused = false
117	    /// Set by `freeze()`: `update` then reads its mark from `menuShowsPaused`
118	    /// and never from the argument.
119	    private var frozen = false
120	
121	    init(
122	        keys: Bool = false, onPause: @escaping () -> Void, onResume: @escaping () -> Void,
123	        onStop: @escaping () -> Void
124	    ) {
125	        self.keys = keys
126	        self.onPause = onPause
127	        self.onResume = onResume
128	        self.onStop = onStop
129	        super.init()
130	    }
131	
132	    @available(*, unavailable)
133	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
134	        fatalError("RecorderStatusItem does not support NSCoder")
135	    }
136	
137	    deinit { remove() }
138	
139	    /// Whether the item is in the menu bar.
140	    var isShowing: Bool { item != nil }
141	
142	    /// Puts the item up, at 0:00 with the RECORDING menu and its one fixed
143	    /// length for its marks. A second call while showing is a no-op.
144	    func show() {
145	        guard item == nil else { return }
146	        let item = NSStatusBar.system.statusItem(withLength: Self.itemLength(keys: keys))
147	        item.menu = NSMenu(title: "Recording")
148	        self.item = item
149	        menuShowsPaused = false
150	        frozen = false
151	        rebuildMenu(paused: false)
152	        item.button?.toolTip = Self.tooltip(paused: false)
153	        update(elapsed: 0, paused: false)
154	    }
155	
156	    /// The owner's timer calls this — 30 Hz from the panel, 1 Hz from the
157	    /// tool — with the recorder's `elapsed`, which freezes while paused, so
158	    /// a paused label holds still on its own. The menu and the tooltip are
159	    /// rebuilt only when `paused` differs from what they show; frozen, the
160	    /// argument is ignored and the mark stays (the type doc).
161	    func update(elapsed: TimeInterval, paused: Bool) {
162	        guard let item else { return }
163	        let paused = frozen ? menuShowsPaused : paused
164	        item.button?.attributedTitle = Self.title(elapsed: elapsed, paused: paused, keys: keys)
165	        guard paused != menuShowsPaused else { return }
166	        menuShowsPaused = paused
167	        rebuildMenu(paused: paused)
168	        item.button?.toolTip = Self.tooltip(paused: paused)
169	    }
170	
171	    /// From the owner's Stop on: the mark and the menu stay what they last
172	    /// were, whatever `update` is told (the type doc).
173	    func freeze() {
174	        frozen = true
175	    }
176	
177	    /// A click on the item's button, which pops its menu as a person's click
178	    /// would (the type doc); false with no item to click, which the caller
179	    /// answers with a beep.
180	    @discardableResult
181	    func openMenu() -> Bool {
182	        guard let button = item?.button else { return false }
183	        button.performClick(nil)
184	        return true
185	    }
186	
187	    func remove() {
188	        guard let item else { return }
189	        NSStatusBar.system.removeStatusItem(item)
190	        self.item = nil
191	    }
192	
193	    /// The rows of the menu the item already has, replaced in place: the
194	    /// first is Pause or Resume by `paused`, the second is always Stop; while
195	    /// shortcuts record, a disabled `keysRow` and a separator come first.
196	    private func rebuildMenu(paused: Bool) {
197	        guard let menu = item?.menu else { return }
198	        menu.removeAllItems()
199	        if keys {
200	            let row = NSMenuItem(title: Self.keysRow, action: nil, keyEquivalent: "")
201	            row.isEnabled = false
202	            menu.addItem(row)
203	            menu.addItem(.separator())
204	        }
205	        let actions = [
206	            paused ? #selector(resumeClicked(_:)) : #selector(pauseClicked(_:)),
207	            #selector(stopClicked(_:)),
208	        ]
209	        for (title, action) in zip(Self.menuTitles(paused: paused), actions) {
210	            let row = NSMenuItem(title: title, action: action, keyEquivalent: "")
211	            row.target = self
212	            menu.addItem(row)
213	        }
214	    }
215	
216	    @objc private func pauseClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
217	        onPause()
218	    }
219	
220	    @objc private func resumeClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
221	        onResume()
222	    }
223	
224	    @objc private func stopClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
225	        onStop()
226	    }
227	
228	    // MARK: - The vocabulary, pure
229	
230	    /// The rows, in order, the separator aside: `keysRow` first while shortcuts record. Pure, so
231	    /// a probe can pin every menu.
232	    static func menuTitles(paused: Bool, keys: Bool = false) -> [String] {
233	        (keys ? [keysRow] : []) + [paused ? "Resume Recording" : "Pause Recording", "Stop Recording"]
234	    }
235	
236	    /// The button's tooltip, which says which of the two states the item
237	    /// is showing.
238	    static func tooltip(paused: Bool) -> String {
239	        paused ? "Frame Job's recording is paused" : "Frame Job is recording"
240	    }
241	
242	    /// `m:ss`, and `h:mm:ss` past an hour. Pure, so a probe can pin it.
243	    static func label(for seconds: TimeInterval) -> String {
244	        let whole = Int(max(0, seconds.rounded(.down)))
245	        let hours = whole / 3600
246	        let minutes = (whole % 3600) / 60
247	        let secs = whole % 60
248	        if hours > 0 { return String(format: "%d:%02d:%02d", hours, minutes, secs) }
249	        return String(format: "%d:%02d", minutes, secs)
250	    }
251	
252	    /// The dot in `DS.meterClip` while recording, or the pause glyph in the
253	    /// menu bar's own colour while paused (the type doc), then, while
254	    /// shortcuts record, a space and `keysGlyph` in the menu bar's own colour,
255	    /// then the time in the menu bar's own face with monospaced digits.
256	    static func title(elapsed: TimeInterval, paused: Bool, keys: Bool = false)
257	        -> NSAttributedString
258	    {
259	        let size = NSFont.systemFontSize
260	        var mark: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [.font: NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: size)]
261	        if !paused { mark[.foregroundColor] = DS.meterClip }
262	        let title = NSMutableAttributedString(string: paused ? pauseGlyph : "●", attributes: mark)
263	        if keys {
264	            title.append(
265	                NSAttributedString(
266	                    string: " " + keysGlyph, attributes: [.font: NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: size)]))
267	        }
268	        title.append(
269	            NSAttributedString(
270	                string: " " + label(for: elapsed),
271	                attributes: [.font: NSFont.monospacedDigitSystemFont(ofSize: size, weight: .regular)]))
272	        return title
273	    }
274	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

245	    /// sitting late. Now the trimmed clip's start is compared with the
246	    /// core's own snap of the requested `to`, and a start that is not it is
247	    /// the clamp: the voice is wholly under its head, mints NO clip, and its
248	    /// sentence names the file. And the moved clip must land exactly where
249	    /// the core's snap of the delta says, at or above the floor, or the
250	    /// throw names the file — a refused op can never ride a committed list.
251	    /// At an INEXACT rate the move's landing can be a tick under a floor
252	    /// that is a grid point (the delta and the trim round separately; grid
253	    /// points are not closed under addition), which the rule would accept
254	    /// and dress as a transition, so that one case is done once more a
255	    /// frame up with a frame more head: the content stays aligned to the
256	    /// tick, the voice starts a sub-frame gap after the previous one, and
257	    /// its first frame past the head is the price — the documented limit of
258	    /// such a rate, beside the pictures' own sub-frame gap.
259	    static func addMicrophoneClip(
260	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, pictureAt: Ticks, offset: Ticks, floor: Ticks,
261	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
262	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
263	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
264	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
265	        if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
266	            notes.append(note)
267	            return nil
268	        }
269	        let start = pictureAt - offset
270	        let head = start < floor ? ReelTime.snapToFrame(floor - start, fps: fps) : 0
271	        guard head > 0 else {
272	            guard
273	                let placed = try placeClip(
274	                    media, on: track, at: max(start, floor), notBelow: floor, scope: scope,
275	                    to: &trial, ops: &ops)
276	            else {
277	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
278	            }
279	            return placed
280	        }
281	        let frame = fps.frameDuration
282	        for (at, head) in [(floor, head), (floor + frame, head + frame)] {
283	            var attempt = trial
284	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
285	            guard
286	                let placed = try headTrimmed(
287	                    media, file: file, on: track, at: at, head: head, floor: floor, fps: fps,
288	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
289	            else {
290	                notes.append(underNote(file, head: head, floor: floor))
291	                return nil
292	            }
293	            if placed.start >= floor {
294	                trial = attempt
295	                ops += attemptOps
296	                return placed
297	            }
298	        }
299	        throw ReelCoreError(
300	            message: "\(file.path) could not be placed clear of the previous microphone clip.")
301	    }
302	
303	    /// The dance once, on `trial`: the add at `at` (never under `floor`),
304	    /// the trim to the landed start + `head`, the move back by what the trim
305	    /// advanced. nil when the trim clamped — the voice is wholly under its
306	    /// head — with the trial left as it was; every other surprise is a
307	    /// throw naming the file. The clip returned may still sit a tick under
308	    /// the floor at an inexact rate, which the caller reads.
309	    static func headTrimmed(
310	        _ media: UInt32, file: MediaSnapshot, on track: UInt32, at: Ticks, head: Ticks,
311	        floor: Ticks, fps: Fps, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
312	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
313	        guard
314	            let added = try placeClip(
315	                media, on: track, at: at, notBelow: floor, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
316	        else {
317	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
318	        }
319	        let trim = ReelOp.trimStart(clip: added.id, to: added.start + head)
320	        let promisedTrim = ReelTime.snapToFrame(added.start + head, fps: fps)
321	        guard let trimmed = try trial.applying(trim.scoped(scope)).project,
322	            try clip(added.id, in: trimmed, scope: scope).start == promisedTrim
323	        else { return nil }
324	        let advanced = promisedTrim - added.start
325	        let move = ReelOp.moveClip(clips: [added.id], delta: -advanced)
326	        let promisedStart = promisedTrim + ReelTime.snapToFrame(-advanced, fps: fps)
327	        guard let moved = try trimmed.applying(move.scoped(scope)).project else {
328	            throw ReelCoreError(
329	                message: "\(file.path) could not be moved back by its \(milliseconds(advanced)) ms head.")
330	        }
331	        let landed = try clip(added.id, in: moved, scope: scope)
332	        guard landed.start == promisedStart, landed.source.sourceIn == advanced else {
333	            throw ReelCoreError(
334	                message: "\(file.path) landed at \(landed.start) with \(landed.source.sourceIn) "
335	                    + "trimmed, not at \(promisedStart) with \(advanced).")
336	        }
337	        trial = moved
338	        ops += [trim, move]
339	        return landed
340	    }
341	
342	    /// The sentence for a voice wholly under its head.
343	    private static func underNote(_ file: MediaSnapshot, head: Ticks, floor: Ticks) -> String {
344	        let clear = floor == 0 ? "the start of the timeline" : "the previous microphone clip"
345	        return "\(file.path) was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of "
346	            + "it would remain after the \(milliseconds(head)) ms head that keeps it clear of "
347	            + "\(clear)."
348	    }

353	/// What a recording ENDS as — `StopReason`, `RecordingResult` and
354	/// `RecorderError` — the foot of `RecordingSetup.swift` moved whole, as a
355	/// pure move landed alone (road map 3, R2's toll), because that file stood
356	/// at 387 lines against the 400-line cap for a new file and the result
357	/// type is where R2's segments land. Values a probe can make, as before:
358	/// `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` constructs every one of them without a
359	/// stream. `RecordingSetup.swift` keeps what a recording IS before it
360	/// starts; `ScreenRecorder+Finishing.swift` is the one producer of a
361	/// `RecordingResult`; `RecordingLanding.swift` and the two doors are its
362	/// readers.
363	
364	/// How the recording ended. `.stopped` is `ScreenRecorder.stop()`; the other
365	/// two are the stream delegate's `didStopWithError` codes: `.userStopped`
366	/// is −3817 (`SCStreamError.Code.userStopped`, the system's own menu-bar
367	/// indicator) and `.systemStopped` is −3821 (the code is spelled
368	/// `.systemStoppedStream`; a display that slept or went away) — and, while
369	/// PAUSED, any other stream stop as well, since nothing was writing
370	/// (`ScreenRecorder+Delegates.swift`).
371	enum StopReason: Equatable {
372	    case stopped
373	    case userStopped
374	    case systemStopped
375	}

377	/// One SEGMENT of a recording — the two files one stretch between a start
378	/// (or a resume) and a pause (or the stop) wrote, probed, and how they line
379	/// up (road map 3, decision 6: a paused recording is a sequence of files
380	/// over one stream, and every segment carries its OWN offset, because R0 q7
381	/// measured a different number for each resume).
382	struct RecordingSegment {
383	    /// The movie, probed through `MediaImporter.probe` (completion on main);
384	    /// for a voice-over (`RecordingResult.isVoiceOver`) that stretch's `.m4a`,
385	    /// with `micDescriptor` nil and `micOffset` 0.
386	    let descriptor: MediaDescriptor
387	    /// The `.m4a`, probed, when a microphone was chosen AND this segment's
388	    /// file landed; nil otherwise, and `micProblem` says which.
389	    let micDescriptor: MediaDescriptor?
390	    /// Screen did-start minus microphone did-start, in ticks, for THIS
391	    /// segment. POSITIVE means the picture began AFTER the microphone, so
392	    /// the microphone clip starts that much earlier than the picture's (or
393	    /// has its in point trimmed by it). Measured per segment, never a
394	    /// constant (R0 q6b: +11 ms mean, 35 ms scatter with the session
395	    /// started first; q7: −22 to +33 ms across resumes). 0 with no
396	    /// microphone.
397	    let micOffset: Ticks
398	    /// The screen's did-start, wall clock (its fallbacks are the call that
399	    /// asked for it, `ScreenRecorder+Finishing.swift`'s rule).
400	    let startedAt: Date
401	    /// Non-nil when a microphone was chosen but this segment's file did
402	    /// not land — it never started, the writer reported an error, the
403	    /// device went away, or the file would not probe (R1 review finding 0:
404	    /// a microphone problem does not fail a recording whose picture is on
405	    /// disk). The sentence names the file when one was left behind.
406	    /// `micDescriptor` is nil whenever this is set. For a voice-over it is
407	    /// set only on a segment whose writer stopped on its own (spec §11
408	    /// recording, "A voice-over is a recording with no picture").
409	    let micProblem: String?
410	    /// A camera beside the screen (spec §11 CAM-9): this segment's
411	    /// `(Camera).mov`, probed; nil without a camera, for a writer that took
412	    /// no buffer, and whenever `cameraProblem` is set.
413	    let cameraDescriptor: MediaDescriptor?
414	    /// The camera's first buffer minus the screen's start (E2, else E1,
415	    /// else the arrivals), in ticks; POSITIVE means the camera began after
416	    /// the screen. 0 without `cameraDescriptor`.
417	    let cameraOffset: Ticks
418	    /// This segment's camera file did not land — its writer failed or it
419	    /// would not probe — naming the file when it is on disk.
420	    let cameraProblem: String?
421	    /// Beside `cameraDescriptor` only: this segment's camera was placed by
422	    /// E1 because the frame watch could not go back on the stream at its
423	    /// resume (CAM-9 (6)), naming why.
424	    let cameraNote: String?
425	    /// This segment's cursor file, `<stem>.fjcursor` beside its movie (spec
426	    /// §11 CU-18); nil when none was written, and then `cursorProblem` says
427	    /// why (a session with no cursor capture writes none and says nothing).
428	    let cursorURL: URL?
429	    /// Why this segment has no cursor file, or what its file lacks (CU-12,
430	    /// CU-13, CU-14); never the recording's failure.
431	    let cursorProblem: String?
432	    /// The written file's `cursor_image` (`none` since CU-S1's verdict);
433	    /// nil without a file.
434	    let cursorImage: CursorImageMode?
435	
436	    init(
437	        descriptor: MediaDescriptor, micDescriptor: MediaDescriptor?, micOffset: Ticks,
438	        startedAt: Date, micProblem: String? = nil, cameraDescriptor: MediaDescriptor? = nil,
439	        cameraOffset: Ticks = 0, cameraProblem: String? = nil, cameraNote: String? = nil,
440	        cursorURL: URL? = nil, cursorProblem: String? = nil, cursorImage: CursorImageMode? = nil
441	    ) {
442	        self.descriptor = descriptor
443	        self.micDescriptor = micDescriptor
444	        self.micOffset = micOffset
445	        self.startedAt = startedAt
446	        self.micProblem = micProblem
447	        self.cameraDescriptor = cameraDescriptor
448	        self.cameraOffset = cameraOffset
449	        self.cameraProblem = cameraProblem
450	        self.cameraNote = cameraNote
451	        self.cursorURL = cursorURL
452	        self.cursorProblem = cursorProblem
453	        self.cursorImage = cursorImage
454	    }

456	    /// This segment with its cursor fields set, every other field kept; `attached`, when given,
457	    /// is its descriptor's `cursor` (spec §11 CU-34 (c), (d)).
458	    func withCursor(
459	        url: URL?, problem: String?, image: CursorImageMode?, attached: MediaCursor? = nil
460	    ) -> RecordingSegment {
461	        var described = descriptor
462	        if let attached { described.cursor = attached }
463	        return RecordingSegment(
464	            descriptor: described, micDescriptor: micDescriptor, micOffset: micOffset,
465	            startedAt: startedAt, micProblem: micProblem, cameraDescriptor: cameraDescriptor,
466	            cameraOffset: cameraOffset, cameraProblem: cameraProblem, cameraNote: cameraNote,
467	            cursorURL: url, cursorProblem: problem, cursorImage: image)
468	    }
469	}

471	/// A segment whose MOVIE would not probe, left out of the recording (#97),
472	/// or a CLOSED segment whose writer failed after its stop, left out
473	/// unprobed (#181): the movie as named, the files it left on disk at settle
474	/// (movie, then microphone, each only if there), and the error `settle`
475	/// built for it — the writer's own sentence for the second.
476	/// `sentence` is what the panel's note and the tool's `note` say about it.
477	/// `micDescriptor` is its microphone file, probed, when it reads (#181 item
478	/// 2, spec §11 recording): the landing puts that voice in the picture's
479	/// slot. `position` is how many of `RecordingResult.segments` were recorded
480	/// before it — where that slot is among the landed segments.
481	struct UnreadableSegment {
482	    /// For a voice-over, the `.m4a` that would not probe.
483	    let moviePath: String
484	    let keptFiles: [String]
485	    let error: RecorderError
486	    let micDescriptor: MediaDescriptor?
487	    let position: Int
488	
489	    init(
490	        moviePath: String, keptFiles: [String], error: RecorderError,
491	        micDescriptor: MediaDescriptor? = nil, position: Int = 0
492	    ) {
493	        self.moviePath = moviePath
494	        self.keptFiles = keptFiles
495	        self.error = error
496	        self.micDescriptor = micDescriptor
497	        self.position = position
498	    }
499	
500	    var sentence: String {
501	        "A segment was left out. " + error.localizedDescription
502	            + (keptFiles.isEmpty
503	                ? " It left no file on disk."
504	                : " Its files are kept at " + keptFiles.joined(separator: ", ") + ".")
505	    }

508	/// What a camera recording records with (spec §11 CAM-3): the device's name,
509	/// the format it recorded at as `CameraDevices.spelled` writes it
510	/// (`1760x1328@30`), and `problem` — the sentence of a camera that stopped on
511	/// its own (a runtime error, an interruption, a disconnect), which ended a
512	/// camera recording with `stoppedBy` `.systemStopped` and, beside a screen
513	/// (CAM-9 (7)), ended only the camera's files; nil when it did not. `note`
514	/// is the warm-up's sentence when the stream had not reached the format's
515	/// rate by the bound and the recording began anyway (`CameraCapture.WarmUp`).
516	struct RecordingCamera: Equatable {
517	    let name: String
518	    let format: String
519	    var problem: String?
520	    var note: String?
521	}

523	/// What a recording ends as: its segments, in order — ONE for a recording
524	/// never paused — and what `RecordingLanding` turns into ops, one clip per
525	/// segment placed at the previous segment's end. `unreadable` is every
526	/// segment whose movie would not probe, or whose writer failed after the
527	/// segment closed (#181), left out of `segments` and named in
528	/// `unreadableNote` (#97); a recording with NO readable movie is a failure,
529	/// never a result.
530	///
531	/// There is deliberately no `micDescriptor` and no `micOffset` on the
532	/// result: those are a SEGMENT's, and a reader that compiled against a
533	/// first-segment convenience would be silently wrong for a paused
534	/// recording. `descriptor` and `startedAt` ARE the first segment's, because
535	/// "the recording's file" is one thing to the readers that use them — the
536	/// untitled document's source and name, the path a tool addresses that
537	/// document by.
538	struct RecordingResult {
539	    /// Never empty.
540	    let segments: [RecordingSegment]
541	    let choice: RecordingChoice
542	    let stoppedBy: StopReason
543	    /// A camera recording's camera (`isCamera`), or the camera recorded
544	    /// beside a screen (spec §11 CAM-9); nil for every other recording.
545	    let camera: RecordingCamera?
546	
547	    /// The FIRST segment's movie.
548	    var descriptor: MediaDescriptor { segments[0].descriptor }
549	    /// The FIRST segment's screen did-start, wall clock.
550	    var startedAt: Date { segments[0].startedAt }
551	    /// A voice-over: the microphone alone, every segment's `descriptor` its
552	    /// `.m4a` (spec §11 recording, #99).
553	    var isVoiceOver: Bool { choice.source == .voiceOver }
554	    /// A camera alone (spec §11 CAM-3): every segment's `descriptor` is the
555	    /// camera's `.mov`, landed by the picture rule as a screen's is.
556	    var isCamera: Bool { choice.source == .camera }
557	    /// Every segment's microphone problem, in order, joined by a space; nil
558	    /// when no segment has one.
559	    var micProblem: String? {
560	        let problems = segments.compactMap { $0.micProblem }
561	        return problems.isEmpty ? nil : problems.joined(separator: " ")
562	    }
563	    /// How many times Pause was pressed — STORED and counted on the session,
564	    /// never `segments.count − 1`: a pause with no resume before the Stop
565	    /// leaves ONE file and was still a pause (the R2 review: it read 0).
566	    let pauses: Int
567	    /// The segments left out because their movie would not probe, or
568	    /// because their writer failed after the segment closed (#181), in
569	    /// segment order; empty when every movie read.
570	    let unreadable: [UnreadableSegment]
571	    /// Every left-out segment's sentence, joined by a space; nil when none.
572	    var unreadableNote: String? {
573	        unreadable.isEmpty ? nil : unreadable.map(\.sentence).joined(separator: " ")
574	    }
575	
576	    /// The files on disk, for a sentence that sends a person to them: every
577	    /// segment's movie in order, comma-joined, then — when any landed —
578	    /// " and its microphone at <file>" for one microphone file or " and its
579	    /// microphone files at <a>, <b>" for several; then, for a camera beside
580	    /// the screen (spec §11 CAM-10 (8)), " and its camera at <file>" or " and
581	    /// its camera files at <a>, <b>" the same way. One shape for the panel's
582	    /// note and the tool's `savedButNotAdded`, so a three-segment failure
583	    /// names three files at both doors (the R2 review: the panel named one).
584	    var filesClause: String {
585	        let movies = segments.map { $0.descriptor.path }.joined(separator: ", ")
586	        let mics = segments.compactMap { $0.micDescriptor?.path }
587	        let cameras = segments.compactMap { $0.cameraDescriptor?.path }
588	        let clause: String
589	        switch mics.count {
590	        case 0: clause = movies
591	        case 1: clause = movies + " and its microphone at " + mics[0]
592	        default: clause = movies + " and its microphone files at " + mics.joined(separator: ", ")
593	        }
594	        switch cameras.count {
595	        case 0: return clause
596	        case 1: return clause + " and its camera at " + cameras[0]
597	        default: return clause + " and its camera files at " + cameras.joined(separator: ", ")
598	        }
599	    }
600	
601	    /// Every segment's camera sentences beside the screen (spec §11 CAM-10
602	    /// (6)): its `cameraProblem`, then its `cameraNote`, segment by segment,
603	    /// joined by a space; nil when no segment has one.
604	    var cameraSegmentsNote: String? {
605	        let sentences = segments.flatMap { [$0.cameraProblem, $0.cameraNote].compactMap { $0 } }
606	        return sentences.isEmpty ? nil : sentences.joined(separator: " ")
607	    }
608	
609	    /// Every segment's `cursorProblem` (spec §11 CU-18), in order, joined by a
610	    /// space; nil when no segment has one.
611	    var cursorSegmentsNote: String? {
612	        let problems = segments.compactMap { $0.cursorProblem }
613	        return problems.isEmpty ? nil : problems.joined(separator: " ")
614	    }
615	
616	    init(
617	        segments: [RecordingSegment], choice: RecordingChoice, stoppedBy: StopReason,
618	        pauses: Int, unreadable: [UnreadableSegment] = [], camera: RecordingCamera? = nil
619	    ) {
620	        precondition(!segments.isEmpty, "a RecordingResult carries at least one segment")
621	        self.segments = segments
622	        self.choice = choice
623	        self.stoppedBy = stoppedBy
624	        self.pauses = pauses
625	        self.unreadable = unreadable
626	        self.camera = camera
627	    }

629	    /// ONE segment — R1's shape, kept so a single-segment construction (the
630	    /// probe's rows, a recording never paused) reads as it did; `pauses`
631	    /// defaults to 0 for it, since one file with no pause is what it means.
632	    init(
633	        descriptor: MediaDescriptor, micDescriptor: MediaDescriptor?, micOffset: Ticks,
634	        choice: RecordingChoice, startedAt: Date, stoppedBy: StopReason,
635	        micProblem: String? = nil, pauses: Int = 0
636	    ) {
637	        self.init(
638	            segments: [
639	                RecordingSegment(
640	                    descriptor: descriptor, micDescriptor: micDescriptor, micOffset: micOffset,
641	                    startedAt: startedAt, micProblem: micProblem)
642	            ], choice: choice, stoppedBy: stoppedBy, pauses: pauses)
643	    }

646	/// One stretch of the recording's timeline, in recording order: a landed
647	/// segment (an index into `segments`), or a left-out segment's readable
648	/// voice with no picture (an index into `unreadable`) — #181 item 2.
649	enum RecordingStretch: Equatable {
650	    case segment(Int)
651	    case voiceOnly(Int)
652	}
653	
654	extension RecordingResult {
655	    /// Every landed segment and every left-out voice that reads, in the
656	    /// order they were recorded: before each segment `k`, the left-out
657	    /// entries at `position == k` with a microphone (in `unreadable`'s
658	    /// order), then the segment; after the last, those at `segments.count`.
659	    /// With no left-out voice it is `.segment(0)…` exactly, so every landing
660	    /// over it is the one before #181 item 2.
661	    var stretches: [RecordingStretch] {
662	        func voices(at k: Int) -> [RecordingStretch] {
663	            unreadable.indices.filter { unreadable[$0].position == k && unreadable[$0].micDescriptor != nil }
664	                .map { RecordingStretch.voiceOnly($0) }
665	        }
666	        var list: [RecordingStretch] = []
667	        for k in segments.indices {
668	            list += voices(at: k)
669	            list.append(.segment(k))
670	        }
671	        return list + voices(at: segments.count)
672	    }
673	
674	    /// What a landing that SUCCEEDED says about each left-out voice it
675	    /// added, joined by a space; nil when no left-out segment's microphone
676	    /// read. Never said by a failed landing (`savedButNotAdded`,
677	    /// `failedToLand`), which `unreadableNote` alone serves.
678	    var leftOutVoiceNote: String? {
679	        let paths = unreadable.compactMap { $0.micDescriptor?.path }
680	        guard !paths.isEmpty else { return nil }
681	        return paths.map {
682	            "The left-out segment's microphone, \($0), was added to the project without its "
683	                + "picture."
684	        }.joined(separator: " ")
685	    }
686	}

688	/// `.busy` is `start()` while not idle, and nothing else answers it any
689	/// more: a `stop()` in any state joins the finishing already under way
690	/// (R1 review finding 1). `.notPaused` is `resume()` while not paused
691	/// (R2); `.alreadyPaused` is `pause()` while paused — its own sentence,
692	/// because "no recording is in progress" is false while `isRecording` is
693	/// true — and `.notRecording` is `pause()` idle, arming or finishing.
694	/// `.startTimedOut` is the arm ceiling and `.timedOut` the finish ceiling,
695	/// two sentences because they name two different waits (finding 5).
696	/// `.filesKept` wraps a failure reached once a file was on disk, so the
697	/// panel's note and the tool's error carry the path with no change on their
698	/// side (finding 6); with segments its `movie` and `microphone` strings are
699	/// comma-joined lists, and the one-file sentence is byte for byte R1's; an
700	/// EMPTY `movie` (no movie on disk) names the microphone files alone (B55).
701	/// `.cameraDevice` is the camera's `.microphoneDevice`: no such camera, or one
702	/// that cannot be recorded from (spec §11 CAM-3).
703	indirect enum RecorderError: Error, LocalizedError {
704	    case busy
705	    case notRecording
706	    case notPaused
707	    case alreadyPaused
708	    case startFailed(String)
709	    case finishFailed(String)
710	    case startTimedOut
711	    case timedOut
712	    case microphoneDevice(String)
713	    case cameraDevice(String)
714	    case filesKept(RecorderError, movie: String, microphone: String?)
715	
716	    var errorDescription: String? {
717	        switch self {
718	        case .busy: return "A recording is already in progress."
719	        case .notRecording: return "No recording is in progress."
720	        case .notPaused: return "The recording is not paused."
721	        case .alreadyPaused: return "The recording is already paused."
722	        case .startFailed(let why): return why
723	        case .finishFailed(let why): return why
724	        case .startTimedOut:
725	            return "The recording did not start within \(Int(ScreenRecorder.armCeiling)) s."
726	        case .timedOut:
727	            return "The recording did not finish writing within "
728	                + "\(Int(ScreenRecorder.finishCeiling)) s."
729	        case .microphoneDevice(let why): return why
730	        case .cameraDevice(let why): return why
731	        case .filesKept(let inner, let movie, let microphone):
732	            let base = inner.errorDescription ?? "The recording failed."
733	            guard !movie.isEmpty else {
734	                return microphone.map { base + " The microphone is at \($0)." } ?? base
735	            }
736	            let clause = microphone.map { "; the microphone at \($0)" } ?? ""
737	            return base + " The recording is at \(movie)\(clause)."
738	        }
739	    }
740	}

5	/// The half of screen recording a probe can call: values in, values out, no
6	/// framework object that needs a bundle (road map 3, R1a). What a recording
7	/// IS before it starts — the choice, where its files go and the two
8	/// ScreenCaptureKit configurations built from that choice (the two grants
9	/// it stands on are `RecordingGrant.swift`'s) — so that
10	/// `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` can read every field back from a bare
11	/// Mach-O that never starts a stream.
12	///
13	/// `ScreenRecorder.swift` (with `+Pause.swift`, `+Microphone.swift`,
14	/// `+Finishing.swift`, `+Delegates.swift` and `+Content.swift`) is the other
15	/// half: the class that owns the `SCStream`, one `SCRecordingOutput` per
16	/// SEGMENT (R2: a pause removes one and a resume adds the next) and, when a
17	/// microphone is chosen, the `AVCaptureSession` for the second file. The
18	/// result types a recording ends as — `StopReason`, `RecordingSegment`,
19	/// `RecordingResult`, `RecorderError` — are `RecordingResult.swift`, moved
20	/// off the foot of this file at the 400-line cap; they are still values a
21	/// probe can make.
22	///
23	/// Three R0 facts shape the configuration and are restated on the fields
24	/// they decide (`archive/roadmap-3.md`, "R0 — the answers"):
25	///
26	/// - **The microphone is a second file** (q2). `captureMicrophone` on the
27	///   stream writes ONE stereo track that is the SUM of system and microphone
28	///   sound, which is decision 5's bad case — so `make` never sets it, and
29	///   `RecordingChoice.microphone` names an `AVCaptureDevice` for
30	///   `ScreenRecorder`'s capture session instead.
31	/// - **`.best` does not scale by itself** (q4). `captureResolution = .best`
32	///   at the display's point size writes a point-sized file; pixels come only
33	///   when `width`/`height` are asked for in pixels, so `make` multiplies the
34	///   point size by the display's backing scale under `.best` itself.
35	/// - **Show Clicks needs BGRA** (q6a). `SCStream.h` says `showMouseClicks`
36	///   "currently applies when pixelFormat is set to BGRA" and a fresh
37	///   configuration reads `420v`, so `make` sets `REDACTED`
38	///   when the stream draws clicks and leaves the default alone otherwise —
39	///   measured, a recording output over a BGRA stream starts and writes. The
40	///   stream draws the pointer and its click ring only In the picture
41	///   (road map creator-jobs CU3c, spec §11 CU-31): with Separate, `make`
42	///   sets neither and keeps `420v`, and Show Clicks lands the screen clips
43	///   with ripples instead (`RecordingLanding+Cursor.swift`).

47	/// What is recorded. `.picked` is the panel's picker result, whose filter
48	/// is carried beside the choice (`ScreenRecorder.start` takes the filter as
49	/// its own argument), so the source enum never holds a framework object.
50	/// `.voiceOver` is the microphone alone, no picture (spec §11 recording, #99):
51	/// `ScreenRecorder.startVoiceOver` records it and `start` refuses it.
52	/// `.camera` is a camera alone, the device in `RecordingChoice.camera` (spec
53	/// §11 CAM-3): `ScreenRecorder.startCamera` records it and `start` refuses it,
54	/// while `start` records a camera beside a display, window or picked source (CAM-9).
55	enum RecordingSource: Equatable {
56	    case display(CGDirectDisplayID)
57	    case window(CGWindowID)
58	    case picked
59	    case voiceOver
60	    case camera
61	}

98	    /// quiet-machine re-run of CU-S2's window rows settled their anchor as E1, so it is

103	    /// window or a picked source, and `.separate` for a voice-over or a camera alone, which have

106	        switch source {
107	        case .display: return .separate
108	        case .window, .picked: return windowDefault

155	/// Decision 2 (road map 3 §0): a recording is ORIGINAL footage and lives in
156	/// `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time — never in the
157	/// package (an untitled document has none) and never in the temporary
158	/// directory (where a cache is regenerable and footage would be lost). The
159	/// folder is created on demand, and `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides it the
160	/// way `-RCFFmpegPath` overrides the binary (`FFmpegRewrap.locate`), so a
161	/// proof can record into `tools/proof/work/` and delete it.
162	enum RecordingFiles {
163	    /// The launch-argument override, read from `UserDefaults.standard` so it
164	    /// works from the argument domain (`-RCRecordingFolder ~/x` on the
165	    /// command line, or a pinned volatile domain in a probe).
166	    static let folderDefaultsKey = "RCRecordingFolder"
167	
168	    /// The default folder's name under `~/Movies`.
169	    static let folderName = "Frame Job Recordings"
170	
171	    /// The folder a recording goes into: the override, tilde-expanded, when
172	    /// one is set; `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` otherwise. Nothing is
173	    /// created here — `create(_:)` is called at the moment a recording has
174	    /// something to put in it, `AppSupport`'s rule.
175	    static func folder() -> URL {
176	        if let override = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: folderDefaultsKey),
177	            !override.isEmpty
178	        {
179	            return URL(
180	                fileURLWithPath: (override as NSString).expandingTildeInPath, isDirectory: true)
181	        }
182	        let movies =
183	            FileManager.default.urls(for: .moviesDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first
184	            ?? FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser.appendingPathComponent(
185	                "Movies", isDirectory: true)
186	        return movies.appendingPathComponent(folderName, isDirectory: true)
187	    }
188	
189	    /// `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22` — the Screenshot app's
190	    /// spelling, in the machine's own time zone. The formatter is pinned to
191	    /// `en_US_POSIX` so a locale with another digit set or a 12-hour clock
192	    /// cannot change the name's shape; the seconds make a name unique across
193	    /// the app's own recordings and `uniqueURL` handles the rest.
194	    static func stem(at date: Date) -> String {
195	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
196	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
197	        formatter.timeZone = .current
198	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Screen Recording' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
199	        return formatter.string(from: date)
200	    }
201	
202	    /// `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04` — a voice-over's file, `stem(at:)`'s
203	    /// spelling and pinning with its own lead word.
204	    static func voiceOverStem(at date: Date) -> String {
205	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
206	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
207	        formatter.timeZone = .current
208	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Voice-over' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
209	        return formatter.string(from: date)
210	    }
211	
212	    /// `<stem>.<ext>` in `folder`, or `<stem> (2).<ext>`, `<stem> (3).<ext>`…
213	    /// while a file of that name exists — the Finder's own collision rule.
214	    static func uniqueURL(in folder: URL, stem: String, ext: String) -> URL {
215	        let manager = FileManager.default
216	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension(ext)
217	        var counter = 2
218	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) {
219	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
220	                .appendingPathExtension(ext)
221	            counter += 1
222	        }
223	        return candidate
224	    }
225	
226	    /// The microphone's own file, beside the movie: the movie's stem plus
227	    /// ` (Microphone)`, as `.m4a` (R0 q6b: `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput` writes
228	    /// one mono 48 kHz AAC track there), made unique the same way.
229	    static func microphoneURL(beside movie: URL) -> URL {
230	        let stem = movie.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent + " (Microphone)"
231	        return uniqueURL(in: movie.deletingLastPathComponent(), stem: stem, ext: "m4a")
232	    }
233	
234	    /// Makes the folder, intermediate directories included. A folder that
235	    /// already exists is not an error.
236	    static func create(_ folder: URL) throws {
237	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
238	            at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
239	    }
240	}

244	/// The two ScreenCaptureKit configurations a choice becomes. PURE — every
245	/// field is set from the arguments and read back by the probe — which is
246	/// what lets the `excludesCurrentProcessAudio` mutant be caught at all: it
247	/// is invisible over MCP (nothing plays during a headless recording) and
248	/// this is the only row that sees it.
249	enum RecordingConfiguration {
250	    /// System audio is asked for at 48 kHz stereo, the rate the tap and
251	    /// `Loudness.swift` already assume of every file.
252	    static let sampleRate = 48_000
253	    static let channelCount = 2
254	
255	    /// `displayPointSize` and `scale` come from the caller, and the caller is
256	    /// `ScreenRecorder.start`, which reads them off the FILTER — its
257	    /// `contentRect` (points) and `pointPixelScale` — the one geometry
258	    /// source that also covers a picker-made filter (`SCDisplay`'s
259	    /// `width`/`height` are POINTS, R0 q4, and a display filter reports the
260	    /// display's point size and backing scale, a window filter the window's
261	    /// frame). The probe passes the numbers directly. `outputURL` is
262	    /// assigned before the output configuration is returned, and must stay
263	    /// so: reading `outputURL` off a fresh `SCRecordingOutputConfiguration`
264	    /// TRAPS (it imports non-optional and is nil underneath until assigned —
265	    /// the SDK scout's finding, exit 133).
266	    static func make(
267	        _ choice: RecordingChoice, displayPointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, outputURL: URL
268	    ) -> (stream: SCStreamConfiguration, output: SCRecordingOutputConfiguration) {
269	        let stream = SCStreamConfiguration()
270	        // R0 q4: pixels are asked for, `.best` does not scale by itself.
271	        let factor: CGFloat = choice.resolution == .best ? max(scale, 1) : 1
272	        stream.width = Int((displayPointSize.width * factor).rounded())
273	        stream.height = Int((displayPointSize.height * factor).rounded())
274	        stream.captureResolution = choice.resolution == .best ? .best : .nominal
275	        stream.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: CMTimeScale(max(choice.rate, 1)))
276	        // CU-31: the pointer and its ring are the stream's only In the picture.
277	        let inPicture = choice.effectiveCursor == .inPicture
278	        stream.showsCursor = inPicture
279	        stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks && inPicture
280	        // R0 q6a: the click circle draws only under BGRA; the default `420v`
281	        // is left alone when the stream draws no clicks, so an ordinary
282	        // recording's pixel path is byte for byte the spike's.
283	        if choice.showClicks && inPicture { stream.pixelFormat = REDACTED }
284	        stream.capturesAudio = choice.systemAudio
285	        stream.sampleRate = sampleRate
286	        stream.channelCount = channelCount
287	        // ALWAYS: the timeline can play while a recording runs and must not
288	        // be in it. `captureMicrophone` is deliberately never touched (R0
289	        // q2 — the microphone is a second file), so it keeps its default of
290	        // false, which the probe reads back on every row.
291	        stream.excludesCurrentProcessAudio = true
292	
293	        let output = SCRecordingOutputConfiguration()
294	        output.outputURL = outputURL
295	        output.outputFileType = .mov
296	        // R0 q2: `availableVideoCodecTypes` is `[avc1, hvc1]` here and the
297	        // default is `avc1`; HEVC halves the file where the encoder offers it.
298	        output.videoCodecType =
299	            output.availableVideoCodecTypes.contains(.hevc) ? .hevc : .h264
300	        return (stream, output)
301	    }
302	}

5	/// The recording session (road map 3, R1a; pause and resume R2a): a state
6	/// machine `idle → arming → recording ⇄ paused → finishing → idle` owning
7	/// the `SCStream`, one `SCRecordingOutput` per SEGMENT and — when a
8	/// microphone is chosen — the `AVCaptureSession` that writes the microphone
9	/// to a SECOND file per segment (R0 q2: `captureMicrophone` on the stream
10	/// sums the microphone into the system track, decision 5's bad case, so it
11	/// is never set). The panel and the `record_screen` tool both drive this
12	/// one object and both receive a `RecordingResult` (`RecordingResult.swift`);
13	/// `RecordingLanding` turns that into ops. This file is the arming half;
14	/// `+Started.swift` how an arm ends (`captureStarted`, `failStart`);
15	/// `+Stop.swift` is `stop()`; `ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift` is what a segment
16	/// is and the two transitions that close one and open the next;
17	/// `+Microphone.swift` the capture session's preparation and the meter;
18	/// `+Finishing.swift` everything that ENDS a session; `+Delegates.swift` the
19	/// three delegates; `+Content.swift` the static helpers over shareable
20	/// content, filters and error codes. A VOICE-OVER (`voiceSession`, spec §11
21	/// recording) is the same machine with no stream — the microphone writer
22	/// alone, a file per segment — in `+VoiceOver.swift` and
23	/// `+VoiceOverFinishing.swift`; `stop()`, `elapsed`, `pause()` and `resume()`
24	/// forward to it. A CAMERA recording (`cameraSession`, spec §11 CAM-3) is the
25	/// same machine with a camera where the stream was, in `+Camera.swift` and
26	/// `+CameraFinishing.swift`, forwarded to on the same terms. A camera BESIDE
27	/// the screen (spec §11 CAM-9) is this machine's: `+CameraBeside.swift`,
28	/// `+CameraBesideFinishing.swift` and `ScreenFrameWatch.swift`. Every screen
29	/// recording's cursor file per segment (spec §11 CU-11…CU-13, CU-18) is
30	/// `+Cursor.swift` and `CursorCapture.swift`.
31	///
32	/// **A paused recording is a sequence of files over one stream** (decision
33	/// 6). ScreenCaptureKit has no pause, so `pause()` REMOVES the segment's
34	/// recording output — its file closes — and `resume()` ADDS a fresh one to
35	/// a new file while the stream keeps capturing (R0 q7: 57 fps while
36	/// paused, the did-finish 5–25 ms after the remove, the did-start 8–10 ms
37	/// after the add); the microphone's writer is stopped and restarted per
38	/// segment on its one running session. `Session.segments` is that
39	/// sequence, never empty, and every callback finds ITS segment — by the
40	/// output's identity, by the microphone file's URL — rather than "the"
41	/// one, because the closed segment's did-finish can land after the next
42	/// has begun and a resume never waits for it.
43	///
44	/// **One hook, one delivery** (R1 review finding 4). `start` takes
45	/// `onFinish`, which is stored ON THE SESSION — installed only once every
46	/// guard has passed, when the arm really begins — and called exactly once,
47	/// at conclude, whoever ended the recording: a `stop()`, the menu bar's
48	/// indicator, the system, a failure. There is no settable hook on the
49	/// recorder any more, because there was one and a panel Record refused
50	/// `.busy` erased the tool's, after which an external stop reached nobody.
51	/// A start that FAILS never concludes: its error is the start completion's
52	/// alone. `stop()` in any state past idle JOINS (finding 1): its completion
53	/// is registered and every registered completion receives the one outcome
54	/// beside `onFinish`, so a person's Stop in the second after the menu
55	/// bar's cannot drop the landing. `.busy` is `start()` while not idle —
56	/// paused included — and nothing else.
57	///
58	/// **No `async`** (spec §11): every ScreenCaptureKit and AVFoundation entry
59	/// point used has a completion-handler or delegate form. **No queue of its
60	/// own**: the frameworks deliver their callbacks on private queues (R0 q6b:
61	/// the microphone's did-start on one labelled "File ou", the recording
62	/// output's on ScreenCaptureKit's), and each is stamped with `Date()` where
63	/// it arrives and hopped to main through `DispatchQueue.main.async` —
64	/// `MediaImporter.probe`'s shape —
65	/// so every transition runs on the main thread and needs no lock. The
66	/// microphone's did-finish arrived ON main in every measured run and is
67	/// hopped anyway.
68	///
69	/// **The callback ORDER the machine tolerates**, all measured (R0 q2, q6b,
70	/// q7): `recordingOutputDidStartRecording` fires 86–107 ms BEFORE
71	/// `startCapture`'s completion in every run, so did-start is a stamp taken
72	/// whenever it arrives and the completion consults it, never the reverse;
73	/// the microphone output's `startRecording` returns with `isRecording`
74	/// still false, so its did-start callback is the truth and the property is
75	/// never read for it; `session.startRunning()` BLOCKS main for 100–180 ms,
76	/// which is why `prepareMicrophone` exists — a countdown pays it before it
77	/// ends, so the first 0.4 s of voice is in the file — and why the session
78	/// goes FIRST when it was not prepared (the two files' first samples then
79	/// land within a frame of each other, offset +11 ms mean, 35 ms scatter);
80	/// stop → did-finish is 0.03 s without a microphone and up to 1.1 s with
81	/// one, so the finishing wait is bounded at `finishCeiling` rather than
82	/// open. The system's own menu-bar indicator can stop a capture from
83	/// outside the app (`.userStopped`; `.systemStopped` for a display that
84	/// sleeps, the stream's `.systemStoppedStream` code), while recording OR
85	/// paused — it stays up through a pause, since the stream never stops:
86	/// both take the SAME finishing path as `stop()`.
87	///
88	/// **Grants** (decision 4): this class never calls
89	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` or `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess`. It
90	/// reads `RecordingGrant.screenRecordingGranted` before building the stream
91	/// and the microphone status before constructing an `AVCaptureDeviceInput`
92	/// (whose initializer auto-prompts on `.notDetermined`), and refuses by name;
93	/// with `choice.keys` `shortcuts`, Input Monitoring is read after the
94	/// microphone and a choice whose key tap cannot be made is refused with the
95	/// same sentence (spec §11 CU-62) — never `CGRequestListenEventAccess`.
96	final class ScreenRecorder: NSObject {
97	    static let shared = ScreenRecorder()
98	
99	    enum State: Equatable { case idle, arming, recording, paused, finishing }
100	
101	    /// Seconds the finishing path waits for the writers' did-finish before
102	    /// probing whatever is on disk.
103	    static let finishCeiling: TimeInterval = 10
104	    /// Seconds `startCapture` may take to answer (R0: under 0.2 s).
105	    static let armCeiling: TimeInterval = 20
106	
107	    /// Written by this class's own six files and nothing else; the pausing,
108	    /// finishing and delegate halves live in extensions, which is why this
109	    /// is not `private(set)`.
110	    var state: State = .idle
111	    /// Every state past idle, PAUSED included: File ▸ Stop Recording, the
112	    /// quit guard and `.busy` all read a paused recording as one in
113	    /// progress. `isPaused` (`+Pause.swift`) is the narrower question.
114	    var isRecording: Bool { state != .idle }
115	    /// The microphone's level. The panel binds a `LevelMeterView(meter:)` to
116	    /// it — never `LevelMeter.shared`, or the timeline bar would meter the
117	    /// microphone.
118	    let meter = LevelMeter()
119	    /// Non-nil from the moment a microphone problem is detected — the file
120	    /// output's did-finish carrying an error while the picture still
121	    /// records (finding 3), a device that went away — so the panel's tick
122	    /// can show it live; set ONCE and kept for the session (the panel
123	    /// writes its note once; a later segment's failure is on its own
124	    /// segment), nil while idle. The result's `micProblem` carries the
125	    /// final sentences, which may say more (each file's path).
126	    var microphoneProblem: String?
127	
128	    /// Seconds RECORDED: the sum over segments of each one's span — its
129	    /// screen did-start (Date-based: the output's `recordedDuration` is
130	    /// whole seconds) to its `stoppedAt`, or to now for the one still open
131	    /// — each floored at 0, so it freezes while paused and never counts a
132	    /// gap; frozen at the stop call; 0 idle, and 0 while arming until the
133	    /// first did-start or `startCapture`'s completion lands (R1's rule,
134	    /// kept for the first segment: an arm can take seconds and none of
135	    /// them is footage).
136	    var elapsed: TimeInterval {
137	        if voiceSession != nil { return voiceElapsed }
138	        if cameraSession != nil { return cameraElapsed }
139	        guard state != .idle, let session else { return 0 }
140	        let now = Date()
141	        var total: TimeInterval = 0
142	        for (index, segment) in session.segments.enumerated() {
143	            guard let start = session.screenStart(of: index) else { continue }
144	            total += max(0, (segment.stoppedAt ?? now).timeIntervalSince(start))
145	        }
146	        return total
147	    }
148	
149	    var session: Session?
150	    /// A voice-over's session (`ScreenRecorder+VoiceOver.swift`); never set
151	    /// beside `session`.
152	    var voiceSession: VoiceSession?
153	    /// A camera recording's session (`ScreenRecorder+Camera.swift`); never
154	    /// set beside `session` or `voiceSession`.
155	    var cameraSession: CameraSession?
156	    var startCompletion: ((Error?) -> Void)?
157	    /// Every `stop()` completion registered since the arm began, delivered
158	    /// together at conclude (or by `failStart`, with its error).
159	    var stopCompletions: [(Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void] = []
