183	    /// MAIN THREAD. `completion` on main, nil on success. A refusal — busy, a
184	    /// grant absent, an unknown microphone, a folder that cannot be made —
185	    /// completes BEFORE this returns, tears down any prepared microphone
186	    /// and touches nothing else; `.busy` in particular touches NOTHING of
187	    /// the running session, its hook included. A start that reaches
188	    /// `startCapture` completes from its completion handler. `onFinish` is
189	    /// the session's (the header): installed here only once every guard
190	    /// has passed, never called for a start that fails.
191	    ///
192	    /// The geometry is the FILTER's own — `contentRect` (points) and
193	    /// `pointPixelScale` — the one source that also covers a picker-made
194	    /// filter; measured, a display filter reports the display's point size
195	    /// and backing scale, a window filter the window's frame. ORDER (R0
196	    /// q6b): the microphone session (prepared, or started here), then its
197	    /// file output, then the stream, all in one run-loop turn (`launchScreen`)
198	    /// — this one, or with a camera beside the screen the turn its warm-up
199	    /// answers (spec §11 CAM-9 (1), (2)). The first segment is minted here,
200	    /// named by the call's own time.
201	    func start(
202	        filter: SCContentFilter, choice: RecordingChoice, mayAsk: Bool,
203	        onFinish: @escaping (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void,
204	        completion: @escaping (Error?) -> Void
205	    ) {
206	        guard state == .idle else { return completion(RecorderError.busy) }
207	        guard choice.source != .voiceOver else {
208	            return refuse(
209	                .startFailed("A voice-over has no picture; it starts through startVoiceOver."),
210	                completion)
211	        }
212	        guard choice.source != .camera else {
213	            return refuse(
214	                .startFailed("A camera recording has no screen; it starts through startCamera."),
215	                completion)
216	        }
217	        guard RecordingGrant.screenRecordingGranted else {
218	            return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal), completion)
219	        }
220	        if choice.camera != nil {
221	            let cameraGrant = RecordingGrant.cameraStatus
222	            guard cameraGrant == .authorized else {
223	                return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(cameraGrant)), completion)
224	            }
225	        }
226	        let camera: (device: AVCaptureDevice, format: Int)?
227	        do {
228	            camera = try cameraBesideDevice(for: choice)
229	        } catch {
230	            return refuse(error as? RecorderError ?? .cameraDevice("\(error)"), completion)
231	        }
232	        var microphone: AVCaptureDevice?
233	        if let id = choice.microphone {
234	            let status = RecordingGrant.microphoneStatus
235	            guard status == .authorized else {
236	                return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.microphoneRefusal(status)), completion)
237	            }
238	            guard let device = Self.microphone(withID: id) else {
239	                return refuse(
240	                    .microphoneDevice("No microphone with the id \(id) is connected."), completion)
241	            }
242	            microphone = device
243	        }
244	        if choice.keys == .shortcuts, !RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringGranted {
245	            return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringRefusal), completion)
246	        }
247	        do {
248	            try RecordingFiles.create(choice.folder)
249	        } catch {
250	            return refuse(
251	                .startFailed(
252	                    "The recordings folder \(choice.folder.path) could not be created: "
253	                        + error.localizedDescription), completion)
254	        }
255	        let calledAt = Date()
256	        let movieURL = RecordingFiles.uniqueURL(
257	            in: choice.folder, stem: RecordingFiles.stem(at: calledAt), ext: "mov")
258	        let displayPointSize = filter.contentRect.size
259	        let scale = CGFloat(filter.pointPixelScale)
260	        let configs = RecordingConfiguration.make(
261	            choice, displayPointSize: displayPointSize, scale: scale, outputURL: movieURL)
262	        let stream = SCStream(filter: filter, configuration: configs.stream, delegate: self)
263	        let output = SCRecordingOutput(configuration: configs.output, delegate: self)
264	        do {
265	            // BEFORE `startCapture`, the header's own rule, so the first
266	            // sample lands in the file.
267	            try stream.addRecordingOutput(output)
268	        } catch {
269	            return refuse(
270	                .startFailed(
271	                    "The recording output could not be added: " + error.localizedDescription),
272	                completion)
273	        }
274	        // The cursor's capture and its segments' header (spec §11 CU-11, CU-13);
275	        // nothing runs until `launchScreen`.
276	        let cursor = CursorCapture()
277	        // Record shortcuts (CU-62): the key tap is made now, enabled with the poll.
278	        if choice.keys == .shortcuts, !cursor.makeKeyTap() {
279	            return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringRefusal), completion)
280	        }
281	        let cursorStart = Self.cursorStart(filter: filter, choice: choice, stream: configs.stream)
282	        // The frame watch rides every screen recording (CU-13): E2 for a
283	        // camera, the geometry for the cursor. Only a camera's start needs it.
284	        var watch: ScreenFrameWatch?
285	        var watchLost: String?
286	        if ScreenFrameWatchRule.attaches(camera: camera != nil, cursor: true) {
287	            let made = ScreenFrameWatch(
288	                bound: ScreenFrameWatch.bound(rate: choice.rate),
289	                onGeometry: { [weak cursor] geometry, pts in cursor?.geometry(geometry, host: pts) })
290	            do {
291	                try stream.addStreamOutput(made, type: .screen, sampleHandlerQueue: made.queue)
292	                watch = made
293	            } catch {
294	                if ScreenFrameWatchRule.failsStart(camera: camera != nil) {
295	                    return refuse(
296	                        .startFailed(
297	                            "The screen's frames could not be watched: " + error.localizedDescription),
298	                        completion)
299	                }
300	                watch = nil
301	                watchLost = error.localizedDescription
302	            }
303	        }
304	        var mic: MicrophoneCapture?
305	        if let device = microphone {
306	            do {
307	                mic = try microphoneCapture(for: device, beside: movieURL)
308	            } catch let failure as RecorderError {
309	                return refuse(failure, completion)
310	            } catch {
311	                return refuse(.microphoneDevice(error.localizedDescription), completion)
312	            }
313	        }
314	        var capture: CameraCapture?
315	        var recorded: RecordingCamera?
316	        if let camera {
317	            do {
318	                let taken = try takeCameraCapture(
319	                    device: camera.device, format: camera.format, adopting: mayAsk)
320	                capture = taken
321	                recorded = RecordingCamera(
322	                    name: camera.device.localizedName, format: CameraDevices.spelled(taken.applied))
323	            } catch {
324	                mic?.session.stopRunning()
325	                return refuse(error as? RecorderError ?? .cameraDevice("\(error)"), completion)
326	            }
327	        }
328	        microphoneProblem = nil
329	        session = Session(
330	            choice: choice, mayAsk: mayAsk, displayPointSize: displayPointSize, scale: scale,
331	            stream: stream,
332	            micSession: mic?.session, micOutput: mic?.output, calledAt: calledAt,
333	            onFinish: onFinish,
334	            segments: [
335	                Segment(movieURL: movieURL, micURL: mic?.url, output: output, addedAt: calledAt)
336	            ], cameraCapture: capture, camera: recorded, frameWatch: watch, cursor: cursor,
337	            cursorStart: cursorStart, cursorWatchLost: watchLost)
338	        state = .arming
339	        startCompletion = completion
340	        if let mic {
341	            if !mic.session.isRunning { mic.session.startRunning() }
342	            guard mic.session.isRunning else {
343	                return failStart(
344	                    RecorderError.microphoneDevice("The microphone session did not start."))
345	            }
346	        }
347	        // With a camera, its warm-up first and the launch turn on its answer
348	        // (spec §11 CAM-9 (2)); without one, the launch is this turn's.
349	        if let capture { armCameraBeside(capture) } else { launchScreen() }
350	        // The stream's own report wins over the bare ceiling (finding 5).
351	        // `.common`, the panel's rule: an open status-item menu runs the
352	        // loop in tracking mode, where a default-mode timer waits.
353	        let ceiling = Timer(timeInterval: Self.armCeiling, repeats: false) { [weak self] _ in
354	            guard let self, self.state == .arming else { return }
355	            self.failStart(self.session?.screenFailure ?? RecorderError.startTimedOut)
356	        }
357	        RunLoop.main.add(ceiling, forMode: .common)
358	        timer = ceiling
359	    }

361	    /// A refusal before the arm: nothing was made, and a microphone the
362	    /// countdown prepared is let go so the input does not stay open.
363	    private func refuse(_ error: RecorderError, _ completion: (Error?) -> Void) {
364	        discardPreparedMicrophone()
365	        completion(error)
366	    }

4	/// The microphone half of `ScreenRecorder`: the capture session that writes
5	/// the second file (R0 q2), prepared AHEAD of the recording, and the meter
6	/// that reads it. Cut out of `ScreenRecorder.swift` along the line the
7	/// header there names — the machine in one file, the device in this one —
8	/// when the preparation took the base file past the 400-line cap.
9	///
10	/// **Why prepare** (R1 review, unjudged and upheld by a −421 ms smoke run:
11	/// the first 0.4 s of voice was simply not in the file). `AVCaptureSession.
12	/// startRunning()` costs 100–400 ms on first use, and a session started
13	/// inside `start` pays it after the countdown has ended, so the microphone
14	/// is deaf for the recording's first words. `prepareMicrophone` builds the
15	/// session and starts it while the countdown still runs; `start` ADOPTS it
16	/// when its device is the choice's and builds one otherwise; a refused
17	/// start and every conclude tear it down, so an input never stays open
18	/// past the recording it was for. Never a prompt: the status is read before
19	/// `AVCaptureDeviceInput(device:)` is made, `start`'s own rule.
20	extension ScreenRecorder {
21	    /// A running session waiting for a `start` whose choice names its device.
22	    struct PreparedMicrophone {
23	        let deviceID: String
24	        let session: AVCaptureSession
25	        let output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput
26	    }
27	
28	    /// What one recording's microphone is: the session, its file output and
29	    /// the `.m4a` beside the movie.
30	    typealias MicrophoneCapture = (
31	        session: AVCaptureSession, output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput, url: URL
32	    )
33	
34	    // MARK: - Preparation
35	
36	    /// MAIN THREAD, idle only. A nil id, a status other than `.authorized`,
37	    /// an id no connected device carries, or a session that will not run
38	    /// does nothing and leaves nothing behind; the same device already
39	    /// prepared and running is kept. Blocks main for the session's start
40	    /// (100–180 ms measured, R0 q6b) — the point is to spend it now.
41	    func prepareMicrophone(_ deviceID: String?) {
42	        guard state == .idle, let id = deviceID, RecordingGrant.microphoneStatus == .authorized,
43	            let device = Self.microphone(withID: id)
44	        else { return }
45	        if let prepared = preparedMicrophone, prepared.deviceID == id, prepared.session.isRunning {
46	            return
47	        }
48	        discardPreparedMicrophone()
49	        guard let built = try? Self.microphoneSession(for: device) else { return }
50	        built.session.startRunning()
51	        guard built.session.isRunning else { return }
52	        preparedMicrophone = PreparedMicrophone(
53	            deviceID: id, session: built.session, output: built.output)
54	    }
55	
56	    /// MAIN THREAD. Stops and forgets a prepared session, if there is one.
57	    /// While IDLE it also publishes silence (#98 c), prepared or not: the
58	    /// countdown's meter read the prepared session, and a cancel, a close,
59	    /// an abandoned or refused start and `failStart` (which idles first) all
60	    /// come here, so the bar never holds a level for an input that is closed.
61	    func discardPreparedMicrophone() {
62	        preparedMicrophone?.session.stopRunning()
63	        preparedMicrophone = nil
64	        if state == .idle { meter.publish(.silent, from: ObjectIdentifier(self)) }
65	    }
66	
67	    /// `start`'s microphone: `adoptMicrophone(for:)`'s session and output,
68	    /// with the `.m4a` beside the movie.
69	    func microphoneCapture(for device: AVCaptureDevice, beside movie: URL) throws
70	        -> MicrophoneCapture
71	    {
72	        let url = RecordingFiles.microphoneURL(beside: movie)
73	        let adopted = try adoptMicrophone(for: device)
74	        return (adopted.session, adopted.output, url)
75	    }
76	
77	    /// The capture session for `device`: the prepared session when its
78	    /// device is `device` and it is still running (a device that went away
79	    /// meanwhile stops its session), else a fresh one, which the caller will
80	    /// run. Either way the prepared slot is empty afterwards — adopted, or
81	    /// discarded because it was the wrong device. `start` (through
82	    /// `microphoneCapture`) and `startVoiceOver` both take theirs here.
83	    func adoptMicrophone(for device: AVCaptureDevice) throws
84	        -> (session: AVCaptureSession, output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput)
85	    {
86	        if let prepared = preparedMicrophone, prepared.deviceID == device.uniqueID,
87	            prepared.session.isRunning
88	        {
89	            preparedMicrophone = nil
90	            return (prepared.session, prepared.output)
91	        }
92	        discardPreparedMicrophone()
93	        return try Self.microphoneSession(for: device)
94	    }
95	
96	    /// The capture session for the second file: the device's input and an
97	    /// `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput`, not yet running.
98	    private static func microphoneSession(for device: AVCaptureDevice) throws
99	        -> (session: AVCaptureSession, output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput)
100	    {
101	        let capture = AVCaptureSession()
102	        let fileOutput = AVCaptureAudioFileOutput()
103	        let input = try AVCaptureDeviceInput(device: device)
104	        guard capture.canAddInput(input), capture.canAddOutput(fileOutput) else {
105	            throw RecorderError.microphoneDevice(
106	                "The microphone \(device.localizedName) cannot be recorded from.")
107	        }
108	        capture.addInput(input)
109	        capture.addOutput(fileOutput)
110	        return (capture, fileOutput)
111	    }
112	
113	    // MARK: - The meter
114	
115	    /// MAIN THREAD, from the panel's 30 Hz timer. Reads the microphone file
116	    /// output's connection channels and publishes one reading: while
117	    /// RECORDING, the recording's output; while IDLE with a PREPARED session
118	    /// running, that session's output — the countdown's meter (#98 c: the
119	    /// connection was measured reporting levels on a running session
120	    /// before `startRecording`, 2026-09-30). A no-op — nothing published —
121	    /// idle with nothing prepared, arming, PAUSED, finishing (the pause
122	    /// published the silence), and once the LATEST segment's microphone has
123	    /// finished or failed (finding 3 published the silence then, and a dead
124	    /// connection must not light the bar again; a closed segment's state is
125	    /// not this segment's). A VOICE-OVER (`voiceSession`) is read the same
126	    /// way: its output while recording and its last segment has neither
127	    /// finished nor failed; and so is a CAMERA recording (`cameraSession`,
128	    /// spec §11 CAM-5): its microphone output while recording, until the
129	    /// latest segment's microphone finishes or reports a problem. One
130	    /// channel is reported on both sides, `LevelMeterSink`'s rule for a
131	    /// mono track (R0 q6c: the connection exposes `averagePowerLevel` and
132	    /// `peakHoldLevel` in dB on every poll, so there is no sample buffer and
133	    /// no queue in it).
134	    func publishMicrophoneLevel() {
135	        let connection: AVCaptureConnection?
136	        if state == .recording, let voice = voiceSession, let last = voice.segments.last,
137	            !last.finished, last.failure == nil
138	        {
139	            connection = voice.micOutput.connection(with: .audio)
140	        } else if state == .recording, let current = session, !current.latest.micFinished,
141	            current.latest.micFailure == nil, let output = current.micOutput
142	        {
143	            connection = output.connection(with: .audio)
144	        } else if state == .recording, let camera = cameraSession, let last = camera.segments.last,
145	            !last.micFinished, last.micProblem == nil, let output = camera.micOutput
146	        {
147	            connection = output.connection(with: .audio)
148	        } else if state == .idle, let prepared = preparedMicrophone, prepared.session.isRunning {
149	            connection = prepared.output.connection(with: .audio)
150	        } else {
151	            connection = nil
152	        }
153	        guard let connection, let first = connection.audioChannels.first else { return }
154	        let second = connection.audioChannels.count > 1 ? connection.audioChannels[1] : first
155	        meter.publish(
156	            LevelMeterReading(
157	                peakLeft: RecordingMeter.linear(fromDecibels: first.peakHoldLevel),
158	                peakRight: RecordingMeter.linear(fromDecibels: second.peakHoldLevel),
159	                rmsLeft: RecordingMeter.linear(fromDecibels: first.averagePowerLevel),
160	                rmsRight: RecordingMeter.linear(fromDecibels: second.averagePowerLevel)),
161	            from: ObjectIdentifier(self))
162	    }
163	}

4	/// A VOICE-OVER (spec §11 recording, "A voice-over is a recording with no
5	/// picture", #99): the same machine with no stream. The microphone's
6	/// `AVCaptureSession` — the one a screen recording writes its second file
7	/// with, adopted from `prepareMicrophone` when the countdown made it — writes
8	/// one `.m4a` per stretch between pauses, named `Voice-over <date> at
9	/// <time>.m4a` by the moment the stretch began, exactly as a screen
10	/// recording's segments are. `ScreenRecorder.voiceSession` is set instead of
11	/// `session`, never beside it, and `stop()`, `elapsed`, `pause()` and
12	/// `resume()` forward here when it is; `state` is the one state machine
13	/// (`idle → recording ⇄ paused → finishing → idle`, with NO arming state —
14	/// the writer's `startRecording` is the whole start), so `isRecording`,
15	/// `isPaused`, the quit guard and both doors read a voice-over as they read a
16	/// recording. This file is the start, the two transitions and the stop;
17	/// `+VoiceOverFinishing.swift` is everything the writer reports and
18	/// everything that ends one.
19	///
20	/// **One writer, a file per segment.** Its delegate is `VoiceOverFileDelegate`
21	/// rather than the recorder — the recorder's own microphone delegate
22	/// (`+Delegates.swift`) reads `session` — and each callback finds ITS
23	/// segment by the output's identity and the file URL it reports, because a
24	/// paused segment's did-finish can land after the resume has opened the
25	/// next. A resume never waits for it (the screen machine's rule, R0 q7).
26	///
27	/// **No prompt**: the microphone status is read before the session is built
28	/// (`adoptMicrophone`), and nothing here asks for a grant or reads the
29	/// Screen Recording one.
30	extension ScreenRecorder {
31	    /// Everything one voice-over owns. `segments` is never empty: the first
32	    /// is minted by `startVoiceOver`, each later one by `resumeVoiceOver`.
33	    struct VoiceSession {
34	        let choice: RecordingChoice
35	        /// Whether a segment's probe may ask the conversion question:
36	        /// false for `record_screen` (spec §11 MC-5).
37	        let mayAsk: Bool
38	        let micSession: AVCaptureSession
39	        let micOutput: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput
40	        let fileDelegate: VoiceOverFileDelegate
41	        /// Called exactly once, at conclude.
42	        let onFinish: (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void
43	        var segments: [VoiceSegment]
44	        /// Presses of Pause, stored (`RecordingResult.pauses`).
45	        var pauses = 0
46	        /// The settle has begun: one probe walk, one conclude.
47	        var settling = false
48	        /// The finishing ceiling fired before every did-finish landed.
49	        var timedOut = false
50	    }
51	
52	    /// One `.m4a`: its URL, the call that asked for it (`calledAt`, the
53	    /// fallback for a did-start that never came), the writer's did-start,
54	    /// and `stoppedAt` — a pause's or the stop's, so non-nil means its
55	    /// did-finish was ASKED for. `failure` is the writer's error when it did
56	    /// not finish well; `stoppedOnItsOwn` is set by a did-finish that came
57	    /// with `stoppedAt` nil — the writer stopped and nobody asked — and holds
58	    /// `<desc>`, that did-finish's error or "It reported no error.".
59	    struct VoiceSegment {
60	        let url: URL
61	        let calledAt: Date
62	        var startedAt: Date?
63	        var stoppedAt: Date?
64	        var finished = false
65	        var failure: String?
66	        var stoppedOnItsOwn: String?
67	
68	        init(url: URL, calledAt: Date) {
69	            self.url = url
70	            self.calledAt = calledAt
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	    static let voiceOverNeedsMicrophoneSentence =
75	        "A voice-over records the microphone alone, so it needs a microphone; none is chosen."
76	
77	    // MARK: - Start
78	
79	    /// MAIN THREAD. `completion` on main, nil on success, and always BEFORE
80	    /// this returns: there is no arming state. A refusal touches nothing —
81	    /// `.busy` not even a prepared microphone; every other refusal lets a
82	    /// prepared one go — in this order: `.busy` when not idle; a choice
83	    /// that is not `.voiceOver`; no microphone; the Microphone grant not
84	    /// `.authorized` (read, never asked); a device id nothing connected
85	    /// carries; a folder that cannot be made; a session that will not run.
86	    /// Otherwise the first segment is minted, named by this call's time,
87	    /// the state is `.recording` and the writer is asked to start; its
88	    /// did-start is stamped where it lands.
89	    func startVoiceOver(
90	        choice: RecordingChoice, mayAsk: Bool,
91	        onFinish: @escaping (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void,
92	        completion: @escaping (Error?) -> Void
93	    ) {
94	        guard state == .idle else { return completion(RecorderError.busy) }
95	        guard choice.source == .voiceOver else {
96	            return refuseVoiceOver(
97	                .startFailed("A voice-over takes the Microphone Only source; this choice names a screen."),
98	                completion)
99	        }
100	        guard let id = choice.microphone else {
101	            return refuseVoiceOver(.startFailed(Self.voiceOverNeedsMicrophoneSentence), completion)
102	        }
103	        let status = RecordingGrant.microphoneStatus
104	        guard status == .authorized else {
105	            return refuseVoiceOver(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.microphoneRefusal(status)), completion)
106	        }
107	        guard let device = Self.microphone(withID: id) else {
108	            return refuseVoiceOver(
109	                .microphoneDevice("No microphone with the id \(id) is connected."), completion)
110	        }
111	        do {
112	            try RecordingFiles.create(choice.folder)
113	        } catch {
114	            return refuseVoiceOver(
115	                .startFailed(
116	                    "The recordings folder \(choice.folder.path) could not be created: "
117	                        + error.localizedDescription), completion)
118	        }
119	        let capture: (session: AVCaptureSession, output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput)
120	        do {
121	            capture = try adoptMicrophone(for: device)
122	        } catch let failure as RecorderError {
123	            return refuseVoiceOver(failure, completion)
124	        } catch {
125	            return refuseVoiceOver(.microphoneDevice(error.localizedDescription), completion)
126	        }
127	        if !capture.session.isRunning { capture.session.startRunning() }
128	        guard capture.session.isRunning else {
129	            capture.session.stopRunning()
130	            return refuseVoiceOver(
131	                .microphoneDevice("The microphone session did not start."), completion)
132	        }
133	        microphoneProblem = nil
134	        let calledAt = Date()
135	        let url = Self.nextVoiceOverURL(in: choice.folder, at: calledAt, holding: [])
136	        let delegate = VoiceOverFileDelegate(recorder: self)
137	        voiceSession = VoiceSession(
138	            choice: choice, mayAsk: mayAsk, micSession: capture.session,
139	            micOutput: capture.output,
140	            fileDelegate: delegate, onFinish: onFinish,
141	            segments: [VoiceSegment(url: url, calledAt: calledAt)])
142	        state = .recording
143	        capture.output.startRecording(to: url, outputFileType: .m4a, recordingDelegate: delegate)
144	        completion(nil)
145	    }

147	    /// A refusal before anything was made: a prepared microphone is let go
148	    /// so the input does not stay open, `start`'s own rule.
149	    private func refuseVoiceOver(_ error: RecorderError, _ completion: (Error?) -> Void) {

156	    /// MAIN THREAD, synchronous; `pause()` forwards here. `.recording` →
157	    /// `.paused`; `.paused` throws `.alreadyPaused`, anything else
158	    /// `.notRecording`. Stamps the open segment's `stoppedAt`, counts the
159	    /// pause, asks the writer to stop (its did-finish lands on THAT segment),
160	    /// silences the meter and posts `pauseDidChangeNotification`.
161	    func pauseVoiceOver() throws {
162	        guard state != .paused else { throw RecorderError.alreadyPaused }
163	        guard state == .recording, let current = voiceSession else {
164	            throw RecorderError.notRecording
165	        }
166	        voiceSession?.segments[current.segments.count - 1].stoppedAt = Date()
167	        voiceSession?.pauses += 1
168	        current.micOutput.stopRecording()
169	        state = .paused
170	        meter.publish(.silent, from: ObjectIdentifier(self))
171	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.pauseDidChangeNotification, object: self)
172	    }

174	    /// MAIN THREAD, synchronous; `resume()` forwards here. `.paused` →
175	    /// `.recording`; anything else throws `.notPaused`. Mints the next
176	    /// segment, named by THIS moment and skipping every name the session
177	    /// holds, appends it BEFORE the writer is asked (so the callback finds
178	    /// it), and restarts the writer to it — never waiting for the paused
179	    /// segment's did-finish.
180	    func resumeVoiceOver() throws {
181	        guard state == .paused, let current = voiceSession else { throw RecorderError.notPaused }
182	        let at = Date()
183	        let url = Self.nextVoiceOverURL(
184	            in: current.choice.folder, at: at, holding: Set(current.segments.map(\.url.path)))
185	        voiceSession?.segments.append(VoiceSegment(url: url, calledAt: at))
186	        state = .recording
187	        current.micOutput.startRecording(
188	            to: url, outputFileType: .m4a, recordingDelegate: current.fileDelegate)
189	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.pauseDidChangeNotification, object: self)
190	    }

194	    /// MAIN THREAD; `stop()` forwards here while a voice-over is held.
195	    /// Idle → `.notRecording`, synchronously; recording or paused →
196	    /// finishing begins now; finishing → JOINED: the completion receives
197	    /// the one outcome beside `onFinish`, `stop()`'s own rule.
198	    func stopVoiceOver(completion: ((Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void)?) {
199	        switch state {
200	        case .idle, .arming:
201	            completion?(.failure(RecorderError.notRecording))
202	        case .recording, .paused:
203	            if let completion { stopCompletions.append(completion) }
204	            beginVoiceFinishing()
205	        case .finishing:
206	            if let completion { stopCompletions.append(completion) }
207	        }
208	    }

212	    /// Seconds recorded: each segment from its did-start (else its call) to
213	    /// its `stoppedAt` (else now), each floored at 0, so it freezes while
214	    /// paused; 0 idle.
215	    var voiceElapsed: TimeInterval {
216	        guard state != .idle, let current = voiceSession else { return 0 }
217	        let now = Date()
218	        return current.segments.reduce(0) { total, segment in
219	            total
220	                + max(
221	                    0,
222	                    (segment.stoppedAt ?? now).timeIntervalSince(
223	                        segment.startedAt ?? segment.calledAt))
224	        }
225	    }

228	    /// a camera recording's — 0 idle.

231	        if let cameraSession { return cameraSession.segments.count }

254	    /// CAM-10 (7)), in segment order — one per segment that armed a camera
255	    /// writer; empty for every other recording and idle. Apart from
256	    /// `heldFilePaths` because that list's count is the segment count the
257	    /// tool's stop wait is sized by.
258	    var heldCameraPaths: [String] {
259	        guard voiceSession == nil, cameraSession == nil else { return [] }
260	        return session?.segments.compactMap { $0.camera?.url.path } ?? []
261	    }

263	    /// The next voice-over file: `RecordingFiles.uniqueURL`'s rule —
264	    /// `<stem>.m4a`, then `<stem> (2).m4a`, `(3)`… — over the files on DISK
265	    /// and the paths in `held`, because a segment's file does not exist
266	    /// until its writer's did-start, so a pause and resume inside one second
267	    /// would otherwise mint one name twice.
268	    static func nextVoiceOverURL(in folder: URL, at date: Date, holding held: Set<String>) -> URL {
269	        let stem = RecordingFiles.voiceOverStem(at: date)
270	        let manager = FileManager.default
271	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension("m4a")
272	        var counter = 2
273	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) || held.contains(candidate.path) {
274	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
275	                .appendingPathExtension("m4a")
276	            counter += 1
277	        }
278	        return candidate
279	    }

5	/// The segment, and the two transitions that close one and open the next
6	/// (road map 3, R2a). ScreenCaptureKit has no pause — `SCStream` and
7	/// `SCRecordingOutput` carry none — and the header's one lever is
8	/// `removeRecordingOutput` ("Stops Recording if the stream is currently
9	/// recording") beside `addRecordingOutput` ("Starts Recording if stream is
10	/// already capturing"). R0 q7 measured that pair on a running stream: the
11	/// remove returns in under 0.1 ms and the removed output's did-finish
12	/// lands 5–25 ms later; the add returns in 0.2 ms and the new output's
13	/// did-start 8–10 ms later (67–78 ms for the first, after `startCapture`);
14	/// the stream never stops and keeps delivering 56–58 fps while paused, so
15	/// a pause costs what a recording costs and the system's own indicator
16	/// stays up. So a paused recording is a SEQUENCE of file pairs over ONE
17	/// stream (decision 6): `pause()` removes the segment's output and stops
18	/// the microphone's writer, `resume()` mints a segment named by ITS OWN
19	/// start time, adds a fresh output and restarts the writer to a new file
20	/// on the one running capture session. Each pair's screen-minus-microphone
21	/// offset is measured per segment (q7: −22 to +33 ms across resumes on one
22	/// host), which is why a `Segment` carries its own stamps and
23	/// `RecordingSegment` its own offset.
24	///
25	/// **A resume never waits for the paused segment's did-finish** (q7's
26	/// `immediate` row: the next output added the moment the previous is
27	/// removed is as clean as one added after a pause). That is why the
28	/// delegates (`ScreenRecorder+Delegates.swift`) find a segment by the
29	/// output's IDENTITY and by the FILE URL the microphone delegate reports,
30	/// never "the current one": the closed segment's did-finish can land after
31	/// the next has begun, and one `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput` writes every
32	/// segment's file.
33	///
34	/// **What a failed pair costs** is R1's posture, per segment, softened for
35	/// the movie (#97): a movie that will not probe LEAVES ITS SEGMENT OUT
36	/// (`settle`, naming its kept files in `RecordingResult.unreadable`), as
37	/// does a CLOSED segment whose output reports a did-FAIL after its stop
38	/// (#181: its `outputFailure`, left out unprobed with the writer's
39	/// sentence); only a recording with no readable movie fails, and only the
40	/// OPEN segment's did-fail is the recording's; a microphone file that
41	/// will not probe is that segment's `micProblem`, and `resume()` asks the
42	/// writer to record the next segment regardless — each is judged on its
43	/// own file (q7: one poisoned writer failed every restarted file, and
44	/// another day's did not).
45	///
46	/// **Two limits the R2 review named, and what became of them.** A pause
47	/// inside the ~10 ms between a resume's add and its output's did-start
48	/// closes a file the writer may not have opened; that empty segment is now
49	/// left out and named rather than failing the recording (#97). And a
50	/// microphone `startRecording` followed by `stopRecording` before its first
51	/// sample answers −11805 with NO file (measured); that did-finish was ASKED
52	/// for, so it is that segment's `micProblem` alone and no longer the
53	/// session's `microphoneProblem` (#97) — every other segment's voice lands.

300	        held.formUnion(session.segments.compactMap { $0.camera?.url.path })
301	        let manager = FileManager.default
302	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension("mov")
303	        var counter = 2
304	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) || held.contains(candidate.path)
305	            || held.contains(RecordingFiles.microphoneURL(beside: candidate).path)
306	            || held.contains(RecordingFiles.cameraURL(beside: candidate).path)
307	        {
308	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
309	                .appendingPathExtension("mov")
310	            counter += 1
311	        }
312	        return candidate
313	    }
314	}

4	/// A camera BESIDE the screen (camera-recording CR3a, spec §11 CAM-9): a
5	/// screen recording — a display, a window or a picked source — whose choice
6	/// names a camera records it too, one `<movie stem> (Camera).mov` per
7	/// segment, written by `CameraCapture` (one `AVAssetWriter` per segment on
8	/// one running session, CAM-3) and paused and resumed with the screen's
9	/// output. This file is the camera's lookup, its arming, the one launch turn,
10	/// each writer's open and close, the capture's reports and the camera that
11	/// stops on its own; `+CameraBesideFinishing.swift` is each landed segment's
12	/// camera half and the offset; `ScreenFrameWatch.swift` is E2.
13	///
14	/// **The warm-up comes before the stream** (CAM-9 (2)). The recorder stays
15	/// `.arming` while the capture starts or joins its prepared start, so CAM-3's
16	/// warm-up is spent before the screen begins; on its answer ONE main turn,
17	/// `launchScreen`, starts the microphone's file, the stream and segment 0's
18	/// camera writer (CR0: the order of the starts made no measurable
19	/// difference). A start without a camera calls `launchScreen` in its own
20	/// turn, so road map 3's order is unchanged.
21	///
22	/// **A camera failure is never the recording's** (CAM-9 (7)): a camera that
23	/// stops on its own while recording or paused is the result's
24	/// `camera.problem`, its open writer closed and no later segment given one;
25	/// only while arming does it fail the start. Every report hops to main (the
26	/// capture does it) and finds its segment by the camera file's URL, never
27	/// "the current one".
28	extension ScreenRecorder {
29	    /// One segment's camera writer and the stamps its offset is read from:
30	    /// the first buffer's arrival and its PTS on the host clock (CAM-3); the
31	    /// screen's did-start on the host clock (E1) and the first complete frame
32	    /// at or after it (E2, `ScreenFrameWatch`); and the writer's close —
33	    /// `finished` once it answered, `wrote` false for a writer that took no
34	    /// buffer (its file removed), `failure` a writer that did not complete;
35	    /// `watchFailure`, the frame watch's re-add at this segment's resume
36	    /// that threw (CAM-9 (6)), so E1 places it.
37	    struct CameraBesideSegment {
38	        let url: URL
39	        var startedAt: Date?
40	        var pts: Double?
41	        var screenHost: Double?
42	        var firstFrame: Double?
43	        var finished = false
44	        var wrote = false
45	        var failure: String?
46	        var watchFailure: String?
47	    }
48	
49	    // MARK: - The start
50	
51	    /// `start`'s camera, after the Camera grant was read: nil without
52	    /// `choice.camera`; else the connected device that id names and its
53	    /// format (`chosenFormat`, CAM-6 (3)). Throws `.cameraDevice` for an id no
54	    /// connected camera carries or a camera that lists no format.
55	    func cameraBesideDevice(for choice: RecordingChoice) throws
56	        -> (device: AVCaptureDevice, format: Int)?
57	    {
58	        guard let id = choice.camera else { return nil }
59	        guard let device = CameraDevices.device(withID: id) else {
60	            throw RecorderError.cameraDevice("No camera with the id \(id) is connected.")
61	        }
62	        let facts = CameraDevices.facts(of: device)
63	        guard
64	            let format = CameraDevices.chosenFormat(
65	                choice.cameraFormat, in: facts.formats, active: facts.activeFormat)
66	        else {
67	            throw RecorderError.cameraDevice("The camera \(device.localizedName) lists no format.")
68	        }
69	        return (device, format)
70	    }
71	
72	    /// MAIN THREAD, while `.arming`: the capture's reports installed, then
73	    /// the capture started (or its prepared start joined,
74	    /// `startCameraCapture`). Its answer is the launch turn, or — a capture
75	    /// that did not start — the start's failure.
76	    func armCameraBeside(_ capture: CameraCapture) {
77	        capture.onSegmentStarted = { [weak self, weak capture] url, pts, arrived in
78	            guard let self, let capture, let current = self.session,
79	                current.cameraCapture === capture,
80	                let index = current.segments.firstIndex(where: { $0.camera?.url.path == url.path }),
81	                current.segments[index].camera?.startedAt == nil
82	            else { return }
83	            self.session?.segments[index].camera?.startedAt = arrived
84	            self.session?.segments[index].camera?.pts = pts.isFinite ? pts : nil
85	        }
86	        capture.onStoppedOnItsOwn = { [weak self, weak capture] sentence in
87	            guard let self, let capture, self.session?.cameraCapture === capture else { return }
88	            self.cameraBesideStoppedOnItsOwn(sentence)
89	        }
90	        startCameraCapture(capture) { [weak self, weak capture] error in
91	            guard let self, let capture, self.state == .arming,
92	                self.session?.cameraCapture === capture
93	            else { return }
94	            if let error {
95	                return self.failStart(
96	                    error as? RecorderError ?? .cameraDevice(error.localizedDescription))
97	            }
98	            self.session?.camera?.note = capture.warmUp?.note
99	            self.launchScreen()
100	        }
101	    }
102	
103	    /// MAIN THREAD, `.arming`: the one launch turn (CAM-9 (2)) — the
104	    /// microphone's file (when one was chosen), then the cursor's capture
105	    /// with segment 0 open (spec §11 CU-11), then the stream, then
106	    /// segment 0's camera writer (none without a camera). `startCapture`'s
107	    /// completion is `captureStarted`'s, which leaves `.arming`.
108	    func launchScreen() {
109	        guard state == .arming, let current = session else { return }
110	        if let micOutput = current.micOutput, let micURL = current.segments[0].micURL {
111	            session?.segments[0].micRecordingCalledAt = Date()
112	            micOutput.startRecording(to: micURL, outputFileType: .m4a, recordingDelegate: self)
113	        }
114	        startCursorCapture()
115	        let stream = current.stream
116	        stream.startCapture { [weak self] error in
117	            let at = Date()
118	            DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.captureStarted(stream, error: error, at: at) }
119	        }
120	        openCameraBeside(at: 0)
121	    }
122	
123	    // MARK: - The writers
124	
125	    /// MAIN THREAD. Arms segment `index`'s camera writer beside its movie
126	    /// (`cameraURL(beside:)`, CAM-9 (5)); nothing without a camera, once it
127	    /// stopped on its own, or for a segment that has one.
128	    func openCameraBeside(at index: Int) {
129	        guard let current = session, let capture = current.cameraCapture,
130	            current.camera?.problem == nil, current.segments.indices.contains(index),
131	            current.segments[index].camera == nil
132	        else { return }
133	        let url = RecordingFiles.cameraURL(beside: current.segments[index].movieURL)
134	        session?.segments[index].camera = CameraBesideSegment(url: url)
135	        capture.beginSegment(url)
136	    }
137	
138	    /// MAIN THREAD. Asks segment `index`'s writer to close; its answer lands
139	    /// on that segment by the file's URL. Called only where the writer is
140	    /// open — a pause, the finishing from `.recording`, a camera that stopped
141	    /// on its own while recording (before its `problem` is set) — so a
142	    /// writer is never asked twice.
143	    func closeCameraBeside(at index: Int) {
144	        guard let current = session, let capture = current.cameraCapture,
145	            current.camera?.problem == nil, current.segments.indices.contains(index),
146	            let camera = current.segments[index].camera, !camera.finished
147	        else { return }
148	        let url = camera.url
149	        capture.endSegment { [weak self, weak capture] wrote, failure in
150	            guard let self, let capture, let current = self.session,
151	                current.cameraCapture === capture,
152	                let found = current.segments.firstIndex(where: { $0.camera?.url.path == url.path })
153	            else { return }
154	            self.session?.segments[found].camera?.finished = true
155	            self.session?.segments[found].camera?.wrote = wrote
156	            self.session?.segments[found].camera?.failure = failure
157	            self.checkFinished()
158	        }
159	    }
160	
161	    /// `failStart`'s camera (CAM-9 (8)): the watch stopped, segment 0's
162	    /// writer closed — its file removed unless the screen output had begun
163	    /// writing — and the capture stopped.
164	    func tearDownCameraBeside(_ current: Session) {
165	        current.frameWatch?.stop()
166	        guard let capture = current.cameraCapture else { return }
167	        if let camera = current.segments[0].camera, !camera.finished {
168	            let keep = current.segments[0].screenStartedAt != nil
169	            capture.endSegment { _, _ in
170	                if !keep { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: camera.url) }
171	            }
172	        }
173	        capture.stop()
174	    }
175	
176	    // MARK: - The reports
177	
178	    /// MAIN THREAD. Segment `index`'s screen did-start arrived at `host` on
179	    /// the host clock (E1): stamped on its camera, and the watch asked for
180	    /// E2 (CAM-9 (3)), whose answer finds the segment by its output — not
181	    /// when the watch could not go back on the stream at its resume (E1).
182	    func screenDidStart(at index: Int, host: Double) {
183	        guard let current = session, let watch = current.frameWatch,
184	            current.segments.indices.contains(index), current.segments[index].camera != nil
185	        else { return }
186	        session?.segments[index].camera?.screenHost = host
187	        guard current.segments[index].camera?.watchFailure == nil else { return }
188	        let output = current.segments[index].output
189	        watch.firstComplete(for: index, atOrAfter: host) { [weak self] pts in
190	            guard let self, let found = self.session?.index(of: output) else { return }
191	            self.session?.segments[found].camera?.firstFrame = pts
192	        }
193	    }
194	
195	    /// The camera stopped on its own (CAM-9 (7)): while arming the start
196	    /// fails with its sentence; while recording or paused it is the
197	    /// result's `camera.problem`, once — the open writer closed first, so
198	    /// what it wrote lands, the capture let go, and no later segment armed —
199	    /// and the screen records on.
200	    func cameraBesideStoppedOnItsOwn(_ sentence: String) {
201	        switch state {
202	        case .arming:
203	            failStart(.cameraDevice(sentence))
204	        case .recording, .paused:
205	            guard let current = session, current.camera?.problem == nil else { return }
206	            if state == .recording { closeCameraBeside(at: current.lastIndex) }
207	            session?.camera?.problem = sentence
208	            current.cameraCapture?.stop()
209	        case .idle, .finishing:
210	            break
211	        }
212	    }
213	}

2	// remainder landing (camera-recording CR3-0): `remainderPlacement`

4	// its undo step can take (`microphoneActionName`, `segmentsActionName`, and
5	// since CR3b `cameraActionName` and `cameraMicrophoneActionName`),

7	// `unplacedNote`, the sentence for a file with no first
8	// clip to follow. A PURE MOVE out of `RecordingLanding+Microphone.swift` at
9	// the 400-line cap, landed alone before camera + screen grows it;
10	// `unplacedNote` stays `private`, because nothing else calls it. The voices
11	// it lands are `+Microphone`'s `addMicrophones`, its cameras `+Camera`'s
12	// `addCameras`, its stretches `+LeftOut`'s `remainderStretches`. Since road
13	// map creator-jobs CU3c (spec §11 CU-31 (c)) the remainder also carries the
14	// ripples a Separate recording with Show Clicks lands its screen clips with
15	// (`+Cursor`'s `addRipples`), and is named `ripplesActionName` when they are

18	import AppKit
19	
20	extension RecordingLanding {
21	    /// The undo step's name for `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`'s
22	    /// remainder edit when the remainder is a microphone ALONE — one segment
23	    /// with a voice. There the picture is the document — undoing the step
24	    /// removes the voice and keeps the picture — so a step called "Add
25	    /// Recording" would promise to take back what it cannot, and the Edit
26	    /// menu would read "Undo Add Recording" over a project the undo leaves
27	    /// with the recording in it. The `.document` landing keeps `actionName`:
28	    /// its one step really does add and remove both.
29	    static let microphoneActionName = "Add Microphone"
30	
31	    /// The same step's name when the remainder holds more than a voice — a
32	    /// paused recording's later segments, with or without microphones.
33	    /// "Segments" and not "Recording" for the reason above: the FIRST
34	    /// segment is the document and stays under the undo; what the step takes
35	    /// back is the rest.
36	    static let segmentsActionName = "Add Recording Segments"
37	
38	    /// The same step's name for ONE segment whose remainder is its camera
39	    /// beside the screen (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)): the picture is the
40	    /// document, and the step takes the camera back.
41	    static let cameraActionName = "Add Camera"
42	
43	    /// …and for ONE segment whose remainder is its camera and a voice.
44	    static let cameraMicrophoneActionName = "Add Camera and Microphone"
45	
46	    /// Which name `untitled(around:)`'s remainder edit takes. For ONE
47	    /// segment: with a camera beside the screen, "Add Camera and
48	    /// Microphone" when there is any voice and "Add Camera" when there is
49	    /// not (CAM-10 (4)); without one, "Add Microphone" for any voice — its
50	    /// own (R1's landing, R1's name) or a left-out segment's. With neither,
51	    /// the remainder can only be its ripples (CU-31 (c)): "Cursor Clicks".
52	    /// "Add Recording Segments" otherwise. A one-segment recording with no
53	    /// voice, no camera and no ripples has no remainder and no step, and the
54	    /// answer for it is never read.
55	    static func remainderActionName(for result: RecordingResult) -> String {
56	        if result.segments.count == 1 {
57	            let voice =
58	                result.segments[0].micDescriptor != nil
59	                || result.unreadable.contains(where: { $0.micDescriptor != nil })
60	            if result.segments[0].cameraDescriptor != nil {
61	                return voice ? cameraMicrophoneActionName : cameraActionName
62	            }
63	            if voice { return microphoneActionName }
64	            return ripplesActionName
65	        }
66	        return segmentsActionName
67	    }
68	
69	    /// Everything a fresh untitled document does NOT already hold, for
70	    /// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, whose `makeProject` placed the
71	    /// FIRST segment's picture at 0 on track 1 before anything else could
72	    /// run: segments 2…n's media and their pictures on that same track from
73	    /// clip 1's end, then every segment's microphone by the floor rule. nil
74	    /// when there is nothing to add — one segment, no microphone, no camera
75	    /// and no ripples (`wantsRipples` with a cursor not in the picture, CU-31).
76	    /// `placement(_:in:place:)` cannot serve it — the first picture's
77	    /// `add_media` would be the documented identity and its `add_clip` at 0
78	    /// would meet its own clip on the front track, refuse, and put the whole
79	    /// sequence a SECOND time on a new track. The answer reads as a whole
80	    /// landing: `mediaIds[0]` and `clipIds[0]` name the picture the document
81	    /// holds.
82	    ///
83	    /// Clip 1 is the FIRST clip whose source is the first segment's media,
84	    /// and the later pictures go on ITS track from ITS end — read off the
85	    /// document, not assumed to be track 1 at 0. That is exact for the one
86	    /// caller: `makeProject` places exactly one clip. A document holding the
87	    /// same media in several clips has no single answer here, and this
88	    /// method does not pretend to one — it is `untitled(around:)`'s, not a
89	    /// general "add the rest of a recording to a document" op. The later
90	    /// pictures take no two-try rule: a refusal on a fresh document's one
91	    /// track is not a track choice to fall back from but something wrong
92	    /// with a file, and is thrown by name.
93	    ///
94	    /// **Without clip 1** — `makeProject` tolerates a first picture the core
95	    /// refuses (a media with no duration) and opens the file in the Media
96	    /// tab — nothing on the timeline says where the recording is, so the
97	    /// remainder lands as MEDIA ONLY, `place: false`'s shape, with a
98	    /// sentence per file in `notes`. The first shape here placed every
99	    /// voice against a picture at 0, R1's one-segment fallback, which with
100	    /// several voices stacked each one under the last (the floor rule
101	    /// trimming a whole voice off) — a wrong sound where a Media-tab list
102	    /// is at least an honest one.
103	    ///
104	    /// **A left-out segment's readable voice** (#181 item 2) is a stretch:
105	    /// after clip 1 a gap the later pictures skip and a voice at its start;
106	    /// BEFORE clip 1, which is the document at 0, media only with
107	    /// `leadingVoiceNote`; without clip 1, media only with `unplacedNote`.
108	    ///
109	    /// **A camera beside the screen** (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)) lands after the
110	    /// later pictures and before the voices, by `addCameras` against each
111	    /// segment's picture start — clip 1's included — on ONE new track in
112	    /// front of the pictures', laid out with its segment's picture; without
113	    /// clip 1, as media only with
114	    /// `unplacedNote`.
115	    ///
116	    /// **The ripples** (CU-31 (c)) go on clip 1 and the later pictures right
117	    /// after those are placed (`addRipples`); without clip 1 there are none.
118	    static func remainderPlacement(
119	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
120	    ) throws -> Placement? {
121	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
122	        let hasMicrophone = result.segments.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
123	        let hasLeftOutVoice = result.unreadable.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
124	        let hasCamera = result.segments.contains { $0.cameraDescriptor != nil }
125	        let more = result.segments.count > 1 || hasMicrophone || hasLeftOutVoice || hasCamera
126	        guard more || wantsRipples(result) else { return nil }
127	        let path = trimmed(result.descriptor.path)
128	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
129	        guard let mediaId = snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
130	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) is not in the document's media list.")
131	        }
132	        let first = snapshot.clips.first { clip in
133	            if case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source { return id == mediaId }
134	            return false
135	        }
136	        let scope = document.scope
137	        var trial = document.project
138	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
139	        var notes: [String] = []
140	        var mediaIds = [mediaId]
141	        for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
142	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
143	        }
144	        var starts: [Ticks?]?
145	        var clips: [UInt32?] = result.stretches.map { _ in nil }
146	        if let first = first {
147	            let placed = try remainderStretches(
148	                result, after: first, mediaIds: mediaIds, firstPath: path, scope: scope,
149	                to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
150	            starts = placed.starts
151	            clips = placed.clips
152	            try addRipples(
153	                clips.compactMap { $0 }, of: result, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
154	        } else {
155	            for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
156	                notes.append(unplacedNote(segment.descriptor.path, behind: path))
157	            }
158	            for segment in result.segments {
159	                if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
160	                    notes.append(unplacedNote(camera.path, behind: path))
161	                }
162	            }
163	            for segment in result.segments {
164	                if let mic = segment.micDescriptor { notes.append(unplacedNote(mic.path, behind: path)) }
165	            }
166	            for left in result.unreadable {
167	                if let mic = left.micDescriptor { notes.append(unplacedNote(mic.path, behind: path)) }
168	            }
169	        }
170	        let cameras = try addCameras(
171	            result, screenStarts: starts.map { segmentStarts($0, of: result) },
172	            screenClips: split(clips, of: result).segments, scope: scope,
173	            to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
174	        let microphones = try addMicrophones(
175	            voices(of: result), pictureStarts: starts,
176	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
177	        // Let in by the ripples alone, and no clip took one: nothing to add.
178	        guard more || !ops.isEmpty else { return nil }
179	        let micMedia = split(microphones.media, of: result)
180	        let micClips = split(microphones.clips, of: result)
181	        return Placement(
182	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds, clipIds: split(clips, of: result).segments,
183	            micMediaIds: micMedia.segments, micClipIds: micClips.segments, notes: notes,
184	            leftOutMicMediaIds: micMedia.leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: micClips.leftOut,
185	            cameraMediaIds: cameras.media, cameraClipIds: cameras.clips)
186	    }
187	
188	    /// The sentence for a file `remainderPlacement` lands as media because
189	    /// the first segment's picture has no clip to follow.
190	    private static func unplacedNote(_ path: String, behind first: String) -> String {
191	        "\(path) was added to the media list without a clip: \(first) has no clip on the "
192	            + "timeline for it to follow."
193	    }
194	}

1	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding+LeftOut.swift — a left-out segment's readable
2	// microphone in the landing (#181 item 2, spec §11 recording: "A left-out
3	// segment's readable microphone lands without its picture").
4	//
5	// A segment the walker left out (`RecordingResult.unreadable`) whose
6	// microphone file read carries it as `micDescriptor`, with `position` its
7	// place among the landed segments; `RecordingResult.stretches` lists the
8	// landed segments and those voices in recording order. Here is what the
9	// landing makes of that list: the PICTURE side as `PictureStretch`es — a
10	// landed segment's media, or a GAP the length of the voice snapped down to
11	// the frame, so the picture track stays empty there and the next picture
12	// starts at the slot's end — and the MICROPHONE side as `Voice`s, one per
13	// stretch, a voice-only one at offset 0 because no picture is there to align
14	// it to. `split` maps a per-stretch answer back to the `Placement`'s
15	// per-segment lists and its per-left-out-segment lists; `remainderStretches`
16	// is `remainderPlacement`'s clip-1 branch over the same list. With no
17	// left-out voice every stretch is a segment and every list is the one it was.
18	//
19	// In its own file because `RecordingLanding+Microphone.swift` stood at 381
20	// lines against the 400-line cap for a new file; `view` and `trimmed` are
21	// the base file's, internal for it.

23	import AppKit
24	
25	extension RecordingLanding {
26	    /// One stretch of the picture track: a landed segment's media, placed
27	    /// by `placeBackToBack`, or a gap of `Ticks` it leaves empty.
28	    enum PictureStretch {
29	        case picture(UInt32)
30	        case gap(Ticks)
31	    }
32	
33	    /// One stretch's microphone: its file when one landed (nil when none),
34	    /// and the offset its clip is placed by — a segment's measured
35	    /// `micOffset`, or 0 for a left-out voice.
36	    struct Voice {
37	        let descriptor: MediaDescriptor?
38	        let offset: Ticks
39	    }
40	
41	    /// One `Voice` per stretch of `result`, in order.
42	    static func voices(of result: RecordingResult) -> [Voice] {
43	        result.stretches.map { stretch in
44	            switch stretch {
45	            case .segment(let k):
46	                return Voice(
47	                    descriptor: result.segments[k].micDescriptor,
48	                    offset: result.segments[k].micOffset)
49	            case .voiceOnly(let i):
50	                return Voice(descriptor: result.unreadable[i].micDescriptor, offset: 0)
51	            }
52	        }
53	    }
54	
55	    /// One `PictureStretch` per stretch of `result`: segment `k`'s picture
56	    /// as `mediaIds[k]` (the ids its `add_media` answered, one per segment),
57	    /// and a left-out voice as a gap of `slotLength`, measured against the
58	    /// container `trial` and `scope` name.
59	    static func pictureStretches(
60	        of result: RecordingResult, mediaIds: [UInt32], in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?
61	    ) throws -> [PictureStretch] {
62	        try result.stretches.map { stretch in
63	            switch stretch {
64	            case .segment(let k):
65	                return .picture(mediaIds[k])
66	            case .voiceOnly(let i):
67	                guard let voice = result.unreadable[i].micDescriptor else { return .gap(0) }
68	                return .gap(try slotLength(voice, in: trial, scope: scope))
69	            }
70	        }
71	    }
72	
73	    /// The slot a voice-only stretch takes on the picture track: the file's
74	    /// length snapped DOWN to the container's frame — the length its clip
75	    /// takes (`SilenceDetector.snapDownToFrame`, the one Swift spelling of
76	    /// that snap, `rc_time_snap_to_frame` over the FFI) — and 0 for a file
77	    /// under a frame, which mints no clip and so takes no time.
78	    static func slotLength(_ voice: MediaDescriptor, in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws
79	        -> Ticks
80	    {
81	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
82	        return max(0, SilenceDetector.snapDownToFrame(voice.duration, fps: fps))
83	    }
84	
85	    /// A per-stretch list, `result.stretches`' order, split into one entry
86	    /// per landed segment and one per left-out segment (nil for a left-out
87	    /// segment with no voice, which has no stretch).
88	    static func split(_ list: [UInt32?], of result: RecordingResult)
89	        -> (segments: [UInt32?], leftOut: [UInt32?])
90	    {
91	        var segments: [UInt32?] = result.segments.map { _ in nil }
92	        var leftOut: [UInt32?] = result.unreadable.map { _ in nil }
93	        for (stretch, id) in zip(result.stretches, list) {
94	            switch stretch {
95	            case .segment(let k): segments[k] = id
96	            case .voiceOnly(let i): leftOut[i] = id
97	            }
98	        }
99	        return (segments, leftOut)
100	    }
101	
102	    /// `remainderPlacement`'s clip-1 branch over the stretches: a left-out
103	    /// voice BEFORE clip 1 — the document at 0 — gets no start (media only)
104	    /// and `leadingVoiceNote`; clip 1 is its own stretch; everything after
105	    /// it goes on clip 1's track from clip 1's end by `placeBackToBack`, a
106	    /// voice's gap included, a refusal thrown by name (no two-try rule on a
107	    /// fresh document's one track). Answers one start and one picture clip
108	    /// id per stretch, for `addMicrophones` and `split`.
109	    static func remainderStretches(
110	        _ result: RecordingResult, after first: ClipSnapshot, mediaIds: [UInt32],
111	        firstPath: String, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp],
112	        notes: inout [String]
113	    ) throws -> (starts: [Ticks?], clips: [UInt32?]) {
114	        let stretches = result.stretches
115	        let lead = stretches.firstIndex(of: .segment(0)) ?? 0
116	        var starts: [Ticks?] = stretches.map { _ in nil }
117	        var clips: [UInt32?] = stretches.map { _ in nil }
118	        for case .voiceOnly(let i) in stretches[..<lead] {
119	            if let mic = result.unreadable[i].micDescriptor {
120	                notes.append(leadingVoiceNote(mic.path, before: firstPath))
121	            }
122	        }
123	        starts[lead] = first.start
124	        clips[lead] = first.id
125	        let rest = Array(
126	            try pictureStretches(of: result, mediaIds: mediaIds, in: trial, scope: scope)[
127	                (lead + 1)...])
128	        guard !rest.isEmpty else { return (starts, clips) }
129	        guard
130	            let placed = try placeBackToBack(
131	                rest, on: first.track, from: first.end, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops,
132	                notes: &notes)
133	        else {
134	            throw ReelCoreError(
135	                message: "The recording's later segments could not be placed after its first.")
136	        }
137	        for (k, landed) in placed.enumerated() {
138	            starts[lead + 1 + k] = landed.at
139	            clips[lead + 1 + k] = landed.clip?.id
140	        }
141	        return (starts, clips)
142	    }
143	
144	    /// The sentence for a left-out voice recorded BEFORE a new project's
145	    /// first segment, which is the document at 0: there is no timeline
146	    /// before it, so the voice lands as media only.
147	    static func leadingVoiceNote(_ path: String, before first: String) -> String {
148	        "\(path) was added to the media list without a clip: it was recorded before \(first), "
149	            + "which starts the new project at 0."
150	    }
151	}

1	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding.swift — where a finished recording goes
2	// (road map 3, phase R1b; a SEQUENCE of segments since R2b).
3	//
4	// A value type, `AudioNormalize`'s shape: a `RecordingResult` and a document
5	// in, an op list and the ids it will mint out, so the recorder panel and the
6	// `record_screen` tool provably land a recording the same way. **Nothing here
7	// commits.** The panel commits through `document.performGroupedEdit`, the
8	// tool through `AgentServer.performGroupedEdit`, and each door keeps its own
9	// posture on a refusal — a sheet, or an in-band error — which a document-side
10	// commit would collapse into the wrong one for the tool.
11	//
12	// A recording is a sequence of segments (road map 3, decision 6: a pause
13	// closes one file and a resume opens the next over the one stream), and the
14	// landing places them back to back — one clip per segment, each at the
15	// previous one's END as the core reports it — so a paused recording is `n`
16	// ordinary media files and `n` clips on ONE track, touching, and the model
17	// learns nothing. An unpaused recording is the one-segment case of the same
18	// list, byte for byte R1's.
19	//
20	// **Every clip is READ BACK after its apply**, never assumed (the R2
21	// review): the core snaps a start to the frame grid, and at an inexact
22	// canvas rate — decision 3's 24981/1000, a document opened from a
23	// recording — a clip's end is a sum of two grid points, which is NOT a grid
24	// point, so an `add_clip` at it can snap DOWN by up to half a frame into a
25	// one-tick overlap the rule accepts and a cross dissolve minted between two
26	// halves of one recording. `placeClip` reads the landed start and, when it is
27	// under the floor, places again a frame up; the rule is **touching, or a
28	// sub-frame gap at an inexact rate — never an overlap, never a transition**,
29	// and the gap is the documented limit of such a rate. A file the core would
30	// refuse outright — one whose length snaps to no frame at all — lands as
31	// MEDIA with a sentence in `Placement.notes`, rather than taking every other
32	// segment down with it.
33	//
34	// The ops come back UNSCOPED. Inside an open nest the caller's door stamps the
35	// scope (`ProjectDocument.addressed`, `AgentServer+Scope.addressed`): every
36	// `add_media` op is document-level and travels unscoped, everything else
37	// carries the nest, and that is exactly what the trial below applies — so the
38	// commit runs the list the trial ran.
39	//
40	// The microphone half — each segment's voice on ONE new back track, the
41	// floor rule that keeps two voices from overlapping, the names its track and
42	// its undo steps carry, and `untitled(around:)`'s remainder landing — is
43	// `RecordingLanding+Microphone.swift`, a pure move landed alone at the
44	// 400-line cap (road map 3, R2's toll) before it grew, and the placing of
45	// one clip on the grid — `placeBackToBack`, `placeClip`, `tooShortNote`,
46	// `mediaEntry`, `milliseconds` — is `RecordingLanding+Placing.swift`, the
47	// same toll paid again when the read-backs arrived. `addMedia`, `view`,
48	// `clip(_:in:scope:)` and `trimmed` are internal for them, because
49	// `private` does not cross a file. A VOICE-OVER's landing — every file on one
50	// new back Microphone track — is `RecordingLanding+VoiceOver.swift`. The same
51	// toll paid twice more at camera-recording CR3-0 moved `Placement` and
52	// `Landed` to `RecordingLanding+Placement.swift`, and `untitled(around:)`'s
53	// remainder and its undo steps' names to `RecordingLanding+Remainder.swift`.
54	// A camera beside the screen (spec §11 CAM-10) — its media, ONE front track
55	// named "Camera", each clip by its segment's offset and the recorder's layout — is
56	// `RecordingLanding+Camera.swift`, called between the pictures and the
57	// microphones. The ripples a Separate recording with Show Clicks lands its
58	// screen clips with (road map creator-jobs CU3c, spec §11 CU-31 (c)) are
59	// `RecordingLanding+Cursor.swift`'s `addRipples`, called right after the
60	// pictures.
