62	import AppKit
63	
64	struct RecordingLanding {
65	    enum Target {
66	        case document(ProjectDocument)
67	        case newProject
68	    }
69	
70	    /// The undo step's name, for both doors — the whole landing, every
71	    /// picture and every microphone in one list.
72	    static let actionName = "Add Recording"
73	
74	    // MARK: - Where
75	
76	    /// The document a `.document(recipeKey:)` destination names, looked up
77	    /// among the open documents by `recipeKey` — minted by
78	    /// `RecipeSource.register()`, monotonic and never reused, so a document
79	    /// that closed mid-recording is a lookup that fails and not a dangling
80	    /// pointer or (the `ObjectIdentifier` trap `RelinkSheetController`
81	    /// records) the next document allocated at the same address. A miss, and
82	    /// `.newProject`, both answer `.newProject`. Main thread.
83	    static func resolve(_ destination: RecordingDestination) -> Target {
84	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
85	        guard case .document(let key) = destination else { return .newProject }
86	        let open = NSDocumentController.shared.documents.compactMap { $0 as? ProjectDocument }
87	        guard let document = open.first(where: { $0.recipeKey == key }) else {
88	            return .newProject
89	        }
90	        return .document(document)
91	    }
92	
93	    // MARK: - What
94	
95	    /// PURE: the op list and the predicted ids for landing `result` in
96	    /// `document` at its playhead, in the container it has open — every
97	    /// segment, as ONE grouped edit.
98	    ///
99	    /// Each segment's picture media goes in first, in order, applied purely
100	    /// against the DOCUMENT's handle (`add_media` is document-level,
101	    /// `ReelOp.documentLevelNames`) and its id read off the result; then,
102	    /// with `place`, the pictures as a sequence on ONE track by the two-try
103	    /// track rule — all of them on the front track of the open container if
104	    /// the core accepts every one there, else all on a new track in front of
105	    /// everything (`addSequence`). The rule is `addGeneratedClip`'s
106	    /// (`EditorViewController+AddClips.swift`) but it cannot be that method:
107	    /// its probe runs against a project that does not hold the media yet,
108	    /// and `add_clip` naming an absent media is an `Err` — every recording
109	    /// would fall to the new-track branch, and the branch would then name
110	    /// the TRACK by the id `add_media` had consumed. `placeImageBackground`
111	    /// / `backgroundMedia(for:in:)` are the precedent: the probe runs over a
112	    /// project that already HOLDS the media.
113	    ///
114	    /// With microphone files the second half — each one's media, ONE new
115	    /// BACK track named "Microphone", each one's clip — is derived from the
116	    /// pictures' purely-applied result, never from one `next_id` read,
117	    /// because the pictures mint `n` or `n + 1` ids and which depends on the
118	    /// branch the track rule took. `place == false` lands every media (the
119	    /// microphones' included) with no clip at all.
120	    ///
121	    /// **A camera beside the screen** (spec §11 CAM-10) lands between the
122	    /// two: each segment's `(Camera).mov` as media, then — with `place` —
123	    /// ONE new FRONT track named "Camera" and each camera clip at its screen
124	    /// segment's start plus its `cameraOffset`, laid out (`addCameras`).
125	    /// The pictures → cameras → microphones order is the one grouped edit's.
126	    ///
127	    /// **A left-out segment's readable voice** (#181 item 2, spec §11
128	    /// recording) is a stretch of its own (`RecordingResult.stretches`): on
129	    /// the picture side a GAP of its slot's length (`pictureStretches`), so
130	    /// the pictures after it start at the slot's end, and on the microphone
131	    /// side a voice at offset 0 at the slot's start, by the same floor rule
132	    /// (`voices(of:)`); `split` reads the answers back per segment and per
133	    /// left-out segment. With no left-out voice the list is the segments.
134	    ///
135	    /// The playhead is nest-local while a nest is open, the ops are unscoped,
136	    /// and the trial stamps the document's scope on the container ops exactly
137	    /// as the commit will. Two refusals are thrown by name rather than
138	    /// answered with a list that would beep: a live gesture (the caller
139	    /// retries when it ends, rather than committing over the gesture's base
140	    /// handle) and anything the core refuses, with the core's own sentence.
141	    ///
142	    /// **The trial sees everything the commit will, the caps included.**
143	    /// Each scoped op is applied to the PARENT handle —
144	    /// `trial.applying(op.scoped(scope))` IS the scoped apply, not a view of
145	    /// it — so `check_caps` and `check_nesting`, which phase 9 runs once on
146	    /// the MERGED parent (`core/src/scope.rs`, `Project::finish`), refuse
147	    /// here with the core's own sentence exactly as they would at the
148	    /// commit: a document at `MAX_TRACKS` throws "too many tracks" before
149	    /// any list is answered, inside a nest or out of one
150	    /// (`tools/proof/recording_probe.py`, section 4, row 8).
151	    ///
152	    /// **One list, one limit.** The pictures and the microphones are ONE
153	    /// grouped edit, so a microphone pair the core refuses takes every
154	    /// picture down with it. The case that reaches it: a document at
155	    /// `MAX_TRACKS` with an empty front track takes the pictures alone (no
156	    /// track is added) and lands NOTHING once a microphone needs its own
157	    /// track. Kept on purpose — half a recording landed, with the voice
158	    /// missing and no undo step that says so, is worse than a refusal — and
159	    /// both doors name the FILES in the refusal, which are on disk whatever
160	    /// happened after them. What is NOT a refusal is a file the core cannot
161	    /// make a clip of at all: it lands as media, with a sentence in `notes`.
162	    static func placement(
163	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, place: Bool
164	    ) throws -> Placement {
165	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
166	        guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
167	            throw ReelCoreError(
168	                message: "A drag is in progress; the recording can be added when it ends.")
169	        }
170	        if result.isVoiceOver { return try voiceOverPlacement(result, in: document, place: place) }
171	        let scope = document.scope
172	        var trial = document.project
173	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
174	        var notes: [String] = []
175	
176	        var mediaIds: [UInt32] = []
177	        for segment in result.segments {
178	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
179	        }
180	        var pictures: [Landed] = []
181	        if place {
182	            let stretches = try pictureStretches(
183	                of: result, mediaIds: mediaIds, in: trial, scope: scope)
184	            pictures = try addSequence(
185	                stretches, from: document.playhead, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops,
186	                notes: &notes)
187	            try addRipples(
188	                pictures.compactMap { $0.clip?.id }, of: result, scope: scope, to: &trial,
189	                ops: &ops)
190	        }
191	        let cameras = try addCameras(
192	            result, screenStarts: place ? segmentStarts(pictures.map { $0.at }, of: result) : nil,
193	            screenClips: split(pictures.map { $0.clip?.id }, of: result).segments,
194	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
195	        let microphones = try addMicrophones(
196	            voices(of: result), pictureStarts: place ? pictures.map { $0.at } : nil,
197	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
198	        let micMedia = split(microphones.media, of: result)
199	        let micClips = split(microphones.clips, of: result)
200	        return Placement(
201	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds,
202	            clipIds: place
203	                ? split(pictures.map { $0.clip?.id }, of: result).segments
204	                : mediaIds.map { _ in nil },
205	            micMediaIds: micMedia.segments, micClipIds: micClips.segments, notes: notes,
206	            leftOutMicMediaIds: micMedia.leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: micClips.leftOut,
207	            cameraMediaIds: cameras.media, cameraClipIds: cameras.clips)
208	    }
209	
210	    // MARK: - The steps, each applied purely and read back
211	
212	    /// `add_media` applied purely; the id it minted, read off the result. A
213	    /// path already in the list is the documented IDENTITY
214	    /// (`core/src/edit_track.rs`), not a failure, and then the id is the
215	    /// entry's, matched by the TRIMMED path because that is what the core
216	    /// stored — `backgroundMedia(for:in:)`'s rule. The op stays in the list
217	    /// either way: `applying(_ ops:)` runs every later op after an identity,
218	    /// so one shape serves both cases and the undo step is one.
219	    static func addMedia(
220	        _ descriptor: MediaDescriptor, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
221	    ) throws -> UInt32 {
222	        let op = ReelOp.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)
223	        ops.append(op)
224	        if let added = try trial.applying(op).project {
225	            trial = added
226	            guard let id = added.snapshot.media.last?.id else {
227	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(descriptor.path) was added and is not listed.")
228	            }
229	            return id
230	        }
231	        let path = trimmed(descriptor.path)
232	        guard let id = trial.snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
233	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) could not be added to the media list.")
234	        }
235	        return id
236	    }
237	
238	    /// The two-try track rule over a SEQUENCE, for a `trial` that holds
239	    /// every `media`: all of them back to back on the front track of the
240	    /// open container, from `at`; if any one REFUSES there — the overlap
241	    /// rule is the only reason the core has — ALL of them on a new track in
242	    /// front of everything, from the same `at`. The sequence never splits: a
243	    /// recording whose first segment sits on one track and whose second on
244	    /// another would read as two recordings, so a refusal part-way discards
245	    /// the front track's half-placed trial whole (it was a copy) and starts
246	    /// the new track's from the trial that holds the media and no clip. The
247	    /// new track's id is `next_id` off the trial, and each clip's is
248	    /// `next_id` off the trial before its own `add_clip`.
249	    ///
250	    /// Only a REFUSAL (nil) falls through to the new track. An `Err` from
251	    /// the first attempt propagates: the caps are the same on either track,
252	    /// so a `try?` here — R1's shape — turned "too many clips" on a full
253	    /// document into a second attempt that added a track and then reported
254	    /// "too many tracks", the wrong cap, when the document was at both.
255	    /// `notes` takes the winning attempt's sentences (the same either way —
256	    /// a picture too short for a frame is too short on any track). The
257	    /// sequence is the whole stretch list, a left-out voice's gap included,
258	    /// so the rule sees every picture where it will land.
259	    private static func addSequence(
260	        _ stretches: [PictureStretch], from at: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,
261	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
262	    ) throws -> [Landed] {
263	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
264	        if let front = container.tracks.last?.id {
265	            var attempt = trial
266	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
267	            var attemptNotes: [String] = []
268	            if let placed = try placeBackToBack(
269	                stretches, on: front, from: at, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
270	                notes: &attemptNotes)
271	            {
272	                trial = attempt
273	                ops += attemptOps
274	                notes += attemptNotes
275	                return placed
276	            }
277	        }
278	        // Index 0 is the BACK of the stack (§6), so the count is the front.
279	        let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: container.tracks.count)
280	        let track = trial.snapshot.nextId
281	        guard let withTrack = try trial.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project else {
282	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the recording could not be added.")
283	        }
284	        var attempt = withTrack
285	        var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = [addTrack]
286	        var attemptNotes: [String] = []
287	        guard
288	            let placed = try placeBackToBack(
289	                stretches, on: track, from: at, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
290	                notes: &attemptNotes)
291	        else {
292	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The recording could not be placed on a new track.")
293	        }
294	        trial = attempt
295	        ops += attemptOps
296	        notes += attemptNotes
297	        return placed
298	    }
299	
300	    /// The clip `id` as the core reports it, read off the CONTAINER the ops
301	    /// are measured against — the nest's view while a scope is open, since
302	    /// a nested clip is not in the parent's `clips`. An id the trial does
303	    /// not list after its own `add_clip` accepted it is a throw, not a
304	    /// guess.
305	    static func clip(_ id: UInt32, in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws -> ClipSnapshot {
306	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
307	        guard let clip = container.clips.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
308	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "Clip \(id) was placed and is not listed.")
309	        }
310	        return clip
311	    }
312	
313	    /// The container the clip ops are measured against: the nest's view
314	    /// while a scope is open (its tracks and clips at the top level, its
315	    /// `next_id` the parent's), else the trial itself. A scope naming a nest
316	    /// the trial has not got is a refusal, not a fallback — `clampViewState`
317	    /// clears one before anything reads it, so this arm is a race with an
318	    /// undo and the caller should not land on the timeline by accident.
319	    static func view(of trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws -> ReelProject {
320	        guard let nest = scope else { return trial }
321	        guard let view = trial.scoped(nest) else {
322	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The open nest (id \(nest)) is no longer in the project.")
323	        }
324	        return view
325	    }
326	
327	    static func trimmed(_ path: String) -> String {
328	        path.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
329	    }
330	}

5	/// The half of screen recording a probe can call: values in, values out, no
6	/// framework object that needs a bundle (road map 3, R1a). What a recording
7	/// IS before it starts — the choice, where its files go and the two
8	/// ScreenCaptureKit configurations built from that choice (the two grants
9	/// it stands on are `RecordingGrant.swift`'s) — so that
10	/// `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` can read every field back from a bare
11	/// Mach-O that never starts a stream.
12	///
13	/// `ScreenRecorder.swift` (with `+Pause.swift`, `+Microphone.swift`,
14	/// `+Finishing.swift`, `+Delegates.swift` and `+Content.swift`) is the other
15	/// half: the class that owns the `SCStream`, one `SCRecordingOutput` per
16	/// SEGMENT (R2: a pause removes one and a resume adds the next) and, when a
17	/// microphone is chosen, the `AVCaptureSession` for the second file. The
18	/// result types a recording ends as — `StopReason`, `RecordingSegment`,
19	/// `RecordingResult`, `RecorderError` — are `RecordingResult.swift`, moved
20	/// off the foot of this file at the 400-line cap; they are still values a
21	/// probe can make.
22	///
23	/// Three R0 facts shape the configuration and are restated on the fields
24	/// they decide (`archive/roadmap-3.md`, "R0 — the answers"):
25	///
26	/// - **The microphone is a second file** (q2). `captureMicrophone` on the
27	///   stream writes ONE stereo track that is the SUM of system and microphone
28	///   sound, which is decision 5's bad case — so `make` never sets it, and
29	///   `RecordingChoice.microphone` names an `AVCaptureDevice` for
30	///   `ScreenRecorder`'s capture session instead.
31	/// - **`.best` does not scale by itself** (q4). `captureResolution = .best`
32	///   at the display's point size writes a point-sized file; pixels come only
33	///   when `width`/`height` are asked for in pixels, so `make` multiplies the
34	///   point size by the display's backing scale under `.best` itself.
35	/// - **Show Clicks needs BGRA** (q6a). `SCStream.h` says `showMouseClicks`
36	///   "currently applies when pixelFormat is set to BGRA" and a fresh
37	///   configuration reads `420v`, so `make` sets `REDACTED`
38	///   when the stream draws clicks and leaves the default alone otherwise —
39	///   measured, a recording output over a BGRA stream starts and writes. The
40	///   stream draws the pointer and its click ring only In the picture
41	///   (road map creator-jobs CU3c, spec §11 CU-31): with Separate, `make`
42	///   sets neither and keeps `420v`, and Show Clicks lands the screen clips
43	///   with ripples instead (`RecordingLanding+Cursor.swift`).

47	/// What is recorded. `.picked` is the panel's picker result, whose filter

56	    case display(CGDirectDisplayID)
57	    case window(CGWindowID)
58	    case picked
59	    case voiceOver

155	/// Decision 2 (road map 3 §0): a recording is ORIGINAL footage and lives in
156	/// `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time — never in the
157	/// package (an untitled document has none) and never in the temporary
158	/// directory (where a cache is regenerable and footage would be lost). The
159	/// folder is created on demand, and `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides it the
160	/// way `-RCFFmpegPath` overrides the binary (`FFmpegRewrap.locate`), so a
161	/// proof can record into `tools/proof/work/` and delete it.
162	enum RecordingFiles {
163	    /// The launch-argument override, read from `UserDefaults.standard` so it
164	    /// works from the argument domain (`-RCRecordingFolder ~/x` on the
165	    /// command line, or a pinned volatile domain in a probe).
166	    static let folderDefaultsKey = "RCRecordingFolder"
167	
168	    /// The default folder's name under `~/Movies`.
169	    static let folderName = "Frame Job Recordings"
170	
171	    /// The folder a recording goes into: the override, tilde-expanded, when
172	    /// one is set; `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` otherwise. Nothing is
173	    /// created here — `create(_:)` is called at the moment a recording has
174	    /// something to put in it, `AppSupport`'s rule.
175	    static func folder() -> URL {
176	        if let override = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: folderDefaultsKey),
177	            !override.isEmpty
178	        {
179	            return URL(
180	                fileURLWithPath: (override as NSString).expandingTildeInPath, isDirectory: true)
181	        }
182	        let movies =
183	            FileManager.default.urls(for: .moviesDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first
184	            ?? FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser.appendingPathComponent(
185	                "Movies", isDirectory: true)
186	        return movies.appendingPathComponent(folderName, isDirectory: true)
187	    }
188	
189	    /// `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22` — the Screenshot app's
190	    /// spelling, in the machine's own time zone. The formatter is pinned to
191	    /// `en_US_POSIX` so a locale with another digit set or a 12-hour clock
192	    /// cannot change the name's shape; the seconds make a name unique across
193	    /// the app's own recordings and `uniqueURL` handles the rest.
194	    static func stem(at date: Date) -> String {
195	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
196	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
197	        formatter.timeZone = .current
198	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Screen Recording' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
199	        return formatter.string(from: date)
200	    }
201	
202	    /// `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04` — a voice-over's file, `stem(at:)`'s
203	    /// spelling and pinning with its own lead word.
204	    static func voiceOverStem(at date: Date) -> String {
205	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
206	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
207	        formatter.timeZone = .current
208	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Voice-over' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
209	        return formatter.string(from: date)
210	    }
211	
212	    /// `<stem>.<ext>` in `folder`, or `<stem> (2).<ext>`, `<stem> (3).<ext>`…
213	    /// while a file of that name exists — the Finder's own collision rule.
214	    static func uniqueURL(in folder: URL, stem: String, ext: String) -> URL {
215	        let manager = FileManager.default
216	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension(ext)
217	        var counter = 2
218	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) {
219	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
220	                .appendingPathExtension(ext)
221	            counter += 1
222	        }
223	        return candidate
224	    }
225	
226	    /// The microphone's own file, beside the movie: the movie's stem plus
227	    /// ` (Microphone)`, as `.m4a` (R0 q6b: `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput` writes
228	    /// one mono 48 kHz AAC track there), made unique the same way.
229	    static func microphoneURL(beside movie: URL) -> URL {
230	        let stem = movie.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent + " (Microphone)"
231	        return uniqueURL(in: movie.deletingLastPathComponent(), stem: stem, ext: "m4a")
232	    }
233	
234	    /// Makes the folder, intermediate directories included. A folder that
235	    /// already exists is not an error.
236	    static func create(_ folder: URL) throws {
237	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
238	            at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
239	    }
240	}

242	// MARK: - The configurations
243	
244	/// The two ScreenCaptureKit configurations a choice becomes. PURE — every
245	/// field is set from the arguments and read back by the probe — which is
246	/// what lets the `excludesCurrentProcessAudio` mutant be caught at all: it
247	/// is invisible over MCP (nothing plays during a headless recording) and
248	/// this is the only row that sees it.
249	enum RecordingConfiguration {
250	    /// System audio is asked for at 48 kHz stereo, the rate the tap and
251	    /// `Loudness.swift` already assume of every file.
252	    static let sampleRate = 48_000
253	    static let channelCount = 2
254	
255	    /// `displayPointSize` and `scale` come from the caller, and the caller is
256	    /// `ScreenRecorder.start`, which reads them off the FILTER — its
257	    /// `contentRect` (points) and `pointPixelScale` — the one geometry
258	    /// source that also covers a picker-made filter (`SCDisplay`'s
259	    /// `width`/`height` are POINTS, R0 q4, and a display filter reports the
260	    /// display's point size and backing scale, a window filter the window's
261	    /// frame). The probe passes the numbers directly. `outputURL` is
262	    /// assigned before the output configuration is returned, and must stay
263	    /// so: reading `outputURL` off a fresh `SCRecordingOutputConfiguration`
264	    /// TRAPS (it imports non-optional and is nil underneath until assigned —
265	    /// the SDK scout's finding, exit 133).
266	    static func make(
267	        _ choice: RecordingChoice, displayPointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, outputURL: URL
268	    ) -> (stream: SCStreamConfiguration, output: SCRecordingOutputConfiguration) {
269	        let stream = SCStreamConfiguration()
270	        // R0 q4: pixels are asked for, `.best` does not scale by itself.
271	        let factor: CGFloat = choice.resolution == .best ? max(scale, 1) : 1
272	        stream.width = Int((displayPointSize.width * factor).rounded())
273	        stream.height = Int((displayPointSize.height * factor).rounded())
274	        stream.captureResolution = choice.resolution == .best ? .best : .nominal
275	        stream.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: CMTimeScale(max(choice.rate, 1)))
276	        // CU-31: the pointer and its ring are the stream's only In the picture.
277	        let inPicture = choice.effectiveCursor == .inPicture
278	        stream.showsCursor = inPicture
279	        stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks && inPicture
280	        // R0 q6a: the click circle draws only under BGRA; the default `420v`
281	        // is left alone when the stream draws no clicks, so an ordinary
282	        // recording's pixel path is byte for byte the spike's.
283	        if choice.showClicks && inPicture { stream.pixelFormat = REDACTED }
284	        stream.capturesAudio = choice.systemAudio
285	        stream.sampleRate = sampleRate
286	        stream.channelCount = channelCount
287	        // ALWAYS: the timeline can play while a recording runs and must not
288	        // be in it. `captureMicrophone` is deliberately never touched (R0
289	        // q2 — the microphone is a second file), so it keeps its default of
290	        // false, which the probe reads back on every row.
291	        stream.excludesCurrentProcessAudio = true
292	
293	        let output = SCRecordingOutputConfiguration()
294	        output.outputURL = outputURL
295	        output.outputFileType = .mov
296	        // R0 q2: `availableVideoCodecTypes` is `[avc1, hvc1]` here and the
297	        // default is `avc1`; HEVC halves the file where the encoder offers it.
298	        output.videoCodecType =
299	            output.availableVideoCodecTypes.contains(.hevc) ? .hevc : .h264
300	        return (stream, output)
301	    }
302	}

5	/// The recording session (road map 3, R1a; pause and resume R2a): a state
6	/// machine `idle → arming → recording ⇄ paused → finishing → idle` owning
7	/// the `SCStream`, one `SCRecordingOutput` per SEGMENT and — when a
8	/// microphone is chosen — the `AVCaptureSession` that writes the microphone
9	/// to a SECOND file per segment (R0 q2: `captureMicrophone` on the stream
10	/// sums the microphone into the system track, decision 5's bad case, so it
11	/// is never set). The panel and the `record_screen` tool both drive this
12	/// one object and both receive a `RecordingResult` (`RecordingResult.swift`);
13	/// `RecordingLanding` turns that into ops. This file is the arming half;
14	/// `+Started.swift` how an arm ends (`captureStarted`, `failStart`);
15	/// `+Stop.swift` is `stop()`; `ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift` is what a segment
16	/// is and the two transitions that close one and open the next;
17	/// `+Microphone.swift` the capture session's preparation and the meter;
18	/// `+Finishing.swift` everything that ENDS a session; `+Delegates.swift` the
19	/// three delegates; `+Content.swift` the static helpers over shareable
20	/// content, filters and error codes. A VOICE-OVER (`voiceSession`, spec §11
21	/// recording) is the same machine with no stream — the microphone writer
22	/// alone, a file per segment — in `+VoiceOver.swift` and
23	/// `+VoiceOverFinishing.swift`; `stop()`, `elapsed`, `pause()` and `resume()`
24	/// forward to it. A CAMERA recording (`cameraSession`, spec §11 CAM-3) is the
25	/// same machine with a camera where the stream was, in `+Camera.swift` and
26	/// `+CameraFinishing.swift`, forwarded to on the same terms. A camera BESIDE
27	/// the screen (spec §11 CAM-9) is this machine's: `+CameraBeside.swift`,
28	/// `+CameraBesideFinishing.swift` and `ScreenFrameWatch.swift`. Every screen
29	/// recording's cursor file per segment (spec §11 CU-11…CU-13, CU-18) is
30	/// `+Cursor.swift` and `CursorCapture.swift`.
31	///
32	/// **A paused recording is a sequence of files over one stream** (decision
33	/// 6). ScreenCaptureKit has no pause, so `pause()` REMOVES the segment's
34	/// recording output — its file closes — and `resume()` ADDS a fresh one to
35	/// a new file while the stream keeps capturing (R0 q7: 57 fps while
36	/// paused, the did-finish 5–25 ms after the remove, the did-start 8–10 ms
37	/// after the add); the microphone's writer is stopped and restarted per
38	/// segment on its one running session. `Session.segments` is that
39	/// sequence, never empty, and every callback finds ITS segment — by the
40	/// output's identity, by the microphone file's URL — rather than "the"
41	/// one, because the closed segment's did-finish can land after the next
42	/// has begun and a resume never waits for it.
43	///
44	/// **One hook, one delivery** (R1 review finding 4). `start` takes
45	/// `onFinish`, which is stored ON THE SESSION — installed only once every
46	/// guard has passed, when the arm really begins — and called exactly once,
47	/// at conclude, whoever ended the recording: a `stop()`, the menu bar's
48	/// indicator, the system, a failure. There is no settable hook on the
49	/// recorder any more, because there was one and a panel Record refused
50	/// `.busy` erased the tool's, after which an external stop reached nobody.
51	/// A start that FAILS never concludes: its error is the start completion's
52	/// alone. `stop()` in any state past idle JOINS (finding 1): its completion
53	/// is registered and every registered completion receives the one outcome
54	/// beside `onFinish`, so a person's Stop in the second after the menu
55	/// bar's cannot drop the landing. `.busy` is `start()` while not idle —
56	/// paused included — and nothing else.
57	///
58	/// **No `async`** (spec §11): every ScreenCaptureKit and AVFoundation entry
59	/// point used has a completion-handler or delegate form. **No queue of its
60	/// own**: the frameworks deliver their callbacks on private queues (R0 q6b:
61	/// the microphone's did-start on one labelled "File ou", the recording
62	/// output's on ScreenCaptureKit's), and each is stamped with `Date()` where
63	/// it arrives and hopped to main through `DispatchQueue.main.async` —
64	/// `MediaImporter.probe`'s shape —
65	/// so every transition runs on the main thread and needs no lock. The
66	/// microphone's did-finish arrived ON main in every measured run and is
67	/// hopped anyway.
68	///
69	/// **The callback ORDER the machine tolerates**, all measured (R0 q2, q6b,
70	/// q7): `recordingOutputDidStartRecording` fires 86–107 ms BEFORE
71	/// `startCapture`'s completion in every run, so did-start is a stamp taken
72	/// whenever it arrives and the completion consults it, never the reverse;
73	/// the microphone output's `startRecording` returns with `isRecording`
74	/// still false, so its did-start callback is the truth and the property is
75	/// never read for it; `session.startRunning()` BLOCKS main for 100–180 ms,
76	/// which is why `prepareMicrophone` exists — a countdown pays it before it
77	/// ends, so the first 0.4 s of voice is in the file — and why the session
78	/// goes FIRST when it was not prepared (the two files' first samples then
79	/// land within a frame of each other, offset +11 ms mean, 35 ms scatter);
80	/// stop → did-finish is 0.03 s without a microphone and up to 1.1 s with
81	/// one, so the finishing wait is bounded at `finishCeiling` rather than
82	/// open. The system's own menu-bar indicator can stop a capture from
83	/// outside the app (`.userStopped`; `.systemStopped` for a display that
84	/// sleeps, the stream's `.systemStoppedStream` code), while recording OR
85	/// paused — it stays up through a pause, since the stream never stops:
86	/// both take the SAME finishing path as `stop()`.
87	///
88	/// **Grants** (decision 4): this class never calls
89	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` or `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess`. It
90	/// reads `RecordingGrant.screenRecordingGranted` before building the stream
91	/// and the microphone status before constructing an `AVCaptureDeviceInput`
92	/// (whose initializer auto-prompts on `.notDetermined`), and refuses by name;
93	/// with `choice.keys` `shortcuts`, Input Monitoring is read after the
94	/// microphone and a choice whose key tap cannot be made is refused with the
95	/// same sentence (spec §11 CU-62) — never `CGRequestListenEventAccess`.
96	final class ScreenRecorder: NSObject {
97	    static let shared = ScreenRecorder()
98	
99	    enum State: Equatable { case idle, arming, recording, paused, finishing }
100	
101	    /// Seconds the finishing path waits for the writers' did-finish before
102	    /// probing whatever is on disk.
103	    static let finishCeiling: TimeInterval = 10
104	    /// Seconds `startCapture` may take to answer (R0: under 0.2 s).
105	    static let armCeiling: TimeInterval = 20
106	
107	    /// Written by this class's own six files and nothing else; the pausing,
108	    /// finishing and delegate halves live in extensions, which is why this
109	    /// is not `private(set)`.
110	    var state: State = .idle
111	    /// Every state past idle, PAUSED included: File ▸ Stop Recording, the
112	    /// quit guard and `.busy` all read a paused recording as one in
113	    /// progress. `isPaused` (`+Pause.swift`) is the narrower question.
114	    var isRecording: Bool { state != .idle }
115	    /// The microphone's level. The panel binds a `LevelMeterView(meter:)` to
116	    /// it — never `LevelMeter.shared`, or the timeline bar would meter the
117	    /// microphone.
118	    let meter = LevelMeter()
119	    /// Non-nil from the moment a microphone problem is detected — the file
120	    /// output's did-finish carrying an error while the picture still
121	    /// records (finding 3), a device that went away — so the panel's tick
122	    /// can show it live; set ONCE and kept for the session (the panel
123	    /// writes its note once; a later segment's failure is on its own
124	    /// segment), nil while idle. The result's `micProblem` carries the
125	    /// final sentences, which may say more (each file's path).
126	    var microphoneProblem: String?
127	
128	    /// Seconds RECORDED: the sum over segments of each one's span — its
129	    /// screen did-start (Date-based: the output's `recordedDuration` is
130	    /// whole seconds) to its `stoppedAt`, or to now for the one still open
131	    /// — each floored at 0, so it freezes while paused and never counts a
132	    /// gap; frozen at the stop call; 0 idle, and 0 while arming until the
133	    /// first did-start or `startCapture`'s completion lands (R1's rule,
134	    /// kept for the first segment: an arm can take seconds and none of
135	    /// them is footage).
136	    var elapsed: TimeInterval {
137	        if voiceSession != nil { return voiceElapsed }
138	        if cameraSession != nil { return cameraElapsed }
139	        guard state != .idle, let session else { return 0 }
140	        let now = Date()
141	        var total: TimeInterval = 0
142	        for (index, segment) in session.segments.enumerated() {
143	            guard let start = session.screenStart(of: index) else { continue }
144	            total += max(0, (segment.stoppedAt ?? now).timeIntervalSince(start))
145	        }
146	        return total
147	    }
148	
149	    var session: Session?
150	    /// A voice-over's session (`ScreenRecorder+VoiceOver.swift`); never set
151	    /// beside `session`.
152	    var voiceSession: VoiceSession?
153	    /// A camera recording's session (`ScreenRecorder+Camera.swift`); never
154	    /// set beside `session` or `voiceSession`.
155	    var cameraSession: CameraSession?
156	    var startCompletion: ((Error?) -> Void)?
157	    /// Every `stop()` completion registered since the arm began, delivered
158	    /// together at conclude (or by `failStart`, with its error).
159	    var stopCompletions: [(Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void] = []
160	    /// A `stop()` arrived while arming: finishing begins the moment the
161	    /// start lands.
162	    var pendingStop = false
163	    /// `prepareMicrophone`'s running session, adopted by the next `start`
164	    /// whose choice names its device (`ScreenRecorder+Microphone.swift`).
165	    var preparedMicrophone: PreparedMicrophone?
166	    /// `prepareCamera`'s started capture, adopted by the next `startCamera`
167	    /// for its device and format (`+CameraPrepare.swift`, spec §11 CAM-5).
168	    var preparedCamera: PreparedCamera?

170	    /// `discardPreparedCamera` (spec §11 CAM-7 (8)). Main only.

172	    var timer: Timer?

181	    // MARK: - Start
182	
183	    /// MAIN THREAD. `completion` on main, nil on success. A refusal — busy, a
184	    /// grant absent, an unknown microphone, a folder that cannot be made —
185	    /// completes BEFORE this returns, tears down any prepared microphone
186	    /// and touches nothing else; `.busy` in particular touches NOTHING of
187	    /// the running session, its hook included. A start that reaches
188	    /// `startCapture` completes from its completion handler. `onFinish` is
189	    /// the session's (the header): installed here only once every guard
190	    /// has passed, never called for a start that fails.
191	    ///
192	    /// The geometry is the FILTER's own — `contentRect` (points) and
193	    /// `pointPixelScale` — the one source that also covers a picker-made
194	    /// filter; measured, a display filter reports the display's point size
195	    /// and backing scale, a window filter the window's frame. ORDER (R0
196	    /// q6b): the microphone session (prepared, or started here), then its
197	    /// file output, then the stream, all in one run-loop turn (`launchScreen`)
198	    /// — this one, or with a camera beside the screen the turn its warm-up
199	    /// answers (spec §11 CAM-9 (1), (2)). The first segment is minted here,
200	    /// named by the call's own time.
201	    func start(
202	        filter: SCContentFilter, choice: RecordingChoice, mayAsk: Bool,
203	        onFinish: @escaping (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void,
204	        completion: @escaping (Error?) -> Void
205	    ) {
206	        guard state == .idle else { return completion(RecorderError.busy) }
207	        guard choice.source != .voiceOver else {
208	            return refuse(
209	                .startFailed("A voice-over has no picture; it starts through startVoiceOver."),
210	                completion)
211	        }
212	        guard choice.source != .camera else {
213	            return refuse(
214	                .startFailed("A camera recording has no screen; it starts through startCamera."),
215	                completion)
216	        }
217	        guard RecordingGrant.screenRecordingGranted else {
218	            return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal), completion)
219	        }
220	        if choice.camera != nil {
221	            let cameraGrant = RecordingGrant.cameraStatus
222	            guard cameraGrant == .authorized else {
223	                return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(cameraGrant)), completion)
224	            }
225	        }
226	        let camera: (device: AVCaptureDevice, format: Int)?
227	        do {
228	            camera = try cameraBesideDevice(for: choice)
229	        } catch {
230	            return refuse(error as? RecorderError ?? .cameraDevice("\(error)"), completion)
231	        }
232	        var microphone: AVCaptureDevice?
233	        if let id = choice.microphone {
234	            let status = RecordingGrant.microphoneStatus
235	            guard status == .authorized else {
236	                return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.microphoneRefusal(status)), completion)
237	            }
238	            guard let device = Self.microphone(withID: id) else {
239	                return refuse(
240	                    .microphoneDevice("No microphone with the id \(id) is connected."), completion)
241	            }
242	            microphone = device
243	        }
244	        if choice.keys == .shortcuts, !RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringGranted {
245	            return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringRefusal), completion)
246	        }
247	        do {
248	            try RecordingFiles.create(choice.folder)
249	        } catch {
250	            return refuse(
251	                .startFailed(
252	                    "The recordings folder \(choice.folder.path) could not be created: "
253	                        + error.localizedDescription), completion)
254	        }
255	        let calledAt = Date()
256	        let movieURL = RecordingFiles.uniqueURL(
257	            in: choice.folder, stem: RecordingFiles.stem(at: calledAt), ext: "mov")
258	        let displayPointSize = filter.contentRect.size
259	        let scale = CGFloat(filter.pointPixelScale)
260	        let configs = RecordingConfiguration.make(
261	            choice, displayPointSize: displayPointSize, scale: scale, outputURL: movieURL)
262	        let stream = SCStream(filter: filter, configuration: configs.stream, delegate: self)
263	        let output = SCRecordingOutput(configuration: configs.output, delegate: self)
264	        do {
265	            // BEFORE `startCapture`, the header's own rule, so the first
266	            // sample lands in the file.
267	            try stream.addRecordingOutput(output)
268	        } catch {
269	            return refuse(
270	                .startFailed(
271	                    "The recording output could not be added: " + error.localizedDescription),
272	                completion)
273	        }
274	        // The cursor's capture and its segments' header (spec §11 CU-11, CU-13);
275	        // nothing runs until `launchScreen`.
276	        let cursor = CursorCapture()
277	        // Record shortcuts (CU-62): the key tap is made now, enabled with the poll.
278	        if choice.keys == .shortcuts, !cursor.makeKeyTap() {
279	            return refuse(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringRefusal), completion)
280	        }
281	        let cursorStart = Self.cursorStart(filter: filter, choice: choice, stream: configs.stream)
282	        // The frame watch rides every screen recording (CU-13): E2 for a
283	        // camera, the geometry for the cursor. Only a camera's start needs it.
284	        var watch: ScreenFrameWatch?
285	        var watchLost: String?
286	        if ScreenFrameWatchRule.attaches(camera: camera != nil, cursor: true) {
287	            let made = ScreenFrameWatch(
288	                bound: ScreenFrameWatch.bound(rate: choice.rate),
289	                onGeometry: { [weak cursor] geometry, pts in cursor?.geometry(geometry, host: pts) })
290	            do {
291	                try stream.addStreamOutput(made, type: .screen, sampleHandlerQueue: made.queue)
292	                watch = made
293	            } catch {
294	                if ScreenFrameWatchRule.failsStart(camera: camera != nil) {
295	                    return refuse(
296	                        .startFailed(
297	                            "The screen's frames could not be watched: " + error.localizedDescription),
298	                        completion)
299	                }
300	                watch = nil
301	                watchLost = error.localizedDescription
302	            }
303	        }
304	        var mic: MicrophoneCapture?
305	        if let device = microphone {
306	            do {
307	                mic = try microphoneCapture(for: device, beside: movieURL)
308	            } catch let failure as RecorderError {
309	                return refuse(failure, completion)
310	            } catch {
311	                return refuse(.microphoneDevice(error.localizedDescription), completion)
312	            }
313	        }
314	        var capture: CameraCapture?
315	        var recorded: RecordingCamera?
316	        if let camera {
317	            do {
318	                let taken = try takeCameraCapture(
319	                    device: camera.device, format: camera.format, adopting: mayAsk)
320	                capture = taken
321	                recorded = RecordingCamera(
322	                    name: camera.device.localizedName, format: CameraDevices.spelled(taken.applied))
323	            } catch {
324	                mic?.session.stopRunning()
325	                return refuse(error as? RecorderError ?? .cameraDevice("\(error)"), completion)
326	            }
327	        }
328	        microphoneProblem = nil
329	        session = Session(
330	            choice: choice, mayAsk: mayAsk, displayPointSize: displayPointSize, scale: scale,
331	            stream: stream,
332	            micSession: mic?.session, micOutput: mic?.output, calledAt: calledAt,
333	            onFinish: onFinish,
334	            segments: [
335	                Segment(movieURL: movieURL, micURL: mic?.url, output: output, addedAt: calledAt)
336	            ], cameraCapture: capture, camera: recorded, frameWatch: watch, cursor: cursor,
337	            cursorStart: cursorStart, cursorWatchLost: watchLost)
338	        state = .arming
339	        startCompletion = completion
340	        if let mic {
341	            if !mic.session.isRunning { mic.session.startRunning() }
342	            guard mic.session.isRunning else {
343	                return failStart(
344	                    RecorderError.microphoneDevice("The microphone session did not start."))
345	            }
346	        }
347	        // With a camera, its warm-up first and the launch turn on its answer
348	        // (spec §11 CAM-9 (2)); without one, the launch is this turn's.
349	        if let capture { armCameraBeside(capture) } else { launchScreen() }
350	        // The stream's own report wins over the bare ceiling (finding 5).
351	        // `.common`, the panel's rule: an open status-item menu runs the
352	        // loop in tracking mode, where a default-mode timer waits.
353	        let ceiling = Timer(timeInterval: Self.armCeiling, repeats: false) { [weak self] _ in
354	            guard let self, self.state == .arming else { return }
355	            self.failStart(self.session?.screenFailure ?? RecorderError.startTimedOut)
356	        }
357	        RunLoop.main.add(ceiling, forMode: .common)
358	        timer = ceiling
359	    }

361	    /// A refusal before the arm: nothing was made, and a microphone the
362	    /// countdown prepared is let go so the input does not stay open.
363	    private func refuse(_ error: RecorderError, _ completion: (Error?) -> Void) {
364	        discardPreparedMicrophone()
365	        completion(error)
366	    }
367	}

4	/// The microphone half of `ScreenRecorder`: the capture session that writes
5	/// the second file (R0 q2), prepared AHEAD of the recording, and the meter
6	/// that reads it. Cut out of `ScreenRecorder.swift` along the line the
7	/// header there names — the machine in one file, the device in this one —
8	/// when the preparation took the base file past the 400-line cap.
9	///
10	/// **Why prepare** (R1 review, unjudged and upheld by a −421 ms smoke run:
11	/// the first 0.4 s of voice was simply not in the file). `AVCaptureSession.
12	/// startRunning()` costs 100–400 ms on first use, and a session started
13	/// inside `start` pays it after the countdown has ended, so the microphone
14	/// is deaf for the recording's first words. `prepareMicrophone` builds the
15	/// session and starts it while the countdown still runs; `start` ADOPTS it
16	/// when its device is the choice's and builds one otherwise; a refused
17	/// start and every conclude tear it down, so an input never stays open
18	/// past the recording it was for. Never a prompt: the status is read before
19	/// `AVCaptureDeviceInput(device:)` is made, `start`'s own rule.
20	extension ScreenRecorder {
21	    /// A running session waiting for a `start` whose choice names its device.
22	    struct PreparedMicrophone {
23	        let deviceID: String
24	        let session: AVCaptureSession
25	        let output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput
26	    }
27	
28	    /// What one recording's microphone is: the session, its file output and
29	    /// the `.m4a` beside the movie.
30	    typealias MicrophoneCapture = (
31	        session: AVCaptureSession, output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput, url: URL
32	    )
33	
34	    // MARK: - Preparation
35	
36	    /// MAIN THREAD, idle only. A nil id, a status other than `.authorized`,
37	    /// an id no connected device carries, or a session that will not run
38	    /// does nothing and leaves nothing behind; the same device already
39	    /// prepared and running is kept. Blocks main for the session's start
40	    /// (100–180 ms measured, R0 q6b) — the point is to spend it now.
41	    func prepareMicrophone(_ deviceID: String?) {
42	        guard state == .idle, let id = deviceID, RecordingGrant.microphoneStatus == .authorized,
43	            let device = Self.microphone(withID: id)
44	        else { return }
45	        if let prepared = preparedMicrophone, prepared.deviceID == id, prepared.session.isRunning {
46	            return
47	        }
48	        discardPreparedMicrophone()
49	        guard let built = try? Self.microphoneSession(for: device) else { return }
50	        built.session.startRunning()
51	        guard built.session.isRunning else { return }
52	        preparedMicrophone = PreparedMicrophone(
53	            deviceID: id, session: built.session, output: built.output)
54	    }
55	
56	    /// MAIN THREAD. Stops and forgets a prepared session, if there is one.
57	    /// While IDLE it also publishes silence (#98 c), prepared or not: the
58	    /// countdown's meter read the prepared session, and a cancel, a close,
59	    /// an abandoned or refused start and `failStart` (which idles first) all
60	    /// come here, so the bar never holds a level for an input that is closed.
61	    func discardPreparedMicrophone() {
62	        preparedMicrophone?.session.stopRunning()
63	        preparedMicrophone = nil
64	        if state == .idle { meter.publish(.silent, from: ObjectIdentifier(self)) }
65	    }
66	
67	    /// `start`'s microphone: `adoptMicrophone(for:)`'s session and output,
68	    /// with the `.m4a` beside the movie.
69	    func microphoneCapture(for device: AVCaptureDevice, beside movie: URL) throws
70	        -> MicrophoneCapture
71	    {
72	        let url = RecordingFiles.microphoneURL(beside: movie)
73	        let adopted = try adoptMicrophone(for: device)
74	        return (adopted.session, adopted.output, url)
75	    }
76	
77	    /// The capture session for `device`: the prepared session when its
78	    /// device is `device` and it is still running (a device that went away
79	    /// meanwhile stops its session), else a fresh one, which the caller will
80	    /// run. Either way the prepared slot is empty afterwards — adopted, or
81	    /// discarded because it was the wrong device. `start` (through
82	    /// `microphoneCapture`) and `startVoiceOver` both take theirs here.
83	    func adoptMicrophone(for device: AVCaptureDevice) throws
84	        -> (session: AVCaptureSession, output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput)
85	    {
86	        if let prepared = preparedMicrophone, prepared.deviceID == device.uniqueID,
87	            prepared.session.isRunning
88	        {
89	            preparedMicrophone = nil
90	            return (prepared.session, prepared.output)
91	        }
92	        discardPreparedMicrophone()
93	        return try Self.microphoneSession(for: device)
94	    }
95	
96	    /// The capture session for the second file: the device's input and an
97	    /// `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput`, not yet running.
98	    private static func microphoneSession(for device: AVCaptureDevice) throws
99	        -> (session: AVCaptureSession, output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput)
100	    {
101	        let capture = AVCaptureSession()
102	        let fileOutput = AVCaptureAudioFileOutput()
103	        let input = try AVCaptureDeviceInput(device: device)
104	        guard capture.canAddInput(input), capture.canAddOutput(fileOutput) else {
105	            throw RecorderError.microphoneDevice(
106	                "The microphone \(device.localizedName) cannot be recorded from.")
107	        }
108	        capture.addInput(input)
109	        capture.addOutput(fileOutput)
110	        return (capture, fileOutput)
111	    }
112	
113	    // MARK: - The meter
114	
115	    /// MAIN THREAD, from the panel's 30 Hz timer. Reads the microphone file
116	    /// output's connection channels and publishes one reading: while
117	    /// RECORDING, the recording's output; while IDLE with a PREPARED session
118	    /// running, that session's output — the countdown's meter (#98 c: the
119	    /// connection was measured reporting levels on a running session
120	    /// before `startRecording`, 2026-09-30). A no-op — nothing published —
121	    /// idle with nothing prepared, arming, PAUSED, finishing (the pause
122	    /// published the silence), and once the LATEST segment's microphone has
123	    /// finished or failed (finding 3 published the silence then, and a dead
124	    /// connection must not light the bar again; a closed segment's state is
125	    /// not this segment's). A VOICE-OVER (`voiceSession`) is read the same
126	    /// way: its output while recording and its last segment has neither
127	    /// finished nor failed; and so is a CAMERA recording (`cameraSession`,
128	    /// spec §11 CAM-5): its microphone output while recording, until the
129	    /// latest segment's microphone finishes or reports a problem. One
130	    /// channel is reported on both sides, `LevelMeterSink`'s rule for a
131	    /// mono track (R0 q6c: the connection exposes `averagePowerLevel` and
132	    /// `peakHoldLevel` in dB on every poll, so there is no sample buffer and
133	    /// no queue in it).
134	    func publishMicrophoneLevel() {
135	        let connection: AVCaptureConnection?
136	        if state == .recording, let voice = voiceSession, let last = voice.segments.last,
137	            !last.finished, last.failure == nil
138	        {
139	            connection = voice.micOutput.connection(with: .audio)
140	        } else if state == .recording, let current = session, !current.latest.micFinished,
141	            current.latest.micFailure == nil, let output = current.micOutput
142	        {
143	            connection = output.connection(with: .audio)
144	        } else if state == .recording, let camera = cameraSession, let last = camera.segments.last,
145	            !last.micFinished, last.micProblem == nil, let output = camera.micOutput
146	        {
147	            connection = output.connection(with: .audio)
148	        } else if state == .idle, let prepared = preparedMicrophone, prepared.session.isRunning {
149	            connection = prepared.output.connection(with: .audio)
150	        } else {
151	            connection = nil
152	        }
153	        guard let connection, let first = connection.audioChannels.first else { return }
154	        let second = connection.audioChannels.count > 1 ? connection.audioChannels[1] : first
155	        meter.publish(
156	            LevelMeterReading(
157	                peakLeft: RecordingMeter.linear(fromDecibels: first.peakHoldLevel),
158	                peakRight: RecordingMeter.linear(fromDecibels: second.peakHoldLevel),
159	                rmsLeft: RecordingMeter.linear(fromDecibels: first.averagePowerLevel),
160	                rmsRight: RecordingMeter.linear(fromDecibels: second.averagePowerLevel)),
161	            from: ObjectIdentifier(self))
162	    }
163	}

4	/// A VOICE-OVER (spec §11 recording, "A voice-over is a recording with no
5	/// picture", #99): the same machine with no stream. The microphone's
6	/// `AVCaptureSession` — the one a screen recording writes its second file
7	/// with, adopted from `prepareMicrophone` when the countdown made it — writes
8	/// one `.m4a` per stretch between pauses, named `Voice-over <date> at
9	/// <time>.m4a` by the moment the stretch began, exactly as a screen
10	/// recording's segments are. `ScreenRecorder.voiceSession` is set instead of
11	/// `session`, never beside it, and `stop()`, `elapsed`, `pause()` and
12	/// `resume()` forward here when it is; `state` is the one state machine
13	/// (`idle → recording ⇄ paused → finishing → idle`, with NO arming state —
14	/// the writer's `startRecording` is the whole start), so `isRecording`,
15	/// `isPaused`, the quit guard and both doors read a voice-over as they read a
16	/// recording. This file is the start, the two transitions and the stop;
17	/// `+VoiceOverFinishing.swift` is everything the writer reports and
18	/// everything that ends one.
19	///
20	/// **One writer, a file per segment.** Its delegate is `VoiceOverFileDelegate`
21	/// rather than the recorder — the recorder's own microphone delegate
22	/// (`+Delegates.swift`) reads `session` — and each callback finds ITS
23	/// segment by the output's identity and the file URL it reports, because a
24	/// paused segment's did-finish can land after the resume has opened the
25	/// next. A resume never waits for it (the screen machine's rule, R0 q7).
26	///
27	/// **No prompt**: the microphone status is read before the session is built
28	/// (`adoptMicrophone`), and nothing here asks for a grant or reads the
29	/// Screen Recording one.
30	extension ScreenRecorder {
31	    /// Everything one voice-over owns. `segments` is never empty: the first
32	    /// is minted by `startVoiceOver`, each later one by `resumeVoiceOver`.
33	    struct VoiceSession {
34	        let choice: RecordingChoice
35	        /// Whether a segment's probe may ask the conversion question:
36	        /// false for `record_screen` (spec §11 MC-5).
37	        let mayAsk: Bool
38	        let micSession: AVCaptureSession
39	        let micOutput: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput
40	        let fileDelegate: VoiceOverFileDelegate
41	        /// Called exactly once, at conclude.
42	        let onFinish: (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void
43	        var segments: [VoiceSegment]
44	        /// Presses of Pause, stored (`RecordingResult.pauses`).
45	        var pauses = 0
46	        /// The settle has begun: one probe walk, one conclude.
47	        var settling = false
48	        /// The finishing ceiling fired before every did-finish landed.
49	        var timedOut = false
50	    }
51	
52	    /// One `.m4a`: its URL, the call that asked for it (`calledAt`, the
53	    /// fallback for a did-start that never came), the writer's did-start,
54	    /// and `stoppedAt` — a pause's or the stop's, so non-nil means its
55	    /// did-finish was ASKED for. `failure` is the writer's error when it did
56	    /// not finish well; `stoppedOnItsOwn` is set by a did-finish that came
57	    /// with `stoppedAt` nil — the writer stopped and nobody asked — and holds
58	    /// `<desc>`, that did-finish's error or "It reported no error.".
59	    struct VoiceSegment {
60	        let url: URL
61	        let calledAt: Date
62	        var startedAt: Date?
63	        var stoppedAt: Date?
64	        var finished = false
65	        var failure: String?
66	        var stoppedOnItsOwn: String?
67	
68	        init(url: URL, calledAt: Date) {
69	            self.url = url
70	            self.calledAt = calledAt
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	    static let voiceOverNeedsMicrophoneSentence =
75	        "A voice-over records the microphone alone, so it needs a microphone; none is chosen."
76	
77	    // MARK: - Start
78	
79	    /// MAIN THREAD. `completion` on main, nil on success, and always BEFORE
80	    /// this returns: there is no arming state. A refusal touches nothing —
81	    /// `.busy` not even a prepared microphone; every other refusal lets a
82	    /// prepared one go — in this order: `.busy` when not idle; a choice
83	    /// that is not `.voiceOver`; no microphone; the Microphone grant not
84	    /// `.authorized` (read, never asked); a device id nothing connected
85	    /// carries; a folder that cannot be made; a session that will not run.
86	    /// Otherwise the first segment is minted, named by this call's time,
87	    /// the state is `.recording` and the writer is asked to start; its
88	    /// did-start is stamped where it lands.
89	    func startVoiceOver(
90	        choice: RecordingChoice, mayAsk: Bool,
91	        onFinish: @escaping (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void,
92	        completion: @escaping (Error?) -> Void
93	    ) {
94	        guard state == .idle else { return completion(RecorderError.busy) }
95	        guard choice.source == .voiceOver else {
96	            return refuseVoiceOver(
97	                .startFailed("A voice-over takes the Microphone Only source; this choice names a screen."),
98	                completion)
99	        }
100	        guard let id = choice.microphone else {
101	            return refuseVoiceOver(.startFailed(Self.voiceOverNeedsMicrophoneSentence), completion)
102	        }
103	        let status = RecordingGrant.microphoneStatus
104	        guard status == .authorized else {
105	            return refuseVoiceOver(.startFailed(RecordingGrant.microphoneRefusal(status)), completion)
106	        }
107	        guard let device = Self.microphone(withID: id) else {
108	            return refuseVoiceOver(
109	                .microphoneDevice("No microphone with the id \(id) is connected."), completion)
110	        }
111	        do {
112	            try RecordingFiles.create(choice.folder)
113	        } catch {
114	            return refuseVoiceOver(
115	                .startFailed(
116	                    "The recordings folder \(choice.folder.path) could not be created: "
117	                        + error.localizedDescription), completion)
118	        }
119	        let capture: (session: AVCaptureSession, output: AVCaptureAudioFileOutput)
120	        do {
121	            capture = try adoptMicrophone(for: device)
122	        } catch let failure as RecorderError {
123	            return refuseVoiceOver(failure, completion)
124	        } catch {
125	            return refuseVoiceOver(.microphoneDevice(error.localizedDescription), completion)
126	        }
127	        if !capture.session.isRunning { capture.session.startRunning() }
128	        guard capture.session.isRunning else {
129	            capture.session.stopRunning()
130	            return refuseVoiceOver(
131	                .microphoneDevice("The microphone session did not start."), completion)
132	        }
133	        microphoneProblem = nil
134	        let calledAt = Date()
135	        let url = Self.nextVoiceOverURL(in: choice.folder, at: calledAt, holding: [])
136	        let delegate = VoiceOverFileDelegate(recorder: self)
137	        voiceSession = VoiceSession(
138	            choice: choice, mayAsk: mayAsk, micSession: capture.session,
139	            micOutput: capture.output,
140	            fileDelegate: delegate, onFinish: onFinish,
141	            segments: [VoiceSegment(url: url, calledAt: calledAt)])
142	        state = .recording
143	        capture.output.startRecording(to: url, outputFileType: .m4a, recordingDelegate: delegate)
144	        completion(nil)
145	    }

147	    /// A refusal before anything was made: a prepared microphone is let go
148	    /// so the input does not stay open, `start`'s own rule.
149	    private func refuseVoiceOver(_ error: RecorderError, _ completion: (Error?) -> Void) {
150	        discardPreparedMicrophone()
151	        completion(error)
152	    }
153	
154	    // MARK: - Pause and resume
155	
156	    /// MAIN THREAD, synchronous; `pause()` forwards here. `.recording` →
157	    /// `.paused`; `.paused` throws `.alreadyPaused`, anything else
158	    /// `.notRecording`. Stamps the open segment's `stoppedAt`, counts the
159	    /// pause, asks the writer to stop (its did-finish lands on THAT segment),
160	    /// silences the meter and posts `pauseDidChangeNotification`.
161	    func pauseVoiceOver() throws {

212	    /// Seconds recorded: each segment from its did-start (else its call) to
213	    /// its `stoppedAt` (else now), each floored at 0, so it freezes while
214	    /// paused; 0 idle.

216	        guard state != .idle, let current = voiceSession else { return 0 }
217	        let now = Date()

219	            total

221	                    0,
222	                    (segment.stoppedAt ?? now).timeIntervalSince(
223	                        segment.startedAt ?? segment.calledAt))

263	    /// The next voice-over file: `RecordingFiles.uniqueURL`'s rule —
264	    /// `<stem>.m4a`, then `<stem> (2).m4a`, `(3)`… — over the files on DISK

266	    /// until its writer's did-start, so a pause and resume inside one second
267	    /// would otherwise mint one name twice.
268	    static func nextVoiceOverURL(in folder: URL, at date: Date, holding held: Set<String>) -> URL {

276	            counter += 1
277	        }
278	        return candidate

5	/// The segment, and the two transitions that close one and open the next
6	/// (road map 3, R2a). ScreenCaptureKit has no pause — `SCStream` and
7	/// `SCRecordingOutput` carry none — and the header's one lever is
8	/// `removeRecordingOutput` ("Stops Recording if the stream is currently
9	/// recording") beside `addRecordingOutput` ("Starts Recording if stream is
10	/// already capturing"). R0 q7 measured that pair on a running stream: the
11	/// remove returns in under 0.1 ms and the removed output's did-finish
12	/// lands 5–25 ms later; the add returns in 0.2 ms and the new output's
13	/// did-start 8–10 ms later (67–78 ms for the first, after `startCapture`);
14	/// the stream never stops and keeps delivering 56–58 fps while paused, so
15	/// a pause costs what a recording costs and the system's own indicator
16	/// stays up. So a paused recording is a SEQUENCE of file pairs over ONE
17	/// stream (decision 6): `pause()` removes the segment's output and stops
18	/// the microphone's writer, `resume()` mints a segment named by ITS OWN
19	/// start time, adds a fresh output and restarts the writer to a new file
20	/// on the one running capture session. Each pair's screen-minus-microphone
21	/// offset is measured per segment (q7: −22 to +33 ms across resumes on one
22	/// host), which is why a `Segment` carries its own stamps and
23	/// `RecordingSegment` its own offset.
24	///
25	/// **A resume never waits for the paused segment's did-finish** (q7's
26	/// `immediate` row: the next output added the moment the previous is
27	/// removed is as clean as one added after a pause). That is why the
28	/// delegates (`ScreenRecorder+Delegates.swift`) find a segment by the
29	/// output's IDENTITY and by the FILE URL the microphone delegate reports,
30	/// never "the current one": the closed segment's did-finish can land after
31	/// the next has begun, and one `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput` writes every
32	/// segment's file.
33	///
34	/// **What a failed pair costs** is R1's posture, per segment, softened for
35	/// the movie (#97): a movie that will not probe LEAVES ITS SEGMENT OUT
36	/// (`settle`, naming its kept files in `RecordingResult.unreadable`), as
37	/// does a CLOSED segment whose output reports a did-FAIL after its stop
38	/// (#181: its `outputFailure`, left out unprobed with the writer's
39	/// sentence); only a recording with no readable movie fails, and only the
40	/// OPEN segment's did-fail is the recording's; a microphone file that
41	/// will not probe is that segment's `micProblem`, and `resume()` asks the
42	/// writer to record the next segment regardless — each is judged on its
43	/// own file (q7: one poisoned writer failed every restarted file, and
44	/// another day's did not).
45	///
46	/// **Two limits the R2 review named, and what became of them.** A pause
47	/// inside the ~10 ms between a resume's add and its output's did-start
48	/// closes a file the writer may not have opened; that empty segment is now
49	/// left out and named rather than failing the recording (#97). And a
50	/// microphone `startRecording` followed by `stopRecording` before its first
51	/// sample answers −11805 with NO file (measured); that did-finish was ASKED
52	/// for, so it is that segment's `micProblem` alone and no longer the
53	/// session's `microphoneProblem` (#97) — every other segment's voice lands.
